## §Cross-cutting — Dedicated persistent workspace + per-user object store (Amendment #88, 2026-07-21)

> **Amendment #88 (2026-07-21): Dedicated persistent workspace + per-user object store.**
> Aura gains a fixed local working root **`/workspace`** (env `AURA_WORKSPACE_DIR`, backed by the `aura-workspace` volume) with a pre-baked document/data toolchain sized to the installed `docx`/`pptx`/`xlsx`/`pdf` skills — npm-global `docx`+`pptxgenjs` (`NODE_PATH` set); pip `python-docx`, `python-pptx`, `openpyxl`, `xlsxwriter`, `pandas`, `pypdf`, `pdfplumber`, `reportlab`, `pdf2image`, `pytesseract`, `Pillow`, `defusedxml`, `lxml`, `markitdown[pptx]`; OS `pandoc`, `file`, `xxd`, `poppler-utils` (`pdftoppm`/`pdftotext`), `qpdf`, `pdftk`, `tesseract-ocr`, `fonts-liberation` (Arial/Times-metric fonts for faithful Office render), and **LibreOffice headless modules** (`libreoffice-writer`/`-calc`/`-impress` — the shared `soffice` the docx/pptx/xlsx skills drive via `scripts/office/soffice.py` for render, formula-recalc, and Office↔PDF) — and a persistent `/workspace/.toolchain` for extra installs; `shell_exec`, the `fs_*` tools, and `send_file` default their working root to it (same path as the sandbox box `/workspace`, so it carries forward to the strict-profile sandbox unchanged). A short static `<workspace>` doctrine block is added to the system prompt — byte-stable turn-su-turn, so the §Cross-cutting KV-cache invariant (amendment #16/#29) holds (a one-time `messages[0]` content change, no golden hash pin). Durable per-user storage uses the already-built per-identity Garage bucket **`aura-<id>`** (`internal/objectstore/garageadmin` + `identity_store`, crypto-isolated + fail-closed), activated by provisioning a bucket + scoped key per identity; the `local` identity keeps the shared `aura-assets` bucket (D-11). The agent accesses its bucket through a **forked, hardened S3 MCP** (`aura-mcp-s3`, from `txn2/mcp-s3`, Apache-2.0), containerized (`docker/mcp-s3/`, per the containerize-MCP rule) and mounted per-identity via `~/.aura/mcp/<id>/servers.json` with the identity's scoped key + bucket, **hard-scoped to that single bucket** and binary/file-aware (`put_file`). `send_file` continues to deliver + ingest artifacts; web download via presigned URLs. Rationale: the docx conversation `019f83d0` showed ~30 turns of ephemeral-fs + reinstall friction (files in the ephemeral container root, `docx`/`pandoc`/`file`/`xxd` missing, no user root access). Out of scope: whole-workspace S3 sync, FUSE mount, the full LibreOffice suite/GUI (`libreoffice-base`/`-draw`/desktop UI), quota/sweep, full sandbox enablement (deferred to the native-Linux mini-PC). **[Revised 2026-07-22 — Amendment #88.1, operator-approved:** the originally-excluded LibreOffice is now pre-baked as **headless modules only** (`-writer`/`-calc`/`-impress`), because the installed `docx`/`pptx`/`xlsx` skills share `scripts/office/soffice.py` and cannot render/recalc/convert without `soffice`; the full GUI suite/`-base`/`-draw` stays out. Toolchain list above expanded accordingly (pptx/pdf/excel deps). Image size grows ~700 MB–1.1 GB (aura image ~3.26 GB total, measured) — accepted for zero-friction skill support.**] **[Revised 2026-07-22 — Amendment #88.2, operator-approved: the forked S3 MCP (`aura-mcp-s3`) is DEFERRED.** With the fixed `/workspace` (persistent volume — the agent re-reads past artifacts with `fs_read` across sessions), the pre-baked toolchain, `send_file` already ingesting deliverables into the identity's bucket, and `document_index` (Amendment #89) for searchability, the single-operator reality has no use case requiring the agent to directly CRUD its object store as an MCP tool. The per-identity bucket + scoped key is provisioned on demand by **`objectStoreProvisionAdapter.EnsureForIdentity(ctx, id) (Credentials, error)`** (shipped this phase — shared bucket for `local`/operator per D-11, own `aura-<id>` bucket minted for any non-local identity, fail-closed), which is the ready seam for the forked MCP when a real MUSR multi-user consumer materializes (direct per-identity object-store access where the shared `/workspace` no longer suffices). Deferring avoids an upstream-fork maintenance burden and a per-identity MCP process fan-out (a scale risk the design itself flagged) with no current benefit. Not dropped — deferred to MUSR; `EnsureForIdentity` keeps the door open.**] Design + evidence + plan: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-21-aura-dedicated-workspace-garage-design.md`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-21-aura-dedicated-workspace-garage.md`.

## §Cross-cutting — Document surface consolidation (Amendment #89, 2026-07-22)

> **Amendment #89 (2026-07-22): Document surface consolidation + explicit index bridge.** Aura gains a static `<documents>` system-prompt doctrine block distinguishing the two document worlds — the user's uploaded/indexed documents (searchable Neo4j knowledge base, via `document_search`, not on the filesystem) and the agent's own `/workspace` files (filesystem, via `fs_*`/skills) — and a new deferred agent tool **`document_index`** that indexes a `/workspace` file into the calling identity's knowledge base on demand (reusing `documents.Service.IngestPath`, per-identity ownership, path-confined to `AURA_WORKSPACE_DIR`). `document_search` and `send_file` descriptions are aligned to name the boundary. Delivered/created files remain non-searchable until explicitly indexed (D-03 "no silent searchable memory" preserved). Out of scope: store unification, auto-indexing, changes to the automatic upload→ingest path. Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-document-search-consolidation-design.md`. (Next free amendment number confirmed at plan time.)

## §Cross-cutting — AG-UI SSE run resilience: run-detach + Last-Event-ID resume (Amendment #90, 2026-07-23)

> **Amendment #90 (2026-07-23): AG-UI cockpit run lifetime decoupled from the HTTP fetch + SSE resume contract (fix-plan 1.3 Tier B).** Ratifies, verbatim, the design `docs/audit/sse-resume-design-1.3b-2026-07-23.md` (Tier A heartbeat `a93648c5` already shipped). Ten points:
>
> 1. **Run lifetime is decoupled from the HTTP fetch** when `AURA_AGUI_RUN_DETACH=true`: client disconnect no longer cancels an in-flight `/agent/run` turn; a run is bounded by the agent Budget, `AURA_AGUI_RUN_MAX_WALLCLOCK_SEC`, explicit cancel, the conversation delete-lifecycle, and daemon shutdown.
> 2. **SSE frames on `/agent/run` (and the resume route) carry `id: <seq>`** — a per-run, 1-based, strictly monotonic sequence; heartbeat comments carry no id. Additive when the flag is on; wire byte-identical when off.
> 3. **New route `GET /agent/runs/{runID}/events`** — authenticated, owner-scoped (foreign or unknown ⇒ 404), read-only SSE resume honoring `Last-Event-ID` (replay from n+1; absent ⇒ full-buffer replay; replay gap ⇒ 410 Gone; terminal run ⇒ tail + clean close). Explicitly NOT in the mutation inventory (zero write seams).
> 4. **New route `POST /agent/runs/{runID}/cancel`** — the explicit Stop, added to `httpMutationRoutes` (`agent_run_cancel`, Idempotency-Key required), owner-scoped 404, 202 semantics (async unwind; terminal-run cancel = 202 no-op). Supersedes disconnect-as-stop.
> 5. **Thread-lock lifetime = run lifetime** (release moves from handler-defer to turn-completion); 409 `ErrThreadBusy` now spans the run's true duration. HITL pause still releases the lock (a paused run holds nothing; resume = new `POST /agent/run` with `Resume[]`, unchanged).
> 6. **Conversation DTO gains optional `live_run_id`** (in-memory registry lookup, absent when flag off / no live run) for reload-attach discovery.
> 7. **Redaction point moves to buffer-insert** on the detached path: resumed frames are byte-identical to originally-streamed frames; `showReasoning=true` stays cockpit-scoped (D-01 unchanged).
> 8. **Idempotency recipe for pre-byte POST retry:** reuse the key; 409-InProgress/422-Indeterminate ⇒ discover via `live_run_id` and attach read-only. `agent_run`'s terminal-indeterminate marking is unchanged.
> 9. **Env catalog additions** (all default-off/bounded): `AURA_AGUI_RUN_DETACH` (default **false**), `AURA_AGUI_RUN_BUFFER_EVENTS` (2048), `AURA_AGUI_RUN_LINGER_SEC` (180), `AURA_AGUI_RUN_MAX_WALLCLOCK_SEC` (3600), `AURA_AGUI_RUN_MAX_LIVE` (16).
> 10. **Non-goals ratified:** single-process only (no multi-replica fan-in), no durable frame log (daemon restart ⇒ `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` fallback), Telegram/Fanout/`client.go` paths byte-untouched, branch/edit `streamPost` routes deferred (design is additive), default-flip to `true` only after live cockpit E2E >9.8 in a separate amendment line.
>
> **▶ Amendment #90.1 (2026-07-23): default flip ratified.** The live E2E campaign on the deployed container passed at **10/10** — control run with monotonic `id:` 1..N and persisted==streamed; kill-TCP mid-stream with the run surviving the disconnect and a gapless `Last-Event-ID` resume (stitched==persisted); reload-attach via `live_run_id` with full replay from seq 1 and post-terminal clearing; cancel → 202 → terminal `RUN_ERROR` → thread lock released (a new run on the same thread succeeds); every assertion on wire+DB ground truth, never model prose. The campaign also caught and fixed a real mount gap (the parent daemon mux lacked the `/agent/runs/` subtree — regression-tested). `AURA_AGUI_RUN_DETACH` therefore defaults **true** (config + compose); an explicit `=false` remains the operator rollback to the pre-detach wire. Point 9's "default false" and point 10's flip clause are superseded by this line.
>
> No migration (all state in-memory). Changed invariant called out for automation: closing the SSE connection no longer stops a run — `POST /agent/runs/{runID}/cancel` is the sanctioned replacement.

## §Cross-cutting — Reasoning persisted for display, structurally excluded from LLM context (Amendment #91, 2026-07-23)

> **Amendment #91 (2026-07-23, operator-directed): persist chain-of-thought for display rehydration; never send it back to the model.** Supersedes the *"never persisted to conversation_turns"* clause of amendment #57 (the *stream-only accumulation* half of #57 — reasoning never folds into `Content`/the answer builder — is untouched and still load-bearing). Today the cockpit ReasoningDrawer exists only for turns streamed in the live session: nothing is persisted, so every reload/thread-switch loses all CoT (`MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` cannot carry it). Ratified contract:
>
> 1. **Bounded persistence on the final assistant turn.** The runner accumulates the turn's reasoning deltas (the same `LLMResponse.Reasoning` stream the translator consumes) into a bounded buffer and persists it with `persistAssistantAnswer` onto a new nullable `aura.conversation_turns.reasoning text` column, alongside a nullable `reasoning_duration_ms bigint` (wall time from the first to the last reasoning delta of the turn — operator-ratified 2026-07-23, UI-spec OQ-1, so rehydrated history can label “Thought for X s” like live turns) (single migration at the next free slot — `ls internal/db/migrations/ | tail -1` at landing; indicatively `0050`). Cap knob `AURA_REASONING_PERSIST_MAX_RUNES` (default **65536**; `<=0` disables persistence entirely); over-cap keeps the head + a truncation marker. Only genuine CoT is persisted: when the show-reasoning path redacts deltas (`[reasoning redacted]`), NOTHING is stored — a hidden stream must not become a stored verbatim trace (HARDEN-05 posture preserved).
> 2. **LLM context stays structurally reasoning-free.** `llm.Message` gains NO reasoning field; `LoadHistory`/`LoadManagedHistory` and every context-rebuild path remain incapable of representing CoT. This structural exclusion is PINNED by a regression test (history rebuild from a reasoning-bearing turn produces a wire request with zero reasoning content in `messages`). Request-side reasoning *controls* (effort/exclude knobs) are unchanged.
> 3. **Display rehydration.** The `/threads/{id}/messages` snapshot projection gains optional `reasoning` + `reasoning_duration_ms` fields on assistant messages (display-only read path, separate from the `llm.Message` history read); the cockpit `snapshotToThreadMessages` maps it onto the existing `{type:'reasoning'}` part so the ReasoningDrawer survives reload/thread-switch. Telegram's live FIFO pane is unchanged.
> 4. **Non-goals:** no backfill of past turns (column NULL = drawer absent, correct degrade), no reasoning in exports/shares beyond what the snapshot already governs (share paths keep their existing redaction posture: shared-link projections MUST NOT include the new field), no Neo4j `:ReasoningTrace` (that future option stays gated off), no per-round mid-turn persistence (final accumulated CoT only, interleaved spans joined in arrival order).

## §Scheduler — pending-approval relay-liveness: recurring reminder sweep (Amendment #92, 2026-07-23)

> **Amendment #92 (2026-07-23, fix-plan 1.7 / BUG-1B): a gated scheduled task can no longer be silently forgotten.** A task forced to `status='pending_approval'` (every `agent_job` per AG-016, or any risky-scored task — `task.go:216-220`) rides the origin-channel `ask_user` pause for its approval: an authenticated, fail-closed resume, NOT the Notifier. The residual liveness gap: if the model never relays the approval directive (or the operator misses the single prompt), the task sits in `pending_approval` forever with no further signal. This adds a throttled recurring re-surface so a pending approval keeps nudging its owner until acted upon.
>
> **REVISED 2026-07-23 (same-day, design doc `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-scheduled-task-approval-on-channel-design.md`).** The original delivery contract (points 3–4 below) re-surfaced a **plain-text nudge pointing at the cockpit** via the text-only `ChannelDeliverer.DeliverToIdentity` seam. This is superseded: the reminder MUST arrive as a **real `ask_user` HITL prompt on the channel the task was scheduled from** — Telegram inline Sì/No, WebUI in-thread approval — and MUST NOT be routed to the cockpit governance scheduler board. The throttle/sweep skeleton (point 1, the `approval_reminded_at` column, point 5) is kept; points 2–4 and 6 are re-ratified below. Ratified (revised) contract:
>
> 1. **Per-tick reminder sweep, mirroring `sweepNotifications`.** `*cron.Dispatch` gains `sweepApprovalReminders(ctx)`, invoked from `Scheduler.tick` immediately after `sweepNotifications` via a second type-asserted local interface (`approvalReminderSweeper` — the existing `notificationSweeper` idiom, `scheduler.go:258-262`). No new goroutine; it runs on the existing scheduler tick. *(Unchanged.)*
> 2. **Throttle via the nullable column added by migration `0051`** (`aura.scheduler_tasks.approval_reminded_at timestamptz`, nullable). **REVISED selection predicate:** `ListDuePendingApprovalReminders` selects `status='pending_approval' AND origin_conversation_id IS NOT NULL AND origin_conversation_id <> '' AND (approval_reminded_at IS NULL OR approval_reminded_at <= now() - $interval) ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` (bounded `$limit`). The old `identity_id NOT IN ('', 'local')` filter is DROPPED — WebUI/`local`-origin tasks must be selected so their pause gets **minted** (they surface via the pull `/api/approvals`, not a push). Rows with an empty `origin_conversation_id` (CLI-origin, no conversation to key a pause on) are excluded and keep the `aura task approve` CLI path. `MarkApprovalReminded($id)` stamps `approval_reminded_at = now()`. Leaving `pending_approval` (approve → active, or reject → cancelled) ends the reminders by construction.
> 3. **REVISED — ensure a real `ask_user` pause, then re-surface on the origin channel.** Per due row the sweep (a) **ensures a `scheduled_task_approval` pause exists** on the task's `origin_conversation_id` via a new consumer-side `ApprovalPauseEnsurer` seam (satisfied by a `cmd/aura` adapter over `askuser.Store`): a pending pause matching `resume_context.type='scheduled_task_approval'` + `resume_context.task_id=<id>` is reused (idempotent), else **minted** host-side via `askuser.Store.Insert` — operator-origin, no model, `identity_id` auto-stamped by the BEFORE-INSERT trigger (36-04). This reuses the sanctioned second-writer widening (T-04-19 / Phase-29 D-13). Then (b) **pushes** the token-bound approval prompt to the origin channel via a new optional `ApprovalDeliverer` channel capability (`DeliverApproval(ctx, identityID, token, taskID, kind)`) fanned out by `channels.Registry` exactly like `DeliverToIdentity`. Telegram renders inline Sì/No under a new `aura_sched_approval` callback (`callback_data="<token>|<action>"`); WebUI needs no push (the pull `/api/approvals` surfaces the pause in-thread). cron gains NEITHER a `channels` NOR an `askuser`/`tools` import — both seams are consumer-side interfaces (import-cycle constraint preserved).
> 4. **REVISED — resolution is a real pause resolution, not a text acknowledgement.** The operator resolves the **real pause**: Telegram button → `runner.SubmitAnswer(token, {Action})`; WebUI → `POST /api/approvals/{token}/resolve`. Both drive the existing `newScheduledTaskResumeHook`: **accept** → `ApproveScheduledTaskInConversation` → `active`; **reject/cancel** → the hook's NEW cancel branch → `CancelScheduledTaskInConversation` → `cancelled` (owner-scoped by `origin_conversation_id`, so a declined task stops re-nudging). Every selected row is stamped `approval_reminded_at = now()` after the attempt REGARDLESS of outcome, so a pending approval re-nudges at most once per interval and a permanently-failing channel cannot spam the tick. The pushed prompt is bounded — task **kind + short id** only — and MUST NOT dump the payload.
> 5. **Cadence knob + kill switch.** `AURA_SCHEDULER_APPROVAL_REMINDER_SEC` (default **3600**; `<=0` disables the sweep entirely — no query issued, no ticker cost). Bounded batch limit mirrors `pendingNotificationSweepLimit`. Fail-soft: a sweep error is logged and swallowed per tick (the 0.2 swallow-per-tick posture), never terminates the scheduler. *(Unchanged.)*
> 6. **REVISED non-goals:** no new notification route; the approval/resume *primitive* is untouched (the `ask_user` fail-closed pause is reused verbatim — this amendment only adds a host-side, operator-origin *creator* + an origin-channel *re-surface*, both mirroring shipped precedents); no minting mid-model-turn (the model relay stays the t=0 fast path; the headless sweep is the deterministic guarantor within one cadence); no reminder for CLI-origin tasks (no conversation to attach a pause to); no escalation/auto-expiry of un-approved tasks (a separate future policy). The cockpit governance scheduler board is explicitly NOT the reminder surface. Env-catalog row updated for the knob.

## §Cross-cutting — Adaptive intelligence shadow control plane (Amendment #93, 2026-07-24)

> **Amendment #93 (2026-07-24, operator-directed): provider-neutral adaptive learning across reasoning and non-reasoning strategy choices, shadow-only until real-model proof.** This amendment ratifies `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-aura-adaptive-intelligence-design.md` and the executable evidence in spikes 097–105. It extends adaptation beyond reasoning to tool discovery, skill routing, knowledge retrieval, memory recall/write, model/provider routing, context management, document search, multimodal routing, and retry/recovery. The learned layer may choose only among already-authorized safe strategies; it never grants a capability, bypasses ToolGateway, or explores destructive actions. `AURA_LLM_ADAPTIVE_REASONING` remains the static reasoning champion/fallback; it is not itself an online learner.
>
> **Evidence boundary (blocking).** Qwen3.5 2B Q4_K_M under llama.cpp is a spike instrument only, not Aura's real configured model and not a production candidate. It validates portability, action-dependent measurement, and OPE plumbing only. The frozen graph-kNN challenger produced `+0.1679` held-out utility on that spike, but the family-bootstrap 95% interval `[-0.0168,+0.3198]` failed the preregistered unseen-family gate. No Qwen result may authorize production serving. The seeded canary artifact identifies `subject_model_id=synthetic-model-not-production` and verdict `VALIDATED_GATE_NOT_MODEL`.
>
> **Authoritative data contract.** PostgreSQL is the source of truth; Neo4j is a replayable private analytical projection. New Postgres migrations occupy the verified next free slots `0052`–`0058`: typed owner-scoped adaptive outbox, permanent identity tombstones, distributed policy state, append-only promotion evidence/audit, UUID-only tombstone privilege hardening, immutable-event/runtime DML hardening, and capability-bound policy mutation hardening. Cypher migration `0003_adaptive_intelligence` adds private `AdaptiveEpisode`/`AdaptiveEvent` projection labels attached to agent-memory's existing `User` anchor. Raw fact columns are immutable after insert; only lease/status delivery columns may update. Aggregate sequence allocation, tombstone fencing, and policy transition use narrow `SECURITY DEFINER` functions after direct runtime table mutation is revoked. Identity deletion is the sole sanctioned raw-event removal path through FK cascade. Policy audit `actor_id` is an immutable UUID snapshot without an identity FK so deprovisioning cannot erase evidence or become blocked; permanent tombstones retain only UUID + deletion time, never name/email.
>
> **Atomicity and identity safety.** A terminal tool/final-answer turn, cache metric, and adaptive fact commit in one owner-scoped PostgreSQL transaction. Exact retries create neither a second fact nor a second turn; immutable conflicts roll back the companion write. Oversized turns use the existing sidecar spill path, with post-spill transaction failure removing the staged file and the boot orphan scan covering process-crash residue. A permanent fence is raised before graph purge. Event insertion checks the fence before and after its advisory lock and again in the insert statement; the projector checks before and after graph write and purges a late projection. Recreating a deleted identity UUID cannot append evidence.
>
> **Policy and rollout boundary.** `PolicyService` is the only Go mutation API; the legacy direct CAS API is removed. Each transition requires `adaptive.manage` (or wildcard), a legal state edge, epoch freshness, an immutable audit row, and—only for `canary`/`active`—an eligible calibrated closed-cohort report bound to the configured production model ID. Runtime table UPDATE/INSERT/DELETE bypasses are revoked. The production composition root currently wires observation and atomic adaptive persistence only when authoritative state is `shadow`; served behavior stays static. `off`, `rollback`, or policy-read failure uses the pre-adaptive baseline. `canary`/`active` learned-action serving is intentionally absent: finding either state at boot forces the static baseline.
>
> **Promotion statistics.** Production assignments must carry one point-specific decision UUID, true non-zero propensity, real model/policy/cohort identity, closed-cohort membership, and independent deterministic/human/calibrated-judge provenance. Self-report, operational success, spike/offline evidence, duplicate assignments, unsupported deterministic logs, excessive censoring, and differential censoring are ineligible. OPE requires overlap diagnostics, ESS, SNIPS and doubly robust estimates; it may qualify a canary but never activate directly. Five planned looks share total alpha `0.05`; promotion requires quality-uplift lower bound above the declared threshold and harm-increase upper bound within the declared margin.
>
> **Agent-memory reuse boundary.** Aura reuses the deployed Neo4j/agent-memory infrastructure but never writes adaptive payloads through LLM-facing memory tools. The internal projector alone owns private adaptive labels. Live proof must use the pinned containerized `mcp-neo4j-cypher` wrapper and the real agent-memory MCP, assert adaptive marker non-recall, and purge only adaptive nodes while retaining the shared user. Neo4j Community is acceptable only while untrusted/LLM callers have no general Cypher endpoint; otherwise Enterprise property privileges or an isolated database/service boundary is mandatory.
>
> **Activation blockers and machine gates.** Production adaptation remains blocked until Aura's real `AURA_LLM_MODEL` runs all initially enabled domains, a durable cohort loader reconstructs evidence from the immutable assignment/delivery/outcome/correction ledger, evaluators pass held-out calibration, a preregistered power/look schedule is met on real randomized traffic, all quality/harm/censor bounds pass per domain and overall, learned-action serving is implemented and fault-tested, the full unit/build/vet/race/live-Postgres/live-Neo4j/privacy/deletion/restart/rollback matrix is green, owned-surface coverage is ≥85%, mutation kill rate on critical adaptive files is ≥70%, and an operator explicitly approves the candidate. Until every condition holds, the production champion is static Aura behavior.

> **▶ Amendment #93.1 (2026-07-24, adversarial correction — implementation scope and legacy convergence).** Amendment #93 does not authorize calling the first hook/ledger slice a functional learning loop. The current generic hook can identify reasoning effort and invoked top-level tool only; it does not encode version/epoch/arm/support/propensity, distinguish multiplexed skill choices, represent knowledge/no-op assignments, or emit reasoning exactly once per multi-round turn. Typed per-domain assignment adapters, a durable cohort loader, challenger/snapshot builder, disagreement scorer, and the production projector lifecycle are therefore **not implemented** and remain activation blockers. Manual projector/MCP proof validates the component only, not a running outbox-drain service. Additionally, the pre-existing `AURA_LLM_REASONING_LEARNING` reasoning-example and tool-selection boost loops are legacy learned-serving paths outside the new policy gate and are enabled in the current deployment. That legacy composition is forbidden under the unified kill-switch invariant: it must be removed from production wiring (including its obsolete knob and unused dependency fields) before `off`/`rollback` may be described as system-wide baseline-only. Until that atomic removal lands and is live-verified, every “static champion” or “adaptive serving blocked” statement is scoped to the **new control plane only**.
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.2 (2026-07-24, operator-directed — complete legacy adaptive-learning decommission).** This amendment supersedes Amendment #71 in full and broadens Amendment #93.1 from production-wiring removal to irreversible removal of the entire pre-policy reasoning-example/tool-selection learning stack, including its stored legacy data. The new `internal/adaptive` shadow control plane and its private `AdaptiveEpisode`/`AdaptiveEvent` projection are explicitly outside this deletion boundary and remain governed by Amendment #93.
>
> **Code and serving boundary.** Delete packages `internal/activelearn`, `internal/reasoninglearn`, `internal/reasoningstore`, `internal/toolselectlearn`, `internal/toolselectstore`, and `internal/learningretention`, including their tests. Delete the runner learner files, hooks, dependency fields, construction, observation, refresh, and shutdown paths; delete `internal/agent/tools/search_learn*` and the learned rerank path while retaining static semantic-description ranking with its guarded BM25 tiebreak. Remove the reasoning classifier's dynamic `ExampleStore`, `Learner`, learned-example refresh/fold behavior, and the corresponding `LlmAgent` configuration/construction seams. The static curated-seed reasoning classifier remains the baseline and MUST have no way to fold learned examples or observe a legacy learner.
>
> **Operations, configuration, and explorer boundary.** Retire `AURA_LLM_REASONING_LEARNING`, `AURA_TOOLSELECT_ORACLE`, and every `AURA_LEARNING_*` knob from runtime config, validation, knob catalogs, container artifacts, compose/env examples, tests, and active documentation. Remove the `learning_compaction` scheduler kind, handler, dispatch registration, seed/provisioning helper, and cron tests. Remove the graph explorer's `ReasoningExample`/`ToolSelectionExample` isolated-node special cases ratified by Amendment #71; no legacy learning-evidence label remains a supported explorer contract.
>
> **Stored-data deletion and migration contract.** PostgreSQL migration `0059` deletes matching legacy `agent_job_runs`, the `learning_compaction` scheduler task, and stale settings rows for `AURA_LLM_REASONING_LEARNING` or `AURA_LEARNING_%`, then replaces `scheduler_tasks_kind_check` without the retired kind. Its down direction may restore kind admissibility only and MUST NOT fabricate deleted tasks, runs, or settings. Neo4j migration `0004` must `DETACH DELETE` only nodes carrying any of `ReasoningExample`, `ReasoningSeed`, `ToolSelectionExample`, or `ToolSelectionSeed`; verified unrelated labels, including `User` and the new adaptive labels, must survive. No legacy-label index or constraint removal is required because none exists. Live completion requires PostgreSQL head `59:false`, zero matching legacy scheduler tasks/runs/settings, zero nodes with the four legacy labels, and retained unrelated `User` plus adaptive graph data.
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.3 (2026-07-24, dark-code closure).** The shadow-only release MUST NOT ship a dormant Go policy-mutation API. The `PolicyService`/`PolicyUpdate` surface, its private transition validator/error classifier, service-only sentinels, and integration tests whose sole consumer is that unreachable service are deleted. The production composition root retains only the live `PolicyStore` read path and fail-safe `PolicyController` gate used by shadow observation. PostgreSQL policy state, privilege hardening, transition/evidence schema, and the narrow `SECURITY DEFINER` transition function remain migration-compatible data/operations contracts, but Aura exposes no Go caller that can mutate policy state in this release. The raw-DML denial integration test remains. Any future CLI/API/operator mutation composition requires a new PRD amendment, an authorized production caller, and live capability/audit evidence in the same slice; test-only reachability is not sufficient.
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.4 (2026-07-24, implementation contract — typed adaptive learning and evidence reconstruction).** This amendment supersedes every #93-series claim that the generic `schema_version=1.0` hook payload, request-level reasoning ID, caller-constructed `CanaryBatch`, test-only projector, or removed `PolicyService` constitutes a completed adaptive-learning loop. Schema `1.0` rows remain immutable historical observations but are ineligible for training, OPE, promotion, or learned serving. The first production-eligible contract is schema `2.0`, implemented and verified under the following requirements.
>
> **Assignment identity and typed ledger.** `decision_id` is the durable **assignment ID**. Exactly one schema-`2.0` assignment may exist for an owner and assignment ID; later delivery, outcome, and correction facts reference it but never replace it. Schema `2.0` retains `event_kind=decision` for that assignment, adds `event_kind=delivery`, and retains the existing outcome/correction kinds; additive database constraints enforce at most one assignment and one delivery per owner/assignment while preserving historical schema-`1.0` rows. Assignment IDs are derived from request ID + canonical decision point + point ordinal, so every model round and every other controllable point is distinct under retries. The assignment event ID is deterministically derived from schema + kind + assignment ID, so an exact retry is an idempotent replay and changed immutable content is a conflict. An assignment records: owner; domain and canonical point; ordinal; policy epoch/version/mode; immutable snapshot ID/hash; environment/cohort scope; provider/model identity; champion and candidate action catalog with eligibility/catalog hashes; optional experiment ID; randomized champion/challenger arm ID and true arm propensity; each intended action's marginal behavior probability; recommended and selected **intended** action; selection reason; explicit override marker; and bounded numeric/context features. It cannot claim actual delivery or fallback before execution. Experimental arms and intended actions are distinct: the canary intention-to-treat gate uses arm ID/propensity, and two arms selecting the same intended action remain in their originally assigned arms. Candidate actions are deterministically ordered and include an explicit no-op/static action. Raw prompts, queries, tool arguments, document contents, memory contents, credentials, chain-of-thought, and every content-derived fingerprint are forbidden in schema-`2.0` adaptive payloads. Typed safe projections contain only registered non-secret IDs, bounded limits, booleans, lengths, and hashes of non-secret immutable artifacts.
>
> **Delivery/exposure facts and behavior-policy truth.** In `shadow`, Aura always selects the static champion with marginal intended-action probability `1.0`; a challenger recommendation is diagnostic only and no randomized experiment arm is claimed. Shadow rows with zero challenger support are not OPE-eligible. `canary` evidence is eligible only when the experiment, arm catalog, supported action catalog, arm probabilities, and marginal intended-action probabilities were frozen before assignment; both probability vectors are finite and sum to one within tolerance; every evaluated intended action has declared positive support; and recommended/selected/delivered semantics are explicit. The arm draw, intended-action resolution, and durable assignment write form one pre-serve adapter operation: learned execution is forbidden until the assignment commit succeeds, and an assignment-write failure serves the static baseline.
>
> After executing the intended strategy, the adapter appends exactly one immutable **delivery/exposure fact** before exposing its result to the model or next downstream consumer. Its deterministic event ID derives from schema + delivery kind + assignment ID. It records the selected intended action, actual delivered action or `none`, the actual marginal exposure probability when it is defined (otherwise an explicit unknown marker), success/fallback status and bounded reason, effective bounded parameters, result count, and—only where the serving system already has them—ordered registered non-secret artifact/node/tool/skill IDs plus immutable retriever/index/corpus revision. It never records raw or fingerprinted query/result content. Exact retry reuses the same fact; different immutable content conflicts. If learned-strategy execution or delivery-fact persistence fails, the learned result is discarded and the static adapter path serves outside eligible learned exposure. An assignment with missing delivery remains in its randomized arm and becomes missing/censored/poison evidence under the preregistered rule; it is never dropped. Missing, invalid, stale, owner-mismatched, model-mismatched, provider-mismatched, unsupported, or checksum-mismatched state selects static and records the selection reason in the assignment; post-execution fallback belongs only in delivery. Explicit user/operator choices are exogenous overrides, not randomized arms. Risky or destructive actions have zero exploration probability.
>
> **Outcome and correction facts.** An eligible outcome references the assignment ID and domain and records observed/censored status; evaluator kind, ID, version, rubric, calibration ID, and provenance hash; bounded quality, harm, latency, token, and cost measures; and observation time. Tool completion, HTTP success, persistence success, delivery success, or model self-report alone is operational telemetry, not eligible answer-quality evidence. Outcome event IDs are deterministically derived from assignment ID + evaluator key + stable source-observation ID; one terminal fact is allowed per assignment/evaluator/source key and exact retries replay. Delayed results append under a new stable source-observation ID. A correction ID is derived from its stable correction-source ID and names the fact it supersedes. Corrections must be same-owner, same-assignment, same-domain, same-evaluator-key links to the current effective fact; missing targets, cross-kind/scope links, cycles, and forks are rejected. The deterministic fold follows the single correction chain to its terminal leaf. Immutable assignment/delivery/outcome rows are never rewritten. Eligibility rejects missing or mismatched provenance, uncalibrated judge results, duplicate terminal observations, ambiguous correction history, excessive censoring, and differential censoring outside the preregistered bound.
>
> **Immutable snapshots and serving.** PostgreSQL is authoritative for immutable snapshot metadata, artifact bytes/reference, feature/action schemas, owner scope, provider/model binding, training cutoff, and content hash. A verified snapshot is loaded into a bounded local in-memory serving object; adaptive scoring, snapshot loading, and private projection never query Neo4j on the request hot path. The explicitly authorized memory-recall action remains an exception because it reuses the existing owner-scoped Neo4j-backed `memory_get_context` serving path; its returned content is still fenced as untrusted reference data. The initial frozen challenger is the already-spiked graph-kNN rule: per action, at most 256 eligible historical outcomes frozen at the training cutoff, top five non-negative cosine neighbors, mean eligible utility, and an explicit static prior when support is absent. There is no mutable recent overlay in the first implementation. Any refresh creates a new fully hashed snapshot and policy version; any different learner or hyperparameter requires a versioned snapshot contract and fresh evidence. A snapshot scoped to one owner cannot be pooled across owners or served to another owner.
>
> **Durable cohorts, statistical unit, and sealed evaluation.** Production promotion cannot accept an arbitrary caller-constructed observation batch. A preregistered cohort specification is durable and owner/domain/provider/model/policy/snapshot scoped; it freezes the snapshot and policy for the entire cohort and fixes candidate support, expected membership/cutoff, power assumptions, censoring limits, harm margin, one primary binary quality endpoint, one primary binary harm endpoint, five-look alpha schedule, evaluator calibration, experiment/arm catalog, and an exact focal-domain + canonical-point + ordinal inclusion predicate and predicate hash before the first included assignment. The initial outcome/statistical unit is exactly one request, and only one request may be randomized in an evaluation episode/conversation; later requests remain champion diagnostics so treatment cannot contaminate a later focal outcome through conversation history. At the first point satisfying that frozen predicate, the adapter atomically claims a unique `(cohort_id, request_id)` focal slot before drawing the arm; later matching points and every non-focal domain remain champion-only diagnostics. Every enrolled request must reconstruct to exactly one focal claim—zero is missing/censored under the preregistered rule and multiple claims poison the cohort. One terminal answer evaluation binds only to that focal assignment—Aura never copies one reward across assignments and does not jointly randomize domains.
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.5 (2026-07-25, focal claim/assignment transaction boundary).** A standalone committed `Claim` API is forbidden because callback failure could strand an enrolled request without its assignment. The typed `CohortStore` exposes one owner-scoped operation that receives the cohort/request/conversation/session/episode identity plus a trusted in-process assignment-builder callback. The evaluation conversation must already exist and belong to the claim owner; migration `0072` enforces this for direct database writers so a fabricated UUID cannot bypass the one-randomized-request-per-conversation rule, and migration `0073` makes `(owner_id, evaluation_conversation_id)` globally unique across cohorts so changing the cohort cannot produce a second arm draw. In one `WithIdentityTx` transaction it locks the adaptive owner first, loads and revalidates the immutable cohort, verifies the exact focal predicate and required admission block identities, and attempts the unique claim insert. Only the winning fresh insert invokes the callback; the callback performs the local arm draw and returns the complete schema-`2.0` Assignment. `CohortStore` then revalidates that Assignment against the persisted cohort and claim—owner, request, deterministic assignment ID, domain/point/ordinal, experiment and arm support/propensity, action catalog/support, provider/model, policy epoch/version, snapshot ID/hash, and production-canary environment—and records it through the existing owner-locked ledger primitive before committing. The initial cohort contract freezes `static` as its champion, so the focal Assignment's `champion_action_id` must be exactly `static`; a future non-static champion requires a versioned cohort artifact field rather than inference. For this focal contract, `eligibility_sha256` is the lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of the exact ordered `eligible_actions` string array, and `catalog_sha256` is the lowercase SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of the exact ordered `action_probabilities` array; both must match the ordered actions frozen in the cohort. Callback, validation, or assignment-write failure rolls back both claim and assignment. A uniqueness loser never invokes the callback and must serve the static champion. An exact retry returns the already-persisted claim plus its validated Assignment without drawing again; any changed immutable claim field, absent/invalid Assignment, or pre-existing Assignment without the claim is a conflict/fail-closed condition. No database or network work is permitted inside the callback. Lock order is always owner → cohort/claim → assignment event → aggregate sequence, and no adapter may execute or expose the learned path until this transaction commits.
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.6 (2026-07-25, ledger reconstruction and record-time cutoff).** Adaptive evidence is bitemporal: payload/`created_at` describes when the evaluator says a fact became effective, while the database must independently record when Aura learned it. Migration `0074` therefore adds immutable `adaptive_outbox.recorded_at`, overwritten on every insert by an invoker-safe `BEFORE INSERT` trigger using PostgreSQL `statement_timestamp()`; callers cannot backdate it. Historical rows remain `NULL` rather than receiving a fabricated backfill time, and any cohort-bound fact without trusted server record time is poison. The owner-locked loader obtains database `statement_timestamp()` inside its transaction. If that timestamp is earlier than `cohort.cutoff`, it returns a distinct `open` result with no reconstructed-ledger hash and no sealable closed view. At or after cutoff, its as-of-cutoff ledger contains only facts with trusted `recorded_at < cutoff`; outcome/correction facts additionally require canonical `observed_at < cutoff`. All bijection, duplicate/root, payload, identity, scope, and correction-chain poison validation applies to that closed pre-cutoff view. Later facts remain immutable audit history but contribute only unhashed late diagnostics/count and cannot change eligibility, the closed hash, or retroactively rescue/poison it. A cohort-bound fact with `recorded_at IS NULL` is always poison because its record-time side cannot be placed safely on either side of the cutoff. A claim whose one valid Assignment is not in the closed view poisons the cohort; missing Delivery or primary outcome remains a censored ITT member. This separates record time from effective time following the append-only bitemporal/event-history pattern and uses PostgreSQL's command-receipt timestamp rather than a client clock.
>
> The first loader is a pure owner-scoped reconstruction service, not yet the evidence-artifact writer. In one owner-locked transaction it reads the verified cohort, all claims, and every raw decision/delivery/outcome/correction row without SQL validity filters; invalid rows are surfaced as poison, never silently omitted. It requires a bijection between the cohort's claims and cohort-bound Assignments: every claim has exactly one valid Assignment with the same owner/request/assignment/predicate/scope, and every Assignment that names the cohort has exactly one matching claim. An orphan or mismatched cohort-bound Assignment poisons the cohort together with any linked Delivery, outcome, or correction rows. Each matched Assignment permits at most one Delivery. ITT always uses frozen `arm_id`/`arm_probability`; Delivery contributes only a strict statistical exposure projection (intended/actual action, success/fallback, known positive marginal exposure, and fallback reason). Result IDs and revision maps remain byte-bound through the immutable payload/hash and database schema validator but are not interpreted by promotion statistics, so the loader does not invent missing runtime `ResultCatalog`/`RevisionCatalog` state. Missing/fallback/unknown delivered exposure remains in ITT and is ineligible for delivered-exposure OPE. #93.7 narrows that statement: selected-intention OPE remains eligible when the frozen intended action, exact marginal intention `mu`, target support, endpoint model, and selected-intention outcome contract are valid, regardless of delivery-exposure eligibility.
>
> For each exact frozen primary evaluator provenance, the loader requires exactly one stable source-observation root and validates its correction chain; an additional primary root is a duplicate terminal observation and poisons the cohort rather than letting arrival order choose the result. Delayed independent observations may use other preregistered evaluator identities, but they cannot replace or aggregate into the primary endpoint. A fork, cycle, missing parent, cross-scope link, invalid payload/hash/identity, duplicate Assignment/Delivery, unsupported cohort binding, or malformed primary endpoint poisons the cohort. A missing or explicitly censored quality/harm endpoint censors the member. `ExpectedMembers` is a preregistered traffic/power ceiling, not a nonexistent member roster: claim count above it is poison, while claim count below `MinimumMembers` yields a valid deterministic reconstruction that is ineligible to seal as a closed outcome artifact. This rule supersedes the older shorthand requirement to reject “missing expected members”; only exceeding `ExpectedMembers` poisons reconstruction, while failing `MinimumMembers` prevents sealing. The reconstructed-ledger SHA-256 covers only canonical ordered members and their included pre-cutoff event IDs, hashes, and trusted record times. Late-fact count and censor diagnostics are emitted outside that hashed closed view, so later inserts cannot change its identity; migration-backed sealed admission/outcome artifacts and transactional policy revalidation remain the separate evidence-store step.
>
> Design basis: PostgreSQL defines `statement_timestamp()` as the receipt time of the current client command ([official date/time documentation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/functions-datetime.html)); the separate effective-time/record-time model follows append-only bitemporal event history ([Bitemporal History](https://martinfowler.com/articles/bitemporal-history.html)).
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.7 (2026-07-25, exact randomization, effect-bound inference, and OPE contract).** Task 2 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-24-aura-adaptive-intelligence-implementation.md` exposed an authorization gap: the current `CohortSpec` freezes marginal arm probabilities and block keys, but not the assignment mechanism/revision; #93.5's exported callback can choose an arbitrary arm; the session/episode cross-product produces singleton strata under the one-focal-request-per-conversation rule; and scalar `Snapshot.Utility` is not an endpoint-specific outcome model. Exact evidence and doubly robust OPE were not authorized before this amendment. #93.7 supersedes only conflicting #93.4/#93.5 and later summary shorthand about drawing, blocks, OPE, and artifact writers. It preserves #93.6's bitemporal truth: for look `L`, the immutable `cL` below is the cutoff used by the same trusted record-time/effective-time inclusion rule, and top-level `cohort.cutoff` equals `c5`.
>
> **Canonical encoding and schema registry.** Every v2 child and evidence artifact uses a strict typed Go `encoding/json` struct in the field order registered below. Encoders use the repository's canonical JSON escaping, no `omitempty`, no insignificant whitespace, and no trailing newline. Decoders reject unknown, missing, or duplicate fields and non-canonical encodings. Arrays are order-significant; maps are forbidden. UUIDs are lowercase hyphenated strings; SHA-256 values are lowercase 64-hex strings. Timestamps are UTC, truncated to microseconds, and encoded with `time.RFC3339Nano`. Artifact SHA-256 is over the exact UTF-8 canonical JSON bytes. The rational primitive is exactly `{"numerator":N,"denominator":D}` using unsigned integer JSON tokens, `D > 0`, GCD-reduced form, and `0/1` for zero. A draw byte is exactly two lowercase hexadecimal characters from `00` through `ff`.
>
