> **Literal arms, policies, and marginal action probability.** Cohort artifact v2 (`aura.adaptive.cohort/v2`) binds one canonical immutable `RandomizationPlan`. Its ordered arm 0 is `arm_id="baseline"`, `arm_role="control"`, weight `1`, `policy_id="aura/static-champion"`, policy revision `1`, and deterministic intended action `"static"`. Ordered arm 1 is `arm_id="challenger"`, `arm_role="treatment"`, weight `1`, `policy_id="aura/graph-knn-snapshot"`, policy revision `1`, and deterministic intended action `aC(x)` from the immutable verified graph-kNN snapshot. Both arm references bind the cohort snapshot and common action-schema hash. Their `feature_schema_sha256` MUST equal the verified snapshot's actual nonempty feature-schema hash; the graph-kNN arm consumes it and the baseline arm binds but does not consult it. The registered canonical empty feature-schema hash is reserved solely for the context-free endpoint action-mean outcome models and MUST NOT appear in either serving-arm reference. The common denominator is `2`; `design_id="independent-bernoulli"`; mechanism ID is `aura/go-crypto-rand-bit`, mechanism revision `1`; entropy-source ID is `go-crypto-rand/os-csprng`; draw-byte count is `1`; and bit index is `0`, the least-significant bit. There is no seed or caller arm selection.
>
> Before entropy, caller/store code fully validates both complete alternatives, computes and validates supported `aC(x)`, and fixes `champion_action_id="static"` plus `recommended_action_id=aC(x)`. No callback sees entropy or performs fallible/arm-dependent work after the draw. Only after the owner-locked transaction revalidates the cohort and wins the fresh globally unique focal claim may store-owned code read one OS-CSPRNG byte: bit `0` selects baseline, bit `1` selects challenger. It atomically persists the Assignment and canonical immutable `RandomizationReceipt`. Vectors are `00→baseline`, `01→challenger`, `fe→baseline`, `ff→challenger`. The receipt proves mapping/replay, not honest entropy freshness; Go `crypto/rand` and the OS CSPRNG remain the explicit trusted boundary.
>
> Every Assignment persists `P(baseline)=P(challenger)=1/2`, retains arm propensity `1/2`, and sets `intended_action_id` to the selected arm's deterministic action. Its exact marginal selected-intention behavior policy is `mu(a|x)=1/2 I[a="static"] + 1/2 I[a=aC(x)]`; coincident actions aggregate, so `aC(x)="static"` gives `mu("static"|x)=1` while the randomized arm stays unchanged. There is no second action draw. Cohort v2's action catalog is an ordered supported-action set. Per-row action probabilities include every catalog action and may be zero when neither arm selects it; the intended action and every target-positive action MUST have positive `mu`. This supersedes the validator shorthand that requires every catalog action to be positive on every row. The v1 OPE target is `pi(a|x)=I[a=aC(x)]`; selected intention is the only v1 estimand, and delivered-exposure OPE is deferred.
>
> An exact retry reloads and validates the persisted claim, Assignment, and receipt and never draws. A uniqueness loser never reads entropy. Entropy, template/callback, validation, rollback, persistence, or unresolved-commit failure serves static and cannot trigger an arm-dependent redraw. Commit-unknown recovery reloads durable state first; complete matching state returns exactly, partial/different state conflicts, and no fresh draw is allowed until absence is authoritative. Uncommitted arm identity cannot escape to retry-controlling code.
>
> **Analysis stratum and interference cluster.** The immutable statistical schema is `aura.adaptive.analysis-stratum/owner-claim-time-block/v1`, revision `1`. `block_origin` is `1970-01-01T00:00:00Z`; positive integer `block_width_seconds` is frozen before enrollment. The canonical schema descriptor is `{"schema_id":"aura.adaptive.analysis-stratum/owner-claim-time-block/v1","revision":1,"field_order":["schema_id","revision","owner_id","time_block_id"],"block_origin":"1970-01-01T00:00:00Z","block_width_seconds":W}` and `analysis_stratum_schema_sha256` is SHA-256 of those exact bytes for frozen width `W`. Store-owned code uses trusted pre-draw `claimed_at`, truncated to microseconds, to calculate `time_block_id=floor((claimed_at_us-origin_us)/(W*1000000))`. The stratum ID is SHA-256 of canonical `{"schema_id":"aura.adaptive.analysis-stratum/owner-claim-time-block/v1","revision":1,"owner_id":owner_id,"time_block_id":time_block_id}`. The plan, focal claim, receipt, closed member, quality/harm/OPE reports, and outcome evidence MUST bind the same schema hash and derived stratum ID or fail closed. `analysis_strata_sha256` is the hash of the canonical ordered distinct `analysis_stratum_id` array used by that look. Constant cohort owner is redundant but harmless. Session, episode, conversation, arm, outcome, delivery, and caller labels never enter the stratum.
>
> The separate immutable cluster schema is `aura.adaptive.interference-cluster/conversation/v1`, revision `1`, with ordered `cluster_keys=["owner_id","evaluation_conversation_id"]`. Its cluster ID is SHA-256 of canonical `{"schema_id":"aura.adaptive.interference-cluster/conversation/v1","revision":1,"owner_id":owner_id,"evaluation_conversation_id":evaluation_conversation_id}`. `InterferencePlan` freezes `carryover_scope="conversation"`, `randomized_focal_units_per_cluster=1`, `within_cluster_rule="arbitrary_carryover_one_focal"`, `between_cluster_assumption="no_treatment_induced_cross_conversation_interference"`, `shared_state_rule="read_only_or_versioned"`, `fold_unit="interference_cluster"`, and `resampling_unit="interference_cluster"`. Mutable shared memory/tool state, treatment-induced writes, or unversioned result-affecting state makes the cohort ineligible. Session and episode remain audit metadata only. Singleton/one-arm statistical strata are retained without dropping, merging, or reblocking and receive the exact vacuous bounds below.
>
> Golden stratum bytes `{"schema_id":"aura.adaptive.analysis-stratum/owner-claim-time-block/v1","revision":1,"owner_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","time_block_id":1}` hash to `620c5a36c88df7ce65c041d67d01754e3224b6e072624a2d6d8afa34b16bc942`. Golden cluster bytes `{"schema_id":"aura.adaptive.interference-cluster/conversation/v1","revision":1,"owner_id":"11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111","evaluation_conversation_id":"22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222"}` hash to `286a699a89345a049f7458ae5fa3986db1a17bac59ce407581e6f120cd41895e`.
>
> **Canonical order and binary64 accumulation.** Every comparison is ascending raw UTF-8 bytes, with no locale, normalization, or case folding. Strata sort by `analysis_stratum_id`; clusters by `interference_cluster_id`; closed members by `(analysis_stratum_id,interference_cluster_id,claim_id,request_id,assignment_id)`; included event refs by `(recorded_at,event_kind,event_id,event_sha256)`; actions and prediction rows by `action_id`; endpoints and their reports by endpoint-kind rank `quality` then `harm`, then `endpoint_id`, evaluator `(kind,id,version,rubric_id,calibration_id,provenance_sha256)`, and `report_id`; reasons and reason-count rows by `reason`. Bootstrap members retain that member order inside each cluster; selected cluster copies follow draw order. A duplicate complete sort key is rejected, never resolved by arrival or input order. Replicates sort by finite numeric value, then zero-based replicate index; `-0` is normalized to `+0`.
>
> `neumaier-binary64-no-fma-v1` starts `sum=+0` and `correction=+0`. For each finite input `x` in canonical order, compute binary64 `t=sum+x`; if `abs(sum)>=abs(x)`, set `correction=correction+((sum-t)+x)`, otherwise set `correction=correction+((x-t)+sum)`; then set `sum=t`. Return binary64 `sum+correction`, normalizing `-0` to `+0`. Every stated operation rounds separately to IEEE-754 binary64 round-to-nearest, ties-to-even; FMA, reassociation, extended precision, and parallel reduction are forbidden. Reject any nonfinite input, intermediate, correction, or result. DR forms each action term in action order and each member term in member order; SNIPS and ESS use the same accumulator for their numerator, weight sum, and squared-weight sum. Final division is one binary64 division after accumulation. `rounding_revision` is `neumaier-binary64-no-fma-outward-8dp-v1`.
>
> **Five UTC-cutoff looks.** `mode="utc_cutoff"` is the only v2 schedule and `look_count=5`. Before enrollment, `LookPlan` stores `c1 < c2 < c3 < c4 < c5`, and top-level `cohort.cutoff` MUST equal `c5`. Look alphas are exactly `[1/200,1/200,1/100,1/100,1/50]`; cumulative alphas are `[1/200,1/100,1/50,3/100,1/20]`. Look 1 has `predecessor_rule="none"`; looks 2–5 have `predecessor_rule="immediate_continue"`. For look `L`, the owner-locked transaction obtains PostgreSQL `statement_timestamp()`. `now < cL` returns `open` without a hash or write; equality closes. The closed view contains claims with `claimed_at < cL`, facts with trusted `recorded_at < cL`, and outcomes/corrections only when canonical `observed_at < cL`. Equality belongs to the later side. Any cohort-bound fact with `recorded_at IS NULL` poisons the look regardless of apparent lateness. Facts excluded by either cutoff are immutable late diagnostics outside the closed-ledger hash; claims at/after `cL` are future members. A pre-cutoff claim whose Assignment is absent from the closed fact view poisons that look. These are #93.6's rules applied at immutable `cL`, not a new client clock.
>
> Exactly one append-only artifact may exist for `(owner_id,cohort_id,look_number)`. Look 1 has null predecessor. Looks 2–5 bind the immediately preceding `canary_outcome` ID/hash, and that artifact's disposition MUST be `continue`. Allowed dispositions are `continue`, `promote`, `retain_canary`, and `ineligible`; only `continue` permits another look, and look 5 cannot emit `continue`. Reuse, replacement, skipped linkage, or post-cutoff fact incorporation conflicts. `ExpectedMembers` remains the ceiling whose excess poisons reconstruction; `MinimumMembers` remains the sealing floor. Admission simulation uses production-shaped repeated owner/time blocks and conversation clusters; insufficient support/power or degenerate realized support is ineligible and never authorizes reblocking. Cohort v1 remains readable history but cannot randomize, seal a look, run OPE, or authorize a transition.
>
> **Exact conservative binary ATE bounds.** Independent `1/2` Bernoulli draws, conditioned on realized treated counts in each frozen stratum, induce the product uniform complete-randomization distribution. The production algorithm is `stratified-bonferroni-hypergeom-ate-v1`, revision `1`, arithmetic revision `exact-bigint-rational-v1`. It implements the first conservative finite-population construction of Li, Spertus, and Stark, not their floating research code, a generic Bernoulli p-value, Fisher/ESI combination, FFT approximation, or sharp-null diagnostic.
>
> For stratum population `N`, sample size `m`, observed successes `x`, and exact rational tail budget `β`, define `H+(g;N,m,x)=Σ[j=x..min(m,g)] C(g,j)C(N-g,m-j)/C(N,m)`, `Lβ(N,m,x)=min{g∈[x,N-m+x]:H+(g;N,m,x)>β}`, and `Uβ(N,m,x)=N-Lβ(N,m,m-x)`. Equality is rejected: `H+<=β` lies outside the confidence set. For `K` realized strata and look alpha `α`, `β=α/(2K)`. In each stratum, infer `[L1k,U1k]` for total `Y(1)` from treated units and `[L0k,U0k]` for total `Y(0)` from controls, then compute exact rationals `ATE_lower=(Σk L1k-Σk U0k)/Σk Nk` and `ATE_upper=(Σk U1k-Σk L0k)/Σk Nk`. This gives the `α/2` treatment/control-total split and Bonferroni protection across strata. Margins are compared as exact rationals before formatting.
>
> A zero-size sample returns `[0,N]`; a census returns `[x,x]`. Thus singleton and one-arm strata remain with vacuous unidentified-side bounds. `K=0`, total `N=0`, cancellation, or cap breach is ineligible. Initial hard caps are 5,000 members, 5,000 strata, 5,000,000 evaluated hypergeometric terms, 16,384-bit integers, 64 MiB, and 10,000 ms. Lower decimals export to eight places rounded toward negative infinity; upper decimals round toward positive infinity. Exact vectors are: `N=10,m=5,x=4,β=1/42` has `H+(4)=1/42`, rejects equality, and therefore `Lβ=5`; `N=4,m=0,x=0` returns `[0,4]`; `N=4,m=4,x=3` returns `[3,3]`. Hand vectors and exhaustive enumeration are authoritative; research repositories may generate comparison fixtures but are neither vendored nor executable dependencies. An optional conditional hypergeometric sharp-null diagnostic has a separate ID/revision and never substitutes for ATE bounds.
>
> Quality passes only when the one-sided challenger-minus-baseline lower ATE bound is strictly greater than the exact frozen uplift. Harm passes only when its one-sided upper ATE bound is at or below the exact frozen increase margin. Both must pass as an intersection-union decision and may use the same look alpha. Missing outcomes remain ITT: quality lower imputes missing challenger `0` and baseline `1`; harm upper imputes missing challenger `1` and baseline `0`. Separate total- and differential-censor gates still apply.
>
> **Endpoint-specific action-mean OPE.** Scalar `Snapshot.Utility` is not `qhat`. Quality and harm each bind a distinct immutable `aura.adaptive.outcome-model/action-mean/v1` artifact with `algorithm_id="aura/endpoint-action-mean"`, revision `1`, the registered canonical empty feature-schema hash, endpoint/evaluator/reward provenance, target-policy hash, and training-ledger hash. Training uses only eligible endpoint-specific history with both trusted `recorded_at` and canonical `observed_at` strictly before its training cutoff, which is strictly before cohort creation. In supported-action order, every prediction row stores unsigned integer `support_count`/`success_count` and reduced-rational `qhat=successes/support` when support is positive, otherwise the preregistered reduced-rational no-support fallback. `clip_min=0/1`, `clip_max=1/1`; no context feature is accepted.
>
> `OPEPlan` freezes `estimand="selected_intention"`, the ordered supported actions, `target_policy_id="aura/deterministic-challenger"` revision `1`, `behavior_policy_id="aura/equal-bernoulli-arm-mixture"` revision `1`, exact policy hashes, `weight_clipping="none"`, exact positive minimum ESS, minimum overlap `1/2`, and both endpoint model refs. For row `i`, `w_i=pi(a_i|x_i)/mu(a_i|x_i)`. Canonical `dudik-langford-li-dr-v1` is `n^-1 Σi[Σa pi(a|x_i)qhat(a)+w_i(r_i-qhat(a_i))]`; `snips-v1` is `Σi w_i r_i/Σi w_i`; `importance-ess-v1` is `(Σi w_i)^2/Σi w_i^2`. Unknown/fallback delivery remains ITT and is counted, but cannot change selected-intention `a_i` or create delivered-exposure OPE. Missing support, target/model/reward leakage, hash mismatch, incomplete action predictions, overlap below `1/2`, insufficient ESS, or nonpositive SNIPS denominator makes endpoint OPE ineligible. OPE remains diagnostic and cannot replace admission or closed-canary outcome evidence.
>
> The `uncertainty` object has exact field order `algorithm_id,revision,confidence,replicates,unit,interval_target,seed_domain,rounding_revision`. Values are `algorithm_id="cluster-percentile-bootstrap-sha256-v1"`, revision `1`, confidence `19/20`, 10,000 replicates, `unit="interference_cluster"`, `interval_target="dr"`, `seed_domain="aura/ope-cluster-bootstrap-sha256-v1"`, and `rounding_revision="neumaier-binary64-no-fma-outward-8dp-v1"`. Each replicate draws `C` clusters with replacement, includes every row of each selected cluster, and recomputes DR. `C<2`, any nonfinite replicate, or a nonpositive original SNIPS denominator makes uncertainty unavailable and OPE ineligible; identical replicates validly return `[v,v]`. Seed bytes are `SHA256("aura/ope-cluster-bootstrap-sha256-v1\0" || canonical({cohort_id,look_number,endpoint_kind,closed_ledger_sha256,target_policy_sha256,outcome_model_sha256}))`. The sampler hashes `seed_raw || uint64be(counter)` from counter zero, consumes four big-endian `uint64` words per digest, sets `threshold=(2^64-C) mod C`, rejects words below threshold, and otherwise emits `word mod C`.
>
> Sort all 10,000 DR replicates; the outward percentile interval uses one-based order statistics 250 and 9751. Accumulate canonical cluster/member order with deterministic compensated `float64` summation. Export eight decimals, lower toward negative infinity and upper toward positive infinity. This interval is approximate and diagnostic, not finite-sample exact or anytime-valid. With a 32-byte zero seed and `C=3`, the first indices MUST be `0,0,0,2,2,1,1,0,2,1,0,2`. The two-row hand vector with challenger target, `mu=1/2`, `qhat(static)=2/5`, `qhat(challenger)=4/5`, and logged rewards `0,1` has weights `0,2`, DR `1`, SNIPS `1`, and ESS `1`.
>
> **Persisted evidence and sole outcome writer.** Cohort v2 and every registered child/ref/receipt/evidence artifact above are immutable, canonical, and content-addressed; the parent binds each child schema ID, revision, canonical hash, and policy/snapshot scope. Legacy v1 artifacts remain readable but ineligible and are never rewritten or backfilled. One forward PostgreSQL migration is permitted only when implementation lands and MUST take the then-current next free disk slot; this amendment assigns no migration number.
>
> Evidence kinds are literal `canary_admission` and `canary_outcome`. Admission binds frozen plans/snapshot/calibration/models/power/operator approval, contains no ledger/outcome fields, and may authorize only canary entry. `CohortStore.Reconstruct` remains pure and non-writing. `EvidenceStore.SealCanaryOutcome(ctx,ownerID,cohortID,lookNumber,sealer)` is the sole outcome writer and accepts no caller ledger, report, endpoint, hash, eligibility, or disposition.
>
> `SealCanaryOutcome` runs one `WithIdentityTx`: lock owner first and revalidate sealer capability; load cohort v2 and verify every child hash; obtain database `statement_timestamp()`; load and validate the unique predecessor; call internal `reconstructAtLookTx` in the same transaction at `cL`; compute censoring, exact ATE bounds, separate quality/harm OPE diagnostics, reports, eligibility, and disposition; canonicalize/hash `canary_outcome`; then insert the unique append-only look artifact. An exact retry returns the existing artifact only after full byte/hash/scope validation. Partial/different state conflicts; rollback writes nothing. The outcome binds the exact look/cutoff/alpha/predecessor, randomization plan, analysis-stratum schema/set hashes, closed ledger, distinct quality and harm report IDs/hashes, distinct quality-OPE and harm-OPE report IDs/hashes, censor-diagnostics ID/hash, owner/domain/provider/model/policy/snapshot/cohort scope, status, and sealer capability provenance. It may authorize only the separately authorized active transition.
>
> **Outcome disposition truth table.** Apply these rows in order; OPE is diagnostic and is excluded from every gate predicate.
>
> | Condition | Transaction result |
> |---|---|
> | `now<cL`; claim count below `MinimumMembers`; missing/invalid required predecessor; cancellation or transaction/commit failure; or inability to construct and hash every mandatory canonical quality, harm, quality-OPE, harm-OPE, and censor report envelope | Write no outcome artifact. |
> | Otherwise, any poison, censoring-limit breach, exact-inference failure/cap breach, canonical-schema/hash failure, or gate-support failure | Seal exactly one audit artifact with `disposition="ineligible"` and `eligible=false`; canonical reports record the failure. |
> | Gate-valid and exact `quality.ate_lower > minimum_quality_uplift` and exact `harm.ate_upper <= maximum_harm_increase` | Seal exactly one artifact with `disposition="promote"` and `eligible=true`. |
> | Gate-valid, either bound does not pass, and `look_number<5` | Seal exactly one artifact with `disposition="continue"` and `eligible=true`. |
> | Gate-valid, either bound does not pass, and `look_number=5` | Seal exactly one artifact with `disposition="retain_canary"` and `eligible=true`. |
>
> Diagnostic OPE availability, overlap, ESS, uncertainty, or model failure changes only the endpoint OPE report's `eligible`, reasons, and nullable diagnostics; it never changes outcome `eligible` or `disposition`. Look 5 cannot continue. Only an artifact whose disposition is `continue` may be the predecessor of a successor; every other disposition terminates the look chain.
>
> Any future transition MUST transactionally reload and revalidate evidence kind, exact target state, owner/domain/provider/model/policy/snapshot/cohort scope, every bound hash, look/cutoff/predecessor, eligible status/disposition, and current operator capability before state mutation/audit append. Admission cannot authorize active; outcome cannot authorize canary entry. This does not restore a policy-mutation API or serving authority.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance.** Tests MUST: reject noncanonical/unknown/missing/duplicate JSON for every registered top-level/nested schema and independently reproduce every literal policy/model golden SHA-256 plus rational, draw, stratum/cluster hash, typed-ref, report, evidence-body, and transition-binding content address; reject serving-arm empty-feature hashes and endpoint-model nonempty-feature hashes; exhaust tiny Bernoulli assignments to prove conditional complete-randomization equality; cover all four draw vectors plus entropy/template/rollback/crash/retry/commit-unknown/concurrency faults with no redraw or duplicate Assignment/receipt; prove all five cutoff/equality/late-fact/predecessor/disposition/unique-artifact rules, the complete disposition table, and exact cumulative alpha; verify every canonical sort/tie rule and Neumaier bit-pattern vector under nonfinite/FMA/reassociation negative oracles; verify hypergeometric tails, strict equality, caps, outward rounding, missing substitutions, singleton/one-arm bounds, and exhaustive compatible binary potential-outcome coverage; pass the deterministic 5,000-member many/tiny/degenerate/rare/all-zero/all-one benchmark within caps with order-independent hashes, retaining the known floating FFT normalization regression as a failing negative oracle; reproduce DR/SNIPS/ESS and bootstrap sampler/rank vectors, including selected-intention eligibility with unknown delivery exposure, and reject policy/reward/model leakage, hashes, support, overlap, ESS, and uncertainty failures without changing the gate disposition; and fault-test the sole writer, exact retry, rollback, distinct endpoint-report bindings, evidence-kind non-substitution, and complete transactional transition revalidation.
>
> **Research basis and bounded choice.** Bernoulli conditioning follows Pashley, Basse, and Miratrix, [*Conditional As-If Analyses in Randomized Experiments*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.01029). The exact per-stratum hypergeometric inversion implements the first conservative Bonferroni-adjusted binary ATE method described by [Li, Spertus, and Stark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03834), without claiming their floating ESI/Fisher implementation as an exact oracle. DR follows [Dudík, Langford, and Li](https://arxiv.org/abs/1103.4601). Plan immutability is informed by [PlanOut](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.3174), and assignment/exposure/metrics/analysis separation by Microsoft's [experimentation platform](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/publication/the-anatomy-of-a-large-scale-experimentation-platform/). Precomputed complete-randomization schedules were rejected because the bounded online cohort has an unknown roster and draws only after a unique live claim. Committed HMAC assignment was rejected because it adds a long-lived secret, rotation/version, and deterministic-input coupling without improving that atomic boundary. Store-owned OS-CSPRNG Bernoulli draws plus receipts fit the requirement.
>
> No clause creates an environment variable, CLI, policy-mutation authorization, or learned-serving authorization. Canary and active learned serving remain unavailable except as separately authorized and implemented by later Task 10 work.
>
> **▶ Amendment #93.8 (2026-07-26, initial memory action catalog).** This amendment supersedes conflicting #93/#93.4/#93.7 shorthand that names `off` as a memory candidate or event action. The initial schema-`2.0` memory action IDs are exactly ordered `static`, `long_term_top_4`, `long_term_top_8`. `static` is the champion and means no long-term recall: the recall provider is not called. There is no separate `off` action or event ID. When recall is disabled or its configured maximum is below 4, the point exposes only `static`, is exogenous, and emits no randomized Assignment. A configured maximum from 4 through 7 exposes `static`, `long_term_top_4`; a maximum of at least 8 exposes all three, with every retrieval still capped by that configured maximum. If context budgeting omits a selected recall item, Delivery records actual action `none` with fallback `context_budget`, while the intended arm/action remains unchanged for ITT. `none` is a delivery outcome, never a candidate action.
>
> Per #93.7, the admission plan freezes owner plus server claim-time block as the statistical stratum and a separate conversation-keyed `InterferencePlan`; session/episode are audit metadata, not cross-product blocks. Power simulation uses the same repeated-owner/time-block and conversation-cluster shape expected in production. The current ESS-weighted Wilson implementation remains simulation evidence only. Production evidence uses the five fixed UTC cutoffs and exact `stratified-bonferroni-hypergeom-ate-v1` bounds; unmodelled cross-conversation, shared-memory, tool-side-effect, or time carryover is ineligible. Bounded-continuous quality still requires a separate preregistered calibrated estimator and cannot replace the binary endpoint.
>
> The pure cohort loader reconstructs assignments, deliveries, outcomes, corrections, and per-look membership solely from the immutable PostgreSQL ledger and uses randomized arm/propensity for ITT. V1 OPE is selected-intention only, with exact marginal `mu` from the two deterministic arm policies; delivered-exposure OPE is deferred. Invalid claims, orphan/mismatched/duplicate facts, unsupported arms/actions, probability/support/overlap failures, incompatible scope, excess `ExpectedMembers`, provenance/calibration mismatch, and censoring violations remain fail-closed. Below-`MinimumMembers` views reconstruct but cannot seal. Only the admission sealer and `EvidenceStore.SealCanaryOutcome` may create eligible artifacts; the pure loader never writes, and no external caller supplies observations, reports, hashes, eligibility, or disposition. OPE remains diagnostic and never substitutes for either evidence kind.
>
> **Two-stage canary evidence.** `canary_admission` contains the verified snapshot, calibration, power analysis, frozen plans, safety/rollback limits, endpoint model refs, and explicit operator approval but no outcomes; it alone is eligible for an authorized `shadow -> canary`. `canary_outcome` is sealed only by `EvidenceStore.SealCanaryOutcome` from one closed #93.6/#93.7 view of real randomized traffic; it alone is eligible for a separately authorized `canary -> active`. Transition/evidence storage MUST reject kind substitution and the legacy single-report ambiguity.
>
> **Real controllable domains.** An adaptive assignment is emitted only where Aura controls a safe alternative **before** serving it. The initial implementation points are: (1) reasoning effort before each model round, before the request is built; (2) the ordered eligible results returned by tool discovery before deferred tools are exposed to the next model request; (3) ordered read-only skill candidates before a skill list/routing result is returned; (4) knowledge/document retrieval route, depth, and rerank strategy before retrieval executes; and (5) owner-scoped long-term memory recall immediately before the existing `ArchivalRecaller` invokes the deployed agent-memory MCP's `memory_get_context`. The first memory catalog is deliberately small: `off`, `long_term_top_4`, and `long_term_top_8`; the configured maximum is a hard safety cap and a disabled memory-recall setting makes learned memory actions ineligible. Every eligible memory action keeps short-term and reasoning recall disabled, preserves the existing untrusted-reference-data fencing, and passes the owner UUID as `user_identifier`. It reuses the current provider/MCP seam but removes recall from `ContextConfig.AlwaysBlock`/`messages[1]`. The exact fenced result becomes one synthetic non-persisted dynamic-tail item supplied to the context budgeter before it returns, protected as an indivisible item from L1/L2.5 rewriting or eviction, and positioned immediately before the current model-visible user message when one exists, otherwise at the tail. After every model-message transformation, the final request is rechecked against the hard cap and for byte-identical inclusion of that item. Only then may its delivery fact commit, still before model exposure. If the full item cannot fit, Aura omits it and records actual action `none` with fallback `context_budget`; partial or unlogged truncation is forbidden. The stable skill-only `messages[1]` block and its cache audit remain byte-identical across requests. It reuses the current sidecar and managed MCP bridge rather than implementing another retriever, graph client, or memory schema. Observing a model-emitted top-level tool call after selection is not a tool-discovery assignment. A model-emitted skill `use`, document query/scope, user-pinned skill, explicit reasoning effort, or on-demand memory-tool call is observation/exogenous input, not a behavior-policy draw. Multiplexed skill/knowledge decisions hidden inside tool arguments require a typed adapter at the internal candidate seam; skill/memory writes, forget, deduplication, entity mutation, and every other risky or destructive subaction remain outside exploration. Memory write, model/provider routing, context compression, multimodal routing, and retry/recovery are added only when their production call sites expose multiple pre-authorized controllable actions with domain-specific risk and evaluation contracts; until then they are explicit static/no-op or observation-only surfaces and cannot be advertised as learned.
>
> **Agent-memory reuse contract.** Aura's vendored Apache-2.0 fork under `docker/agent-memory` is the production execution path for the memory-recall domain. Reuse its POLE+O graph, user scoping, provenance-safe/exact dedup, non-cascading forget, managed MCP transport, and existing static recall provider/MCP call; do not retain its query-dependent result in the stable `messages[1]` block. Its labelled retrieval/audit/preference evaluator may be reused as an offline regression witness, but it is not a calibrated promotion artifact. For eligible memory delivery evidence, the same `memory_get_context` operation must add typed metadata beside the text: stable result node kind/ID/order, effective per-type K/count, immutable retriever/reranker/embedding/index revision, and a coherent corpus revision for the delivered read. The entire multi-query operation is bracketed by equal service-owned monotonic corpus epochs, and every writer capable of changing recall result membership, content, order, or score advances that epoch in the same transaction; Neo4j's default read-committed transaction and a final causal bookmark are insufficient. The adaptive projector's compatible `User` field repair and private adaptive edges need not advance it only after tests prove those writes cannot affect recall results. Missing/unequal epochs or any untracked result-affecting writer makes the row diagnostic-only. It must not add raw query/content or content fingerprints. Neo4j memory remains mutable serving data; PostgreSQL remains authoritative for assignment, propensity, delivery, outcome, correction, cohort, snapshot, and policy facts. The fork's buffered writer, reasoning traces, tool observations, formatted context, and absence of an exception are ineligible substitutes for a pre-serve durable assignment or an independent quality outcome. Adaptive payloads stay out of LLM-facing memory labels and tools.
>
> The private projector may reuse `:User {identifier}` only with agent-memory-compatible creation semantics: on create it sets non-null `id`, `created_at`, and compatible `attributes_json`, and on match it repairs legacy null schema fields without overwriting agent-memory attributes. It may alternatively attach with `MATCH` only after the supported agent-memory user upsert. Live proof must project first, then successfully perform an owner-scoped agent-memory write/read and preserve both memory and adaptive subgraphs. The vendored tree must include the upstream Apache-2.0 `LICENSE` and required notices in source and image, and Docker/Compose provenance must bind the upstream base/fork commit plus the actual Aura vendored-tree revision; it must not claim the post-fork tree is an exact `c1c2d65` archive. `AURA_AGENT_MEMORY_VENDOR_REV` is the required build-only provenance input for that label: release/CI sets it to the exact Aura Git revision whose `docker/agent-memory` tree is built, Docker/Compose fail closed when it is empty, and Aura never loads it as runtime config or stores it in `aura.settings`.
>
> **Skill reuse and self-improvement boundary.** The initial skill domain adapts only the ordering of already authorized read-only candidates. Creating, updating, installing, deleting, or otherwise mutating executable skills, code, configuration, prompts, policies, or model weights is never a runtime learning arm. Research from [SAGE](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.17102v2) supports testing exact producer-to-consumer skill reuse, but its AppWorld-only Qwen2.5-32B result depends on expert SFT and large-scale RL; its name-occurrence reuse signal, idealized same-scenario retrieval, CC BY-NC implementation, and multi-H100 training path are not production contracts or dependencies for Aura. Producer, immutable skill, consumer, gateway invocation, and outcome provenance proves exposure, not causal contribution: many skills may reach one consumer and one skill may reach many consumers. Reusable-skill learning therefore remains shadow-only until a separate amendment preregisters randomized skill/no-skill exposure or encouragement, many-to-many attribution, cluster/interference assumptions, reuse horizon, censoring, and contamination controls. It cannot copy a later reward to unrelated points or reuse the initial one-request estimator.
>
> **Adaptive improvement proposals.** The proposal/approval/application separation demonstrated by [BerriAI/self-improving-agent](https://github.com/BerriAI/self-improving-agent) is a useful review pattern, not an Aura dependency or authorization design. A future code/skill/config improvement workflow must bind a durable proposal to the exact source/artifact revision, verify explicit approval from the current user message on the server side, enforce Aura capability/owner scope and idempotency, apply in an isolated review boundary, run every normal Aura verification gate, and append an immutable audit before any push or activation. A model-supplied approval boolean, optional callback, exact-snippet replacement, or draft PR alone is insufficient. No autonomous production mutation is authorized by adaptive evidence.
>
> **Retrieval-policy evidence.** Lexical/structural, graph, vector, hybrid/reranked, and no-retrieval strategies are versioned candidate actions, not an assumed quality hierarchy. SAGE's ablation found query 2-gram retrieval closer to its privileged same-scenario result than query or skill embeddings, while a longer three-task chain regressed. Aura therefore freezes the complete retrieval implementation and thresholds, tenant/ACL scope, corpus/bookmark epoch, parser/chunker, embedding model, index, reranker, top-K, and tie-breaking semantics in each snapshot. The delivery fact records the actual exposed stable IDs/order and effective limits. Each candidate is benchmarked on Aura's own calibrated data and real model; extra graph hops, history length, or embedding sophistication are hypotheses that must earn promotion.
>
> **Projector and policy lifecycle.** The private Neo4j projection gains a production `Start`/`Stop` lifecycle composed at boot, with bounded lease/retry/dead-letter behavior, tombstone fencing, restart recovery, and privacy/non-recall tests; component-only tests or manual MCP projection are not lifecycle proof. The shadow release continues to expose no application policy mutation caller under #93.3. A future capability-gated CLI/API and its `PolicyService` may return only in one atomic slice containing its real composition root, authorization tests, append-only audit, live evidence, and rollback proof. Canary/active serving remains unavailable until that authorized surface, the durable cohort loader, and domain serving adapters land together.
>
> **Qwen/llama.cpp portability proof.** Qwen3.5 2B Q4_K_M remains a spike model, never the configured production-model proof. Its Aura end-to-end test MUST change only allow-listed rows in `aura.settings` to select `llamacpp`, the Qwen model ID, and the OpenAI-compatible base URL; capture the prior rows first; exercise Aura's real request/runner/ledger/projection path; then restore the rows exactly and prove equality. Environment files and production defaults are not rewritten. A passing run demonstrates provider portability and contract execution only; it does not authorize promotion or support a production quality claim.
>
> **Implementation and activation gates.** Each slice is test-first and removes superseded generic/dead paths when its typed replacement lands. Every Go edit passes affected unit and race tests plus repository `go vet`/`go build`; final closure also requires the full lint suite, live PostgreSQL/Neo4j/agent-memory privacy and deletion/restart/rollback tests, owned-surface coverage at least 85%, mutation kill rate at least 70% on critical adaptive code, real configured-model shadow and preregistered canary evidence, an independent adversarial approval, operator approval, rebuild of the deployed Aura binary/container at migration head, atomic verified commits, push, and green remote CI. Until all gates pass, Aura serves the static baseline.

Conversation turns and assistant cache metrics retain their existing conversation-store atomicity. Schema-`2.0` adaptive facts follow the typed timing boundaries already fixed by #93.4: an eligible Assignment commits before learned execution, its Delivery commits before exposure, and an independent evaluator appends an Outcome when that observation exists. Those facts cannot be collapsed into one terminal-turn transaction without falsifying assignment, exposure, or evaluator time. The command requires explicit `--confirm-operator-approval` and capability `adaptive.evidence.seal`, owned by the cohort owner. It accepts one bounded, strict canonical manifest binding exactly five frozen child artifacts; it is not a policy, canary-transition, active-transition, outcome, or learned-serving mutation surface.

The currently measured local witness is llama.cpp `b9994` / revision `14d3ba45f`, image digest `sha256:b57dce073940d6f347d59230d4d28fc947db8948f2eb162326008380b07bab77`, model SHA-256 `aaf42c8b7c3cab2bf3d69c355048d4a0ee9973d48f16c731c0520ee914699223`; a later run records what it actually verifies and fails on artifact drift rather than silently claiming these values.

Requests use temperature zero, the frozen prompt/tool templates, and at most one in-flight benchmark inference even if the server exposes more slots. No password, API key, `.env` value, or other settings row may enter the journal. A fixed PostgreSQL advisory lock key `4707759426009125972` serializes capture/apply/run/restore. Every Aura settings `Upsert` and `Delete` takes the matching transaction advisory lock; raw DBA DML is outside application guarantees.

> Under the lock, one transaction first recovers any expired prior journal, verifies that recovery byte-for-byte, then captures the three rows and commits the journal plus overrides atomically. The real Aura child is started only after that commit. Cleanup on success, error, panic, SIGINT, or SIGTERM restores existing rows with all captured metadata, deletes rows that were originally absent, verifies exact equality, marks the audit complete, and only then releases the lock. A killed process leaves the durable journal: the next benchmark invocation and Aura boot recover an expired journal before `OverlayEnv`; until recovery succeeds, boot/benchmark fail closed instead of loading the temporary rows. The command heartbeat extends a bounded lease while its child is alive. Concurrent settings writes through Aura block on the same lock and therefore cannot be overwritten by restore. Failure-injection tests cover every transaction boundary, signal cleanup, stale-journal recovery, absent/existing/mixed rows, exact timestamp/actor restoration, and a waiting concurrent writer.

Fixtures may seed only the committed synthetic document/memory inputs under a run-scoped namespace and must delete them after retention/privacy assertions. The harness must prove reasoning, tool discovery, read-only queried skill routing, document retrieval, and long-term memory recall each reached its production typed seam; a missing domain invalidates the run.

>
> JSON types and nested field order are part of the schema. Timestamps are canonical UTC RFC3339Nano strings; durations/counts/tokens are nonnegative JSON integers; SHA-256 values are lowercase 64-hex strings; UUIDs are canonical lowercase strings. `git` is `revision:string,dirty:boolean,changed_files:array`, where each changed-file object is `path:string,sha256:string`, sorted by path. `environment` is `os:string,arch:string,aura_version:string,go_version:string,migration_head:string,neo4j_revision:string|null,agent_memory_revision:string|null`. `model` is `provider_id:string,model_id:string,base_url_class:enum(loopback,remote),server_name:string|null,server_version:string|null,server_revision:string|null,artifact_name:string|null,artifact_sha256:string|null,snapshot_revision:string|null,image_digest:string|null`; Qwen requires every nullable provenance field except `server_name` to be non-null, while an upstream production API may legitimately report null. `frozen_inputs` is `dataset_id:string,dataset_revision:integer,dataset_sha256:string,prompt_template_sha256:string,evaluator_id:string,evaluator_revision:integer,calibration_sha256:string|null,action_catalogs_sha256:string,policy_version:string,policy_sha256:string,snapshot_id:string|null,snapshot_sha256:string|null,price_table_id:string|null,price_table_revision:integer|null,price_table_sha256:string|null,seed:integer`. The three price-table fields are all non-null exactly when any scenario cost is calculated from that table; they are all null for provider-reported costs and local/unknown cost. Unknown fields, duplicate fields, noncanonical key order, nonfinite numbers, negative integers, unsorted arrays, inconsistent nullable groups, and trailing data are rejected.
>
> Scenario records are ordered by the deterministic schedule and have exact fields `scenario_id`, `domain`, `request_id`, `assignment_id`, `delivery_event_id`, `quality_outcome_id`, `harm_outcome_id`, `champion_action_id`, `recommended_action_id`, `intended_action_id`, `actual_action_id`, `action_probabilities`, `quality`, `harm`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `latency_ns`, `cost_usd`, `status`, `reason_codes`. The report contains no raw conversation, prompt, tool result, memory/document content, content-derived fingerprint, secret, or owner attribute; IDs and registered artifact hashes provide linkage. Latency is monotonic end-to-end from immediately before `Runner.Turn` through its terminal event and is stored as integer nanoseconds. Tokens come from provider usage. Cost is the exact provider-reported USD value when available, otherwise a versioned price-table calculation whose table hash is bound; local/unknown cost is JSON `null`, never zero. Summaries state sample sizes and missingness and never impute missing measurements.
>
> In a scenario record, `domain` is one of the five registered domains; every event ID is `string|null` and is non-null exactly when that fact exists. `action_probabilities` is a catalog-ordered array of exact objects `action_id:string,probability:number`; each probability is finite in `[0,1]` and the array sums to exactly `1` under the registered binary64 summation. `quality` and `harm` are each `null` or an exact object `evaluator_id:string,evaluator_revision:integer,value:number|null,eligible:boolean,reason_codes:array<string>`; a missing observation is null rather than a fabricated zero. `cost_usd` is a finite nonnegative number or null. Scenario `status` is exactly one of `pass`, `fail`, `invalid`; `reason_codes` is a lexicographically sorted unique array from the registered bounded reason catalog. `summary` has exact order `scenario_count`, `pass_count`, `fail_count`, `invalid_count`, `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`, `latency_count`, `latency_p50_ns`, `latency_p95_ns`, `latency_p99_ns`, `cost_count`, `cost_usd`, `domains`; the first nine scalar counts/tokens are integers, percentile fields are integer-or-null, `cost_usd` is number-or-null, and `domains` is a five-domain registered-order array of objects `domain:string,scenario_count:integer,pass_count:integer,fail_count:integer,invalid_count:integer`. Top-level `mode` is one of the two entrypoint modes, `verdict` is one of `pass`, `fail`, `invalid`, and `portability_only` is true if and only if mode is `qwen-portability`.
>
> **Fixed control/fault matrix.** `controls` has exact ordered cases: `negative_control`, `static_equivalence`, `restart_recovery`, `rollback_static`, `privacy_redaction`, `retention_cleanup`, `same_owner_concurrency`, `cross_owner_isolation`, `assignment_write_failure`, `delivery_write_failure`, `outcome_write_failure`, `model_transport_failure`, `memory_epoch_mismatch`, `settings_apply_failure`, `settings_restore_failure`, `stale_override_recovery`. Each has `status`, `started_at`, `completed_at`, `evidence_ids`, `reason_codes`. Static equivalence compares served champion bytes and action probability `1.0`; shadow recommendation remains diagnostic. Restart/rollback prove no learned exposure. Privacy/retention inspect persisted stores after cleanup. Concurrency uses the preregistered four-client schedule and proves unique point identity and owner isolation. Injected assignment/delivery failures prove no unlogged learned exposure; other faults prove bounded failure and exact recovery.
>
> A control record's `status` is one of `pass`, `fail`, `invalid`; `evidence_ids` is a lexicographically sorted unique array of canonical UUID strings; `reason_codes` follows the same bounded/sorted rule as scenarios. The exact concurrency schedule uses clients `C0..C3`: `C0=(owner A, conversation A0, r01)`, `C1=(owner A, conversation A0, r02)`, `C2=(owner A, conversation A1, m01)`, `C3=(owner B, conversation B0, k01)`. Start C0 and block it immediately after its Assignment commits but before model execution; start C1 and prove it cannot reach Assignment while C0 holds the conversation lock; start C2 and C3 and block each after its own Assignment; then release in exact order C3, C2, C0, C1. Every wait has a bounded timeout and records invalid on timeout. The assertions are: four unique request/assignment IDs; C1 assignment time strictly after C0 terminal time; C2/C3 assignment times before C0 release; no cross-owner facts; one delivery per exposed assignment; and the static champion remains probability `1.0`. No live latency sample from this controlled schedule enters scientific percentiles.
>
> `verdict` is `pass`, `fail`, or `invalid`. Any schema/provenance/dataset/catalog drift, missing domain/control, broken linkage, private payload, non-exact settings restore, or failed safety control is `invalid`. A valid Qwen run can be `pass` only for provider portability and remains non-promotable. A production-shadow quality failure is `fail`, not invalid, when execution/evidence are otherwise complete.
>
