Il multi-skill selector è il flag `--skill` del CLI; il format-keyword teaching vive nella builtin skill. 004b resta valido come misura (native 3× più veloce, hash canonico) ma moot quando è il modello a guidare il CLI.]**
- Writer in `~/.aura/skills/pending/<name>/` per le mutation in attesa di approval; al `Approva` move atomico in `~/.aura/skills/active/`.
- Audit log append-only in **Postgres** tabella `aura.skill_audit` di OGNI mutation con `{id, ts, actor_id (fk aura.identities), action, name, content_hash, source, approval_source (enum), paused_state_token fk, computed_risk_tier, gate_recommended, gate_taken, blocklist_override}`. Migrate **`0010_skill_audit.up.sql`** aggiunta in Slice 7c (floor `0009_scheduler` — D-32; NON `0007`, riservato da Slice 8/10 shipped). Query via sqlc `internal/db/queries/skill_audit.sql`. `approval_source` (Area #10 closed 2026-05-28) enum `{ask_user, cli, auto}` esplicito su COME la mutation è stata autorizzata, governato dalla matrice D-29 (vedi sotto). **Metadata consolidation (D-19)**: usage/archive state (status/last_used_at/use_count) NON è in colonne ALTER di `skill_audit` — vive in un sidecar JSON per-skill (atomic-write, la sola live-state source) + un'opzionale tabella `snippet_runs` (migration 0011) per le forensics per-run.

**Discovery + prompt injection design (amended #48, D-06/D-07).** Le skill NON entrano nel system prompt (`messages[0]` resta byte-stable, CAP-04 invariant). Tre livelli:
- **Manifest** (name + trigger-rich description per skill) vive nella **Description del tool `skill`**, generata a registry-build da `internal/skills/manifest.go` (precedente: `toolSearchDescription(reg)` in 08.1, D-06). Turn-stable: cambia solo su skill add/remove (busta la tools-prefix cache UNA volta, raro, accettato). Ordine alfabetico/byte-stable (cache-load-bearing). Oltre `AURA_SKILL_MANIFEST_CAP_BYTES` (~8k, Codex parity) il blocco termina con "N more — search with skill action=list {query}" (BM25 overflow, D-09 — riusa il ranker 08.1).
- **`always:true` bodies** rendono in UN solo blocco user-role a **`messages[1]`** (D-07, pattern convergente Claude Code CLAUDE.md / Codex AGENTS.md; il concat in system-prompt di nanobot è l'anti-pattern). Questo è IL seam che Phase 14 Agent.md condivide (profile first, always-skills after). **VINCOLO FLAGGATO**: l'evictor L2.5 di `conversations/context.go` deve proteggere il blocco `messages[1]` come protegge il system L0 — altrimenti una conversazione lunga sfratta silenziosamente la always-mode.
- **`messages[0]`** riceve la sezione frozen **"Skills — capability gaps"** del canonical system prompt (amendment #49, D-39) — **RIDOTTA a pointer dal #51/D-40**: il routing operativo (check-installed, format-token discovery, self-install, use-by-path) vive nella builtin skill `find-skills-aura` a messages[1]; messages[0] tiene solo il principio (skills esistono, la skill always-on insegna il loop). Resta una const byte-stable mechanism-not-enumeration (D-08/D-09 invarianti).

> **Amendment #49 (D-39, Phase 11 gap-closure, live-E2E-driven, 2026-06-05).** Il live xlsx North-Star E2E (judge 0.40 vs gate ≥0.90, `docs/aura-skills-eval-2026-06-05.md`) ha provato che la policy D-06 "UNA sola frase" era insufficiente: il modello — istruito solo con "skills exist; the skill tool lists/applies them" + la doctrine `tool_search` — ha razionalmente brute-forzato web+sandbox (3× `tool_search` a vuoto, 15× `sandbox_exec` con Python ad-hoc) senza mai toccare la catalog→install path. Tre supersessioni discovery-routing, tutte cache-safe (const byte-stabili, nessun cambio schema, zero nuove dep), per il principio "se il modello non invoca il tool è bug del system prompt o del manifest, NON del test" (§Slice 1 + memoria `feedback_agent_must_know_tools_exist`):
> 1. `agent.SystemPrompt` è promosso al **canonical capability-gap system prompt** (`docs/system_prompt.txt`, adottato verbatim): tone, loop budget discipline, tool doctrine (tool_search 2-phrasing cap), sezione "Skills — capability gaps" (installed-check prima di build-by-hand; artifact families → `skill action=catalog`; install SEMPRE via ask_user, mai self-granted; snippet BY-PATH `python3 /skills/<name>/...`), sandbox/artifact verify-before-report, honesty, nota operator-pinned `messages[1]`. Nomina solo i verbi strutturali (`tool_search`/`text_response`/`skill`/`ask_user`) — mai il tool set concreto: D-08/D-09 reggono.
> 2. Il no-result di `tool_search` guadagna una coda fissa di orientamento verso `skill action=catalog` — il momento esatto del capability gap deve instradare DENTRO il sistema skills, non verso codice ad-hoc.

> **▶ Amendment #53 (D-42, il modello scrive file via fs tool — non via heredoc shell; parity fs nella eval registry, 2026-06-06).** Driver = 9 run live del gate D-35 post-#52: l'unico 1.00 era taintato dal leak del hint word nel run-dir (correttamente bocciato dal floor prompt-natural, poi fixato); con prompt naturale il best è 0.50-0.60, e il run 9 mostra la root cause meccanica: il modello chiude discovery+install (selfInstall/target/selector tutti true) e raccoglie i dati, poi brucia ~10 `shell_exec` fallendo la SCRITTURA dello script multi-riga — 4 heredoc consecutivi morti (`here-document delimited by end-of-file`: terminatore mai matchato — repro: il wrap cwd di `shell_exec` è innocente con LF+terminatore pulito; CRLF/indentazione lo rompono), poi `python -c` col footgun backslash Windows (`'D:\tmp\build_xlsx.py'` → `\b`=backspace), budget esaurito, zero artifact. TRE concause, TRE fix:
> 1. **Parity violation nella eval registry (bug, fix mandato dalla regola #52 punto 4):** la production registry registra i 5 fs tool nativi dal #50/D-15c; la seam-free dell'eval li OMETTEVA — il modello in eval non aveva `fs_write` nel manifest (un suo `tool_search` ha risposto "no matching tools") mentre in produzione l'avrebbe avuto. La eval registry registra ora anche `fs_read`/`fs_write`/`fs_edit`/`fs_grep`/`fs_glob` con `WorkspaceRoot` = run workspace (in produzione il root vuoto = cwd del processo, che È il workspace annunciato dal tail hint — semantica identica).
> 2. **Il canonical prompt `<machine>` insegna WRITE sui file tool nativi:** la riga "Prefer the native file tools (read, exact-string edit, grep, glob) for surgical changes" ometteva il verbo write e spingeva "direct filesystem work" su `shell_exec` — il modello era letteralmente istruito a scrivere file via shell. Riga emendata: il CONTENUTO dei file (script inclusi) si scrive col file-write/file-edit tool nativo, MAI via heredoc shell o blob echo/printf quotati (fragili al quoting, provato live); `shell_exec` serve a ESEGUIRE. Prefix cache: un bust one-shot, poi il prefix è di nuovo byte-stable (`docs/system_prompt.txt` sync-enforced dal test).
> 3. **`shell_exec` normalizza CRLF→LF nel `command`** (hardening: un modello che emette CRLF rompe il wrap POSIX di cwd-tracking — repro committata nel test). Nessun cambio di contratto wire.

Nessuna nuova env, nessuna nuova dep, nessun nuovo tool: `fs_*` erano già shippati e in produzione — questo amendment chiude il gap eval↔production e il gap prompt↔toolbelt.

**SKILL.md format** (agentskills.io spec compat, D-30):
```
---
name: aura-implementation-loop      # ≤64, [a-z0-9-], must match dir name
description: Trigger-rich one-liner (≤1024) — incorporates when-to-use inline.
# Optional, tolerated-but-inert (agentskills.io interop): license, compatibility, metadata, allowed-tools
# Aura extensions: always: true (D-07/D-10) ; type: instruction|snippet (default instruction)
---

# Body markdown freeform
```
Parse con una **vera libreria YAML** (`goccy/go-yaml`, RESEARCH-verified — il
double-quoted scalar con escaped quotes del corpus reale richiede un parser vero;
+ CRLF normalization). NIENTE `when_to_use`/`tools` field (la description ricca
incorpora il when-to-use, confermato dalla spec). `always:true` è proposable dal
modello ma il gate lo flagga ("⚠ ALWAYS-ON: steers every future turn"); `install`
lo STRIPpa incondizionatamente dalle skill di terze parti (D-10).

./aura chat "ho bisogno di un'analisi statistica avanzata. cerca su skills.sh"

**Acceptance.**
- [ ] **SKILL.md format minimo**: frontmatter YAML obbligatorio (`name`, `description`), corpo non vuoto. `name` regex `^[a-z0-9-]+$`. **NO** `when_to_use:` o `tools:` field (rimossi dal design — la `description` ben scritta incorpora il when-to-use inline, pattern Anthropic-style confermato da `D:/tmp/assistant-ui/.claude/skills/tap/SKILL.md`). File invalidi loggati + skippati (no crash).
- [ ] Multi-root precedence: `~/.aura/skills/active/` override `internal/config/defaults/skills/`. Test asserisce override visibile in `list()`.
- [ ] TTL cache 1s preservato dal pre-rewrite.
- [ ] **Manifest packing (amended #48, D-09)**: il manifest (name + trigger-rich description, 1 riga/skill) vive nella **Description del tool `skill`** (D-06), cap a `AURA_SKILL_MANIFEST_CAP_BYTES` (~8k); oltre il cap il blocco termina con "N more — search with skill action=list {query}" (BM25 overflow — il `list` è BM25-ranked su name+description, riusa il ranker 08.1). Il body si carica on-demand via `skill(action=info)`. **NON** "tutte le skill listate anche 100+" (acceptance pre-rewrite SUPERSEDED — un manifest illimitato sfonda il context). Ordine alfabetico/byte-stable (cache-load-bearing).
- [ ] **Mutation flow (create/update/install/delete) Risk-Based (Area #5 closed 2026-05-28)**: il tool scrive in `pending/<name>/`, calcola `tier = scoring.ComputeSkillTier(action, body)` (oggi: create/update/install → RISKY, delete → DESTRUCTIVE). Ritorna tool result `{name, content_hash, risk_tier, gate_recommended:true, status:'pending'}`. **NON** ritorna automaticamente `ErrAwaitingUserInput`: l'agente decide se ri-emettere `ask_user(kind=approval, ResumeContext={action:'activate'|'install_active'|'delete_active', name})`. Resume handler: approve → `Writer.Activate()` (move atomico pending→active) + `Loader.Invalidate()` + audit `gate_taken=true`. Reject → delete pending + audit `gate_taken=true`. Se agente skippa gate: skill RESTA in `pending/` (non caricata), Notifier IMMEDIATE alert, audit `gate_taken=false`, l'utente attiva con `aura skills approve <name>` o ignora. **NO `approve` action model-facing (D-03)** — l'attivazione è solo umana/CLI. Edit ("approva con modifiche"): out of scope Slice 7.
- [ ] **Audit log + coherence matrix (amended #48, D-29)**: ogni mutation (anche le reject) scritte nella tabella `aura.skill_audit` di Postgres (sqlc-managed, migration **0010**). `aura skills audit --since=1h` query SQL. Postgres trigger `BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE` su `skill_audit` → `RAISE EXCEPTION` (audit append-only enforced a livello DB). La **5-row coherence matrix D-29** governa `(approval_source, paused_state_token, gate_recommended, gate_taken)` via CHECK SQL:

  | Event | approval_source | paused_state_token | gate_recommended | gate_taken |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | Mutation scritta in pending (gate non ancora esercitato) | NULL | NULL | true | false |
  | User approved via ask_user resume | `ask_user` | NOT NULL | true | true |
  | User rejected via ask_user resume | `ask_user` | NOT NULL | true | true |
  | Operatore CLI approve / `--allow-blocklisted` | `cli` (+`blocklist_override`) | NULL | true | true |
  | System (TTL `auto_archive`, `cleanup_pending_stale`) | `auto` | NULL | false | true |

- [ ] **BEFORE TRUNCATE trigger (amendment #17, Pitfall #6 P0)**: function `raise_audit_immutable_truncate()` + trigger `skill_audit_truncate_block BEFORE TRUNCATE ON aura.skill_audit FOR EACH STATEMENT`. Acceptance test (`db_integration`): connect as `aura_migrate`, `TRUNCATE aura.skill_audit;` → returns explicit error `audit table is append-only`. Cross-link role separation: connect as `aura_app`, same TRUNCATE → returns permission denied (role lacks TRUNCATE privilege). Both gates active = belt-and-suspenders defense per Pitfall #6 P0.
- [ ] ~~**Catalog browse default-ON (amended #48, D-12)**: `action=catalog`, `aura skills catalog list`, `disable-catalog` escape hatch, audit enable/disable.~~ **[SUPERATA #51/D-40: niente action=catalog, niente CLI catalog, niente escape hatch — discovery via `npx skills find` nel sandbox.]**
- [ ] **`Validator.SanitizeName` chokepoint (audit round 1 P0)**: `internal/skills/paths.go` espone `SanitizeName(name) (clean string, err error)` — UNICA via per derivare path filesystem da user input. Regex `^[a-z0-9-]+$`, length 1-64, no reserved (`init`, `delete`, `.`, `..`). Writer + Deleter + Installer DEVONO chiamarlo prima di `filepath.Join(skillsDir, name)`. Test asserisce ogni file-touch site via static analysis (`grep -L 'SanitizeName' internal/skills/{writer,deleter,installer}.go` → empty).
- [ ] **skills.sh integration ~~via native Go clone (amended #48, D-14/D-15 — npx SUPERSEDED)~~ [SUPERATA #51/D-40: l'intero blocco sotto è la spec dell'installer Go cancellato — install = `npx skills add` via shell; symlink-risk e blocklist si spostano al Loader scan]**:
  - **NESSUNA dipendenza `node`/`npm` host** (droppata: native clone WINS, spike 004b).
  - Catalog browse: **client JSON `GET /api/search?q=` lax-decode** (D-11, spike 003), rank by `installs`, mai `DisallowUnknownFields`. HTML scrape DEAD.
  - Install: `exec.LookPath("git")` fixed-argv `git clone --depth 1 --single-branch -c core.autocrlf=false <repoURL> <scratchDir>` (D-15) + copy skill subdir + **symlink-strip a materialization** (Lstat-no-follow — i symlink risolvono in-container, spike 005) + **Aura canonical hash** (byte-sorted `(relPath,bytes)` sha256, TOFU pin — NON l'upstream `skills-lock.json` `computedHash`, locale/platform-sensitive). Post-install `ParseSkill()` re-validation prima di `Invalidate()`.
  - **`AURA_SKILL_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_SEC` (90s)** via `context.WithTimeout`.
  - Install gate surfaces red flags (D-13): `metadata.*.install[]` blocks, tool wildcards, bundled-executable count; `always` stripped (D-10); body injection-blocklist (D-27).
  - **Acceptance**: install d'una skill che contiene un symlink fuori dal suo tree → lo strip lo rimuove a materialization, test asserisce (il `--ignore-scripts` pre-rewrite era un no-op — il clone non gira mai postinstall, D-14 — quindi quell'acceptance è moot e rimossa).
- [ ] **Capability boundary open-by-default per single-user**: nel tabula-rasa Aura locale, l'identity seed `'local'` (Slice 1.7) ha capability grant `'*'` (wildcard) — l'agente può self-extend liberamente (gate-ato comunque da `ask_user`). Capability lookup via `aura.capability_grants` (sqlc), non hard-coded: struttura estendibile per future multi-user senza toccare il codice. **Scaffolding intenzionale**: nessuna slice 1→10 ha consumer che chiama `HasCapability` (l'enforcement effettivo arriva con la slice multi-user/auth futura). Per oggi `HasCapability` è esportato e testabile, ma sempre `true` di fatto via grant `'*'` — non rimuoverlo, è il foundation pre-built per multi-user.
- [ ] `skill.info(name)` ritorna corpo intero come `ToolResult` — usa il pattern Slice 1 (preview + sidecar file se >2 KiB).
- [ ] **Prompt injection guard espanso (audit round 1 P0)**: body size cap `AURA_SKILL_BODY_CAP_BYTES` (default `32768` = 32 KiB, era hardcoded, promosso a env in Area #8 closed 2026-05-28) a write time. Refuse write se body contiene una di queste sequence (literal blocklist):
  - OpenAI ChatML: `<|im_start|>`, `<|im_end|>`, `<|endoftext|>`
  - Anthropic: `</system>`, `</human>`, `</assistant>`, `\n\nHuman:`, `\n\nAssistant:`
  - Llama / Mistral: `[INST]`, `[/INST]`, `<<SYS>>`, `<</SYS>>`
  - Meta / Llama 3: `<|begin_of_text|>`, `<|start_header_id|>`, `<|end_header_id|>`, `<|eot_id|>`
  - DeepSeek / Gemma / Qwen: `<|fim_begin|>`, `<|fim_hole|>`, `<start_of_turn>`, `<end_of_turn>`
  Basic literal check, no semantic detection. Lista refresh-abile via config (`AURA_SKILL_INJECTION_BLOCKLIST`).

### Slice 7e-core — Executable code snippets + TTL archived (v1; pattern analyzer → 7f v1.x per amendment #13)

> **Pattern reference**: rubato da Voyager (Wang et al., NeurIPS 2023) "skill library" pattern — agent costruisce libreria persistente di funzioni eseguibili discoverable via semantic embedding + lifelong learning. Plus mem0 procedural memory ADD-only pattern.
>
> **Idea (amended #48/#55, D-04/D-15b/D-17/D-21/D-01)**: gli script Python/shell utili vengono **salvati** come `SKILL.md type: snippet`, **materializzati** come file su `AURA_SKILL_EXPORT_DIR` (la skills-home host), **scoperti** via BM25 `action=list` (D-21 — semantic Neo4j HNSW deferred a 7f/Phase 15), **eseguiti by-path sul TERMINALE FULL DELL'HOST** (`shell_exec`, `<interpreter> <host-export-path>` — es. `python3 ~/.aura/skills/export/<name>/<name>.py`, interpreter+path MAI exec bit) **[SUPERATO #55/D-01 — postura HOST-PRIMARY (Phase 18): supera il wording #48 "eseguiti by-path via il shipped `sandbox_exec` → `sandboxagent.Client` HTTP `:2468` (`python3 /skills/<name>.py`)" come PATH PRIMARIO; `sandbox_exec` resta l'escalation deliberata per untrusted/model code]**. `action=use` ritorna le istruzioni + l'`<host-export-path>`; il modello esegue via `shell_exec` (D-04 — il codice non ri-entra mai nel context, NESSUN bespoke `run`/`executor.go` con `sandbox.Runner.Execute`, che è DEAD). Token saving ~520/riuso.
>
> **Dipendenze (amended #48)**: il **sandbox-agent portable hardening floor** (token D-38 + seccomp + no-new-privileges + read-only rootfs + egress allowlist D-37) — il codice model-authored rende load-bearing l'isolation gap. Il gVisor `runsc` overlay + seccomp re-tightening sono una **regressione sandbox-wide di Phase 8** (D-38 scope note), tracciata lì, NON owned da Phase 11; Phase 11 dipende solo dal floor portabile. NIENTE Slice 2b bespoke session (killed, amendment #44).
>
> **Scope v1 (amendment #13)**: questa è la Slice 7e-core. `pattern_analyzer` cross-conv auto-suggest (sezione "Pattern auto-suggest" nella smoke, env vars `AURA_SKILL_PATTERN_ANALYSIS_*` + `AURA_SKILL_AUTOSUGGEST_*`) è SPLIT in Slice 7f (v1.x deferred SKILL-V2-01). 7e-core ship ~450 LOC; 7f ~250 LOC.

#### Estensione SKILL.md (backwards-compat con 7a)

Nuovo field `type: instruction|snippet` (default `instruction` per backwards-compat con Skills esistenti). Se `type: snippet`:

```yaml
---
name: parse_csv_groupby
type: snippet
language: python          # python|shell|js (multi-lang)
description: Parse CSV from URL or path, group by column, aggregate.
inputs_schema:
  source: { type: string, desc: "URL or local path" }
  by:     { type: string, desc: "Column to group by" }
  agg:    { type: string, enum: [sum, mean, count], default: sum }
outputs_desc: JSON array of {group_key, value}
deps: [pandas]            # PyPI per Python, npm per JS, none per shell
needs_network: false      # → influenza Risk-Based tier al run-time
needs_workspace: false    # → influenza sandbox mount (Slice 2b)
tags: [csv, data-analysis, groupby]
---

```python
import pandas as pd
import json, sys

args = json.load(sys.stdin)
df = pd.read_csv(args["source"])
result = df.groupby(args["by"]).agg(args.get("agg", "sum")).reset_index()
print(result.to_json(orient="records"))
```
```

Body = code block in fenced markdown con `language` matching. Parser estrae code, lo **materializza** come file su `AURA_SKILL_EXPORT_DIR` (la skills-home host); `action=use` ritorna il path. L'esecuzione è **by-path sul TERMINALE FULL DELL'HOST** (`shell_exec`, `<interpreter> <host-export-path>`, D-04/D-01) **[SUPERATO #55/D-01: supera il wording #48 "by-path via il shipped `sandbox_exec` (`python3 /skills/<name>.py`)" come primario; host shell_exec è ora il primario, sandbox l'escalation]** — NON `sandbox.Run(...)`/`sandbox.Runner.Execute(...)` (seam DEAD, amendment #44). Materializzazione solo su activation (pending/archived non materializzano; archive/delete de-materializza — export dir in lockstep col loader state).

#### Pattern analysis multi-conversation (smart auto-suggest)

Background goroutine `internal/skills/pattern_analyzer.go`:

```
Loop ogni AURA_SKILL_PATTERN_ANALYSIS_INTERVAL_MIN=60 minuti:
  1. Query: tutti i tool_call con tool='execute' degli ultimi N giorni
     (default N=AURA_SKILL_PATTERN_ANALYSIS_WINDOW_DAYS=7)
     filtrato per identity_id corrente
  2. Per ogni execute call, estrai (code, args, exit_status):
     - Solo successful (exit_status=0)
     - Solo code >= AURA_SKILL_AUTOSUGGEST_MIN_LOC=20 righe
  3. Compute embedding del code (riusa aura-llama-embed Slice 0.7)
  4. Cluster via HNSW similarity threshold 0.85
  5. Per cluster size >= AURA_SKILL_AUTOSUGGEST_MIN_OCCURRENCES=3:
     - Synthesize snippet candidate (LLM call: "Generalizza questi 3
       script in una funzione parametrizzata")
     - Generate name + description + inputs_schema
     - Emit ask_user(kind=approval, ResumeContext:
       {action: 'save_snippet', candidate_yaml: ...},
       question: "Ho notato che hai eseguito 3 volte uno script per
       [X]. Vuoi salvarlo come `parse_csv_groupby`? [✅ Salva]
       [✏️ Modifica nome] [❌ No]")
  6. Risk-Based: tier RISKY (mutation) → gate_recommended=true
```

Trigger event-driven (non solo periodic): on `execute` exit_status=0, append a queue + lazy analyzer.

#### TTL 90gg + archived state

```
Metadata = sidecar JSON per-skill (D-19, the ONLY live-state source, atomic-write):
  last_used_at: timestamp ultimo successful run
  status: active|archived|deprecated
  use_count: int
  archived_at: timestamp (NULL se active)
(NON colonne ALTER su skill_audit — D-19 metadata consolidation.)

Sweep = cron TaskKind `skill_ttl_sweep` (D-16, NOT a goroutine), seeded daily
like the backup tasks (Phase-10 machinery: persistence/HA/missed-catch-up free):
  Per ogni skill type=snippet (scan sidecars, small N):
    Se last_used_at < now() - AURA_SKILL_SNIPPET_TTL_DAYS(90) AND status='active':
      status = 'archived' ; archived_at = now() ; de-materialize from /skills
      INSERT skill_audit (action='auto_archive', source='auto',
        approval_source='auto', gate_recommended=false, gate_taken=true)  # D-29 row 5
  NOTE: adding 'skill_ttl_sweep' requires ALTERing the 0009 scheduler_tasks.kind
  CHECK constraint in 0010 (the task is system-seeded, not model-schedulable).

Discovery default (skill action=list, BM25):
  WHERE status='active'  (archived skip)

Recovery:
  skill(action=restore, name) → status='active', archived_at=NULL ; re-materialize
  Audit log RESTORE entry
```

## Slice 8 — AG-UI gateway (transport agnostico CLI / Telegram / web)

> **Slice 0.9 amendment**: l'AG-UI emitter consuma `iter.Seq2[*Event, error]` direttamente da `(*LlmAgent).Run()` (Slice 0.9). Mapping `*Event` Aura → AG-UI event types diventa una sola funzione `mapToAGUI(*Event) []agui.Event` invece di subscribere a 5 channel/callback diversi del Loop. Saving stimato: **−100 LOC** (no Subscribe/emitter plumbing custom, range-over-func nativo).

**Goal.** Esporre il Loop di Aura attraverso il protocollo **AG-UI** ([ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui)), MIT, **28 event types attivi** (~~17-25~~ corretto #56 da spike 015; +5 `THINKING_*` deprecati da NON usare — `REASONING_*` è il canonico), transport SSE/WS/webhook. Aura diventa un'agent compatibile con qualsiasi UI AG-UI-aware (CopilotKit, AG-UI Dojo, future custom frontend, Telegram bot adapter, browser SPA). Niente lock-in al transport; sostituisce/preempt qualsiasi channel-adapter custom.

**Razionale.** Out-of-scope ha sempre tenuto fuori Telegram, dashboard, web. Risolto via standard invece che codice custom: implementi una volta il protocollo, ogni transport ha il suo client (Telegram bot in-process via SSE, browser via fetch+SSE, CLI in-process). Pattern verificato production-grade: LangGraph + CrewAI (1st party), Microsoft Agent Framework + Google ADK + AWS Strands + Mastra + Pydantic AI + Agno + LlamaIndex + AG2 (1st party integrations), Claude Agent SDK + Langroid (community).

**Pre-requisiti.**
- Slice 1.8 conversation persistence (`threadId` = `conversation_id`).
- Slice 1.5 multi-pause FIFO (`outcome{type: interrupt}` con `interrupts[]` mappato da `PausedState[]` — literal #56).
- Slice 1 streaming SSE accumulator (event delta merging già pronto).
- Slice 1.7 identity (per future auth dell'endpoint `aura serve`, oggi local-only).

**Dipendenza Go.**
```go
// go.mod
require github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui/sdks/community/go v0.0.0-20260514093510-e9e910b230b9 // amendment #6+#56: pin = PSEUDO-VERSION literal (commit e9e910b230b9329c905e31ca024b4114dedf7918, 2026-05-14 "interrupt, resume, multimodal"; HEAD del SDK al 2026-06-06). Risolto live da spike 014, sigillato da go.sum. Gotcha CI bootstrap: pinnare PRIMA che il codice importi il modulo richiede un secondo `go get .../pkg/core/events@<pseudo-version>` per i sums transitivi (logrus).
```

**Smoke.**
```bash
./aura serve --agui-port=9080 &      # background

# AG-UI Dojo client (npx) si connette
npx @ag-ui/dojo --backend http://127.0.0.1:9080
# → UI mostra chat, invio "ciao dimmi 2+2"
# → backend stream-a TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT delta token-per-token
# → UI rende "Risposta: 4"

# Test minimo via curl
curl -N -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9080/agent/run \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"threadId":"<conv_uuid>","runId":"<auto>","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"ciao"}]}'
# → SSE stream:
# event: RUN_STARTED
# data: {"threadId":"...","runId":"..."}
# event: TEXT_MESSAGE_START
# data: {"messageId":"msg-1","role":"assistant"}
# event: TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT
# data: {"messageId":"msg-1","delta":"Ciao"}
# ...
# event: RUN_FINISHED
# data: {"threadId":"...","runId":"...","outcome":{"type":"success"}}
```

**Acceptance.**
- [ ] **[8b — DEFERITO, amendment #35]** `aura serve --agui-port=<N>` (default `9080`) avvia HTTP server con endpoint `POST /agent/run` e `GET /threads/<id>/messages`. Lifecycle gestito (start/stop su SIGTERM), graceful drain delle connessioni SSE attive a shutdown. (8b atterra solo con un client HTTP reale + auth; non pre-req di Slice 9.)
- [ ] **Mapping Aura ↔ AG-UI**:
  - `threadId` = `aura.conversations.id` (Slice 1.8). Se thread non esiste in DB → 404. Se esiste ma `identity_id != local` → 403 (future auth).
  - `runId` = generated server-side (UUID v4 prefix `run-`) per ogni `POST /agent/run`. Persisted in `aura.conversation_turns.metadata.run_id` per audit.
  - `messageId` = UUID prefix `msg-`. Mapped 1:1 con `conversation_turns.seq` via metadata jsonb.
  - `toolCallId` = ID dal LLM (es. DeepSeek/OpenRouter `tool_call_id`). Persisted in `conversation_turns.tool_call_id`.
- [ ] **Eventi emessi dal Loop** (post-Slice 8 il Loop ha un `emitter` interface):
  - `RUN_STARTED` all'inizio di `Loop.Turn`.
  - `STEP_STARTED` / `STEP_FINISHED` per ogni iterazione (LLM call + tool dispatch).
  - `TEXT_MESSAGE_START` / `TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT` (delta token-per-token) / `TEXT_MESSAGE_END` per il contenuto assistant.
  - `TOOL_CALL_START` / `TOOL_CALL_ARGS` (delta JSON args) / `TOOL_CALL_END` per ogni tool call emesso dal LLM.
  - `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` (con `content` = preview + footer di `ToolResult`) dopo l'esecuzione.
  - `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` su `GET /threads/<id>/messages` (rehydration UI client).
  - `STATE_SNAPSHOT` opzionale al run start (current state della conv).
  - `STATE_DELTA` con `JSONPatchOperation[]` (RFC 6902) per update incrementali (es. cost USD running sum).
  - `RUN_FINISHED` con `outcome.type ∈ {success, interrupt}` (**#56**: i literal SDK sono questi due — ~~`interrupted`~~ non esiste; ~~`errored`~~ non è un outcome, il failure path è l'evento `RUN_ERROR`). Se `interrupt`, `outcome.interrupts[]` (`[]types.Interrupt{ID, Reason, Message, ToolCallID, ResponseSchema, ExpiresAt}`) mappato da `pending []*PausedState` (Slice 1.5 multi-pause); `ResponseSchema` (JSON Schema) pubblica la shape attesa della risposta — le `ask_user` options diventano schema, `ExpiresAt` disponibile per pause TTL.
  - `RUN_ERROR` per failure non recuperabili (LLM 5xx finale, panic loop, etc.).
- [ ] **REASONING_* events (dual-field, amendment #33)**: se `reasoning_content` (stile DeepSeek-V4 remoto) **OPPURE `reasoning`** (vLLM ha rimosso il campo deprecato `reasoning_content` allineandosi alla guidance OpenAI — sul path local-LLM DGX il reasoning arriva qui) è presente in `usage.*`/`delta.*`, il client wire emette `REASONING_START` / `REASONING_MESSAGE_CONTENT` / `REASONING_END` parallelamente ai TEXT_MESSAGE_* (separate messageId). Accept-both, niente parse semantico, stream byte-per-byte. **Senza il dual-field il path DGX/`local-only` non emette mai reasoning** → la status-line "💭 Reasoning..." di Telegram resta vuota proprio sul deployment max-privacy. Acceptance: fixture SSE golden per entrambi i nomi campo → stessi eventi.
- [ ] **Resume contract (riscritto #56 — protocol-native)**: per riprendere un Loop interrupted, il client invia un nuovo `POST /agent/run` con stesso `threadId` + nuovo `runId` + **`resume: []ResumeEntry{interruptId, status ∈ {resolved, cancelled}, payload}`** (campo first-class di `types.RunAgentInput` dal commit pinnato). ~~`messages` includono i RoleTool answers per gli interrupts precedenti (matching su `tool_call_id`)~~ — superato: il match è `interruptId` → `PausedState` token; il server ricostruisce lo stato Loop via `LoadHistory + ResumeBatch(answers)`. `status=cancelled` = HITL cancel nativo. Il parser/validation di `RunAgentInput` è SDK-provided (unmarshal dual camelCase/snake_case su ogni campo): `internal/agui/types.go` tiene SOLO la validazione semantica Aura (threadId = conversation UUID esistente, messages non vuoto).
- [ ] **Auth dell'endpoint (Out of scope esplicito)**: niente auth in Slice 8 (continuità con Out of scope "Auth dell'endpoint `aura serve`"). Endpoint bind di default a `127.0.0.1:9080` (local-only). Future slice auth aggiunge bearer token + identity FK alle conversations.

> **Amendment #35 (D15 split + reconciliation D00/D13, 2026-06-01) — RATIFY AG-UI + 3 fix.** AG-UI ratificato come transport standard 2026 (CopilotKit Series A 27M$ mag-2026; integrazioni 1st-party Google/Microsoft/AWS/Oracle; SSE copre il 99% dei casi; blast-radius confinato a `internal/agui/` ~440 LOC via translator puro → orphan-risk basso; WebSocket-rejected corretto). Tre aggiustamenti: **(1) Split 8a/8b.** Telegram (Slice 9b) consuma via **fanout in-process, NON via HTTP/SSE** (`agui_subscriber.go`/`fanout.go`) → solo `translator.go`+`fanout.go`+`client.go`+`types.go`+property-test sono sul critical-path = **Slice 8a** (pre-req di Slice 9). L'endpoint HTTP (`server.go`), `aura serve`, la Dojo conformance suite e `aura chat --via-agui` non hanno client in v1 (dashboard SPA out-of-scope) = **Slice 8b**, deferita finché non esiste un client HTTP reale **e** l'auth è progettata. **(2) Cloud-auth/D00 footgun (8b).** Il bind `127.0.0.1` + auth-out-of-scope è corretto su mini-PC/DGX (loopback) ma non copre il target **Hetzner cloud** (D00). `--bind` su indirizzo non-loopback DEVE richiedere auth (futura) e **fail-fast sotto `AURA_PRIVACY_MODE=local-only`** (coerente boot-fail #30/#33). Il check `identity_id != local → 403` è authorization SENZA authentication: non è un controllo di sicurezza finché l'auth non atterra. **(3) Reasoning dual-field** ~~già risolto in Slice 1 (amendment #33)~~ **[CORRECTED #57: claim falsa — Slice 1 è shippata SENZA il parsing reasoning; il data-plane atterra con Phase 12, vedi Amendment #57]**: il renderer mappa REASONING_* da entrambi `reasoning`/`reasoning_content`.

> **▶ Amendment #56 (Phase 12 pre-plan, spike ground-truth 014-016, 2026-06-06) — SDK reality fixes.** La spike session 4 (`.planning/spikes/014…016`, blueprint in `spike-findings-Aura/references/agui-gateway.md`) ha eseguito live pin + enumerazione event-surface + SSE round-trip sul SDK Go ufficiale. Quattro correzioni al testo Slice 8: **(1) Pin #6 = pseudo-version literal** `v0.0.0-20260514093510-e9e910b230b9` — il grep 40-hex originale non può MAI matchare (`require <path> <sha40>` non è sintassi go.mod valida; il repo non ha subdir tags → Go registra solo pseudo-version); gate CI riscritto sul literal, intent di #6 (no floating) pienamente servito via go.sum. **(2) Outcome literals** = `{success, interrupt}`; `errored` non esiste (failure → evento `RUN_ERROR`). **(3) Resume contract protocol-native**: `RunAgentInput.Resume []ResumeEntry` supera il design RoleTool-answers; `types.Interrupt.ResponseSchema` pubblica la shape della risposta, `status=cancelled` dà l'HITL cancel gratis. **(4) Conteggio eventi**: 28 active (+5 `THINKING_*` deprecati; `REASONING_*` canonico serve #33 coi nomi esatti); Aura ne emette 21 — i property-test targetizzano quelli (golden fixtures spike 015). Conferme live: il design iter.Seq2 −100 LOC regge (translator puro ~60 LOC core, ZERO modifiche a `internal/agent` — D-17 verificato); `SSEWriter.WriteEventWithType` produce il framing `event:`+`id:`+`data:` dello smoke (il default SDK è data-only — ri-verificare compat Dojo a 8b se si tiene `event:`); floor loopback 35-40ms coerente con OQ#4; obblighi translator: skip empty deltas + garanzia `messageId`/`toolCallId` (il `Validate()` SDK rigetta entrambi); logrus entra nel binario via `core/events/decoder.go` (tollerato, path decode client-side mai usato dall'emit).

> **▶ Amendment #57 (operator directive + audit codice, 2026-06-06) — Reasoning data-plane: debito Slice 1 pagato in Phase 12.** Audit ground-truth: la claim #35(3) "reasoning dual-field già risolto in Slice 1" è **falsa** — `openai_compat.wireChunk.Delta` decodifica solo `content`+`tool_calls` (i delta `reasoning_content`/`reasoning` sono scartati al wire), `llm.Chunk` e `agent.LLMResponse` non hanno campo reasoning. L'acceptance Slice-8 a riga ~2753 (REASONING_* dual-field) era quindi non-implementabile senza data-plane. Directive operatore: la CoT completa DEVE essere visibile in streaming all'operatore — il reasoning è la fase più lunga del turno DeepSeek-V4 e lo stream la maschera. **Il data-plane atterra con Phase 12** (additivo, nessun refactor): (a) `wireChunk.Delta` accept-both `reasoning` + `reasoning_content` (#33), emit immediato `Chunk{Reasoning}` token-per-token in `parseSSE`; (b) `llm.Chunk.Reasoning string`; (c) `agent.LLMResponse.Reasoning` additivo + case reasoning nel consume loop (`llm_agent.go` ~416) → reasoning chunk Events (D-17 forward-compat regge: shape additiva, nessun import inverso); (d) translator `internal/agui`: lifecycle `REASONING_START`/`REASONING_MESSAGE_START`/`CONTENT*`/`MESSAGE_END`/`REASONING_END` con `messageId` separato (prefix `rsn-`), coalescing identico ai TEXT_MESSAGE_*, interleave PRIMA del primo TEXT_MESSAGE_*; (e) `cmd/aura/chat_render.go`: render live del reasoning (dim/prefisso `💭`) — l'operatore vede la CoT anche sulla superficie CLI odierna. Reasoning resta **stream-only**: NON persistito in `conversation_turns` (niente parse semantico, byte-per-byte, #33 invariato). Il "ZERO modifiche a internal/agent" di #56 resta vero per il seam translator (agui non richiede mai modifiche ad agent); il campo Reasoning è debito Slice-1, non accoppiamento nuovo. Acceptance #33 invariata: fixture SSE golden per ENTRAMBI i nomi campo → stessi eventi.
- [ ] **CORS**: header permissivi per dev (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` se `AURA_AGUI_CORS_PERMISSIVE=1`, default `*` per `127.0.0.1` origin). Future restrittivo via env.
- [ ] **Backpressure**: SSE writer buffered channel (capacity 64); su client lento, channel full → drop con WARN log + `RUN_ERROR` se persistente. Niente blocco del Loop.
- [ ] **[8b — DEFERITO, amendment #35] AG-UI Dojo compliance**: test integrazione che esegue il Dojo conformance suite (50-200 LOC per building block come da spec) contro `aura serve --agui-port`. Validation: text streaming, tool calls, state sync, HITL interrupts.

| `internal/agui/translator.go` | ~180 | `Translate(seq iter.Seq2[*agent.Event, error]) iter.Seq2[events.Event, error]` — mapping deterministico 1:N da `*agent.Event` Slice 0.9 a AG-UI event types (text/tool/state/lifecycle/reasoning, 21 types emessi su 28 attivi — #56). ID generation via `IDGenerator` interface. Funzione pura, no mutable state cross-event eccetto IDs. Sostituisce `Emitter` interface pre-0.9 (drop ~180 LOC plumbing). |
| `internal/agui/fanout.go` | ~80 | Fanout helper per in-process subscribers (Slice 9b Telegram consumer): `Fanout` struct wrappa `iter.Seq2[*agent.Event, error]` e distribuisce a N subscriber channel concurrent. Aggiunto qui per centralizzare la dependency Slice 9b → Slice 8 (era retro-aggiunto in Slice 9, fix audit Round 1). |
| `internal/agui/server.go` **[8b deferito #35]** | ~200 | HTTP server: `POST /agent/run` (SSE response), `GET /threads/<id>/messages` (JSON `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT`). Consume `(*LlmAgent).Run(ctx) iter.Seq2[*Event, error]` direttamente, passa a `Translate`, scrive SSE. Backpressure-bounded (buffered channel cap 64), CORS, graceful shutdown. `--bind` non-loopback richiede auth + fail-fast sotto `local-only` (#35). |
| `internal/agui/types.go` | ~40 (#56, era ~80) | Validazione semantica Aura su `types.RunAgentInput` SDK-provided (threadId = conversation UUID esistente, messages non vuoto policy) + helpers. Il parser JSON + dual-case unmarshal è del SDK — NON riscriverlo. |
| `cmd/aura/main.go` (diff) | ~+80 | Subcommand `aura serve [--agui-port <N>] [--bind <addr>]`. |

Default in-process. **Note refactor-on-touch**: questo file viene rinominato/migrato a `internal/channels/cli/cli.go` in Slice 9a — la diff `+50` qui resta come delta intermedio, Slice 9a refactor la assorbe. |
| `internal/agui/server_test.go` **[8b deferito #35]** | ~180 | Integration test: spawn server, run AG-UI Dojo conformance suite, assert eventi. |
| `internal/agui/translator_test.go` | ~120 | Property-based translator coverage. Fixture sequenza `*agent.Event` → expected AG-UI events. |

**Deferred-tool partition.** Niente tool LLM-facing nuovo. AG-UI è transport infrastructure, non capability LLM-facing.

**Open questions.**
1. **Endpoint path canonico**: la spec ufficiale AG-UI suggerisce `POST /agent/run`? → *Default proposto*: `/agent/run` (allineato con SDK Go community sample). Configurabile via `AURA_AGUI_PATH_RUN` env.
2. **WebSocket transport?** → *Decisione*: Slice 8 implementa solo SSE (default AG-UI). WebSocket è transport opzionale (1 client supportato, non frontend tipico). Atterra in slice futura se serve telecom-grade bidi.
3. **Cost streaming via STATE_DELTA**: `running_cost_usd` aggiornato per turn via JSONPatch delta? → *Default proposto*: SÌ. Pattern: `STATE_DELTA { delta: [{op:"replace", path:"/cost_usd", value:0.0042}] }` dopo ogni LLM call.
4. **CLI default mode**: in-process o via-agui? → *Decisione differita post-benchmark*: Slice 8 implementa entrambe (in-process default), `aura chat --via-agui` flag opzionale. Scegliamo dopo aver misurato latency aggiunto su prompt tipico (~50-150 ms attesi per il roundtrip HTTP loopback).
5. **Telegram bot adapter slot**: dopo Slice 8 o in slice dedicata? → *Slice 9 dedicata*: `internal/channels/telegram/` come AG-UI client process (`aura telegram-bot` subcommand). Riusa eventi standard, traduzione one-way (events → Telegram messages). HITL interrupts → Telegram inline keyboard buttons. Scope separato.

**Mini-PC RAM budget.** AG-UI server è una goroutine HTTP minimal. Buffer 64 event/connection × N connessioni concurrent. Per Aura single-user local: 1-3 connessioni attese (CLI + opzionale Dojo o Telegram bot). RAM negligible (~5-10 MB heap aggiuntivi).

> **▶ Amendment #65 (Web + Telegram perceived-latency UX, 2026-07-03) — chronological per-turn activity timeline.** The user-facing issue is not only provider TTFT/TPS: Aura already streams AG-UI `REASONING_*`, `TOOL_CALL_*`, `TEXT_MESSAGE_*`, and `STATE_DELTA` events, but the surfaces must preserve that event order so users see work happening as it happens. Web cockpit and Telegram therefore share the same UX contract:
> **(1) Web assistant messages preserve arrival order.** The frontend reducer MUST materialize ordered message parts as frames arrive. A stream `REASONING_MESSAGE_* -> TOOL_CALL_* -> REASONING_MESSAGE_* -> TEXT_MESSAGE_*` renders as `reasoning -> tool-call -> reasoning -> text`, not as a single reasoning drawer hoisted before every tool. Multiple reasoning spans with distinct `messageId` values become separate reasoning parts; reused `messageId` values merge into the same part.
> **(2) Tool timing is visible where the wire supplies timestamps.** Tool parts may carry `startedAt` from `TOOL_CALL_START.timestamp` and `finishedAt` from `TOOL_CALL_RESULT/END.timestamp`; existing tool cards render elapsed time without changing the AG-UI protocol.
> **(3) Telegram status pane is a chronological activity pane.** Msg #1 remains the throttled status pane and msg #2 remains the streamed answer, but the pane body shows a `Sequenza`/activity list ordered by first event seen: reasoning span, tool start/result, answer writing. The older category-only rendering (`Strumenti` list plus separate reasoning state) is insufficient because it hides the actual turn timeline.
> **(4) Privacy posture is unchanged.** Raw provider reasoning only surfaces when the existing `AURA_SHOW_REASONING`/channel `ShowReasoning` path allows it. Redacted or unavailable reasoning must render as safe lifecycle/status text, never as a fake chain-of-thought.
> **(5) Acceptance gates.** Add reducer tests for `reasoning -> tool -> reasoning -> text`, reused reasoning `messageId` merge, and late reasoning after text preserving order. Add Telegram status-pane tests/goldens proving ordered reasoning/tool/answer activity while retaining throttle, Telegram 4096 cap, cancel markup lifecycle, cost footer, and no raw-reasoning leak when redacted.
>
> **▶ Amendment #66 (Container readiness, 2026-07-03) — no false-green cockpit health.** The perceived-latency fix is only useful when the appliance reports the cockpit as available after the HTTP surface is actually ready. The Compose `aura` healthcheck MUST query the in-container AG-UI HTTP listener, not merely execute `aura version`. Because `/readyz` includes dependency readiness and is normally protected by the cockpit auth boundary, the auth middleware may expose `GET /readyz` only to same-process loopback probes (`127.0.0.1`/`::1` `RemoteAddr`) for orchestrator healthchecks; unauthenticated host/browser/proxy requests remain gated exactly as before. Acceptance gates: unit tests prove unauthenticated host `/readyz` stays blocked, loopback `/readyz` reaches the handler, and forged auth/identity headers still grant nothing; Compose artifact tests pin the healthcheck to `curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:9080/readyz`; live Docker validation proves the recreated container becomes healthy only after `/readyz` returns 200.
>
> **▶ Amendment #67 (Chat IA hygiene, 2026-07-03) — sidebar starts chats; Settings creates identities.** The chat sidebar primary action MUST be conversation-first, matching the Claude/GPT mental model: a compact compose row labelled `New chat` / `Nuova chat` creates an empty conversation, selects it, routes to `/c/:id`, and closes the mobile drawer. Identity provisioning is no longer a chat-navigation action; it lives in Settings as an explicit identity-management action that opens the existing full-screen onboarding wizard. Desktop and mobile must share this split: the app drawer can navigate to Settings, but must not expose `Create identity` as a global sidebar action. Acceptance gates: unit tests prove the sidebar exposes `New chat` and not `Create identity`, clicking it posts `/api/conversations` before selecting the new thread, Settings exposes `Create identity`, and the Settings action opens the existing wizard; E2E onboarding opens the wizard through Settings on desktop and mobile.
>
> **▶ Amendment #68 (Graph empty-state UX, 2026-07-03) — evidence workspace is never visually empty.** The Graph surface empty result is a productive state, not a blank canvas with one paragraph. When a thread has no linked evidence yet but the graph schema is available, the canvas MUST render an industrial evidence-readiness board: explicit status, live schema counts, a compact topology preview derived only from real schema labels/relationship types, and the primary `Explore this conversation` action. It MUST NOT fabricate nodes, claims, or documents. The existing left filter pane and bottom path strip remain, but the central canvas carries enough visual structure that the workspace feels useful before data arrives. Acceptance gates: jsdom tests prove empty seed renders the readiness board with schema counts and CTA; desktop/mobile Playwright checks prove the graph page is nonblank and the primary action remains visible.
>
> **▶ Amendment #69 (Graph overview data visibility, 2026-07-03) — live Neo4j evidence must render.** The Graph surface MUST NOT appear empty when Neo4j contains drawable evidence relationships. The read path currently supports the older authenticated `User → Conversation → Message → Entity` footprint, but Aura's document indexer also writes `Document → Chunk`, `Chunk → Chunk`, and user preference relationships that may not carry that conversation footprint. For the local single-user graph, the overview and expand queries may include those document/chunk/preference evidence rows when the authenticated Neo4j store contains only the current `User`; multi-user stores remain conversation/user scoped. Acceptance gates: live Cypher evidence shows unscoped `HAS_CHUNK`/`NEXT_CHUNK` rows and scoped overview no longer drops them; Go compiler tests pin the single-user evidence fallback and the multi-user guard; frontend tests still render a productive empty state only when the API truly returns no drawable rows.
>
> **▶ Amendment #70 (Graph filter execution, 2026-07-03) — filter buttons must change the graph.** The left Graph Explorer `Node types` and `Connection types` controls are live controls: selecting or clearing a filter MUST immediately issue a new structured graph query with the updated `labels`/`rel_types` arrays and refresh the canvas/path-strip result. A button that only changes pressed state is a defect. Acceptance gates: jsdom tests prove clicking a label or relationship filter posts `/api/graph/query` with the selected filter; the existing graph E2E remains green on desktop/mobile after the live-query behavior.
>
> **▶ Amendment #71 (Graph learning-evidence visibility, 2026-07-03) — isolated auto-learn examples are evidence.** Aura's auto-learning stores compact `:ToolSelectionExample` / `:ReasoningExample` nodes in Neo4j, while full runtime tool-call telemetry remains application/audit state in Postgres (`aura.tool_invocations`). The graph explorer MUST make that distinction visible: a label filter for an isolated learning-evidence label must render the matching nodes even when they have zero relationships, instead of looking empty. The default relationship overview remains relationship-first and must not fabricate `Tool`/`ToolCall` nodes from Postgres audit rows. Acceptance gates: live Neo4j counts can show saved learning examples with zero relationships; a filtered graph query for `ToolSelectionExample` returns nodes; Go tests pin the isolated-node branch and the single-user guard.
>
> **▶ Amendment #72 (Graph canvas label legibility, 2026-07-03) — dense evidence must not turn into label noise.** The Graph canvas may render many document/chunk/runtime-evidence nodes with long technical IDs, but the visual canvas MUST remain inspectable on desktop and mobile. Low-signal technical captions (UUIDs, chunk IDs, hashes, long path-like identifiers) should be compacted for canvas use, and dense overviews should suppress ambient labels until the operator focuses a node/path. Full captions remain available in the DOM node list and inspector. Acceptance gates: pure renderer tests prove technical captions are shortened and dense graphs hide unfocused labels; Playwright screenshots on desktop/mobile show the graph is nonblank without overlapping ID text; existing graph E2E remains green.
>
> **▶ Amendment #73 (Shell touch-target floor, 2026-07-03) — compact controls must still be reachable.** The cockpit shell must not ask mobile users to hit sub-44px controls. Shared icon buttons, the bottom mode dock, and the runtime telemetry disclosure MUST render at a physical 44px minimum touch target on mobile; compact desktop-only theme/language toggles MUST keep at least a 32px target. Acceptance gates: component tests pin the shared class contracts; a rendered Playwright audit on desktop/mobile shows the shell controls no longer regress below the target floor while preserving no-overflow/no-console-error checks.

> **▶ Amendment #74 (Focused workspace containment, 2026-07-03) — focused content must not cover the mobile dock.** Focused workspaces may contain dense scroll regions, WebGL canvases, document lists, and evidence lists, but they MUST stay inside the shell's middle grid row and never intercept or hide the bottom mode dock. The Graph surface's mobile layout therefore must let the canvas shrink inside the available shell row and keep the evidence list as an internal scroll region; the Documents surface may keep its mobile library header but must still reserve the dock row. Acceptance gates: component/static tests pin the Graph workspace overflow containment, mobile canvas shrink contract, and Documents shell-row CSS; a rendered Playwright audit proves bottom-dock buttons are topmost/clickable on mobile Graph and Documents while no page overflows horizontally.

> **▶ Amendment #75 (Mobile dock label clarity, 2026-07-03) — navigation must not ellipsize.** The mobile bottom mode dock is a primary navigation surface and MUST NOT render clipped labels such as `Govern...` or `Docum...`. Each tab should use a familiar icon plus a short localized visible label that fits at narrow mobile widths, while the button keeps the full localized mode name as its accessible label and tooltip. Acceptance gates: component tests prove compact labels are rendered without `truncate` while `aria-label` remains the full name; rendered Playwright audit checks every visible mobile dock label has `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` and no horizontal overflow.

> **Amendment #76 (Mobile graph row containment, 2026-07-03) - evidence must stay above the runtime dock.** On narrow mobile viewports, the Graph surface must keep its canvas and evidence/path strip inside the shell middle row. The mobile canvas may shrink, but the evidence list MUST remain a real internal scroll region with readable first rows and MUST NOT paint under the runtime footer or bottom mode dock. Acceptance gates: static CSS tests pin the mobile graph flex-basis/min-height contract; rendered Playwright audit at 320px/393px proves Graph has no horizontal overflow, no sub-44px controls, and no visible evidence controls beneath the bottom dock.

> **Amendment #77 (Header-only runtime readiness, 2026-07-03) - no empty runtime rail.** The cockpit shell MUST NOT reserve a permanent right rail or open a drawer only to repeat health rows already summarized by the header readiness chip. Runtime readiness belongs in the header as a compact text+dot status that is visible on desktop and mobile; detailed health diagnostics can remain in standalone tests/routes, but the main shell must give that width back to the active workspace. Acceptance gates: component tests prove the chat shell has no `#runtime-rail`, no runtime drawer trigger, and a visible header readiness status; E2E proves the served shell shows readiness in the header while no right runtime rail is present.

> **▶ Amendment #78 (Phase 37B pre-execution gate — Web Artifact Sidebar "Artefatti" surface + WEBART-05..08 + client-side preview deps + saved-conversation download persistence, 2026-07-08, D-19) — BLOCKING, lands before any 37B code (CLAUDE.md PRD-first; the `git log` ordering is the gate, same pattern as #44/#62/#63/#64).** Phase 37B aggregates the artifacts an agent delivers in a thread into a right-side **"Artefatti"** panel in the web cockpit (parity with Telegram + the Claude UI), built entirely on Phase 37A's `asset_id` + `GET /api/assets/{id}/download` — **no new source of truth, no new backend endpoint**. This amendment records the WEBART-05..08 requirement group, the sidebar surface, the two new web preview deps + the sandboxed-iframe HTML policy, and the saved-conversation download-persistence behavior that the WEBART-01..04 delivery lane (37A) did not cover.
> **(1) Requirement group WEBART-05..08 (REQUIREMENTS.md:69-72, locked — transcribed here as the PRD record).**
> - **WEBART-05** — the web cockpit renders a right-side "Artefatti" panel in the `AppShell` chat shell (`ResizablePanelGroup`) that lists every asset delivered via `aura.artifact` in the active thread (filename, `size_bytes`, `mime_type`, type icon), newest-first, with a graceful empty-state; on mobile/tablet it collapses into a drawer/overlay like the navigation without breaking the layout.
> - **WEBART-06** — each artifact row exposes a download action targeting `GET /api/assets/{id}/download` (identity-scoped, `Content-Disposition: attachment`, per WEBART-03), and a "Scarica tutto" control downloads the thread's assets sequentially (client-side; no server-side zip endpoint unless evidenced); no raw container/host path ever reaches the browser.
> - **WEBART-07** — the panel is a single derived view merging the thread asset list (`GET /api/assets?thread_id=`) with live `aura.artifact` events from `sseAdapter.ts` (no new source of truth); ownership is enforced by `assets.Store.GetForIdentity` — a non-owner request returns 404/403 and no unauthenticated surface is added.
> - **WEBART-08** — non-regression: the inline `local_artifact` display chip keeps rendering and CLI / no-authenticated-identity degrades to today's host-path behavior. Coverage: React unit tests (panel render + download-all) + a Playwright e2e (artifact appears in the panel + download) + web coverage ≥85%.
> **(2) The "Artefatti" sidebar surface.** A **toggleable third right-side `ResizablePanel`** is added to the existing chat-shell `ResizablePanelGroup` in `AppShell.tsx` (surface order `[nav | workspace | artefatti]`), shown/hidden by a header doc-icon toggle, resizable + width-persisted like the left nav rail, **closed by default and auto-opened exactly once** on the first artifact of a thread. Below the `lg` breakpoint it collapses into the existing `web/src/shell/Drawer.tsx` with `side="right"` titled "Artefatti" (portal/backdrop/focus-trap/Esc/scroll-lock, routed through the "one heavy overlay at a time" reducer). The list is a **derived** `useQuery(['assets', threadId])` view over the already-shipped, identity-scoped `GET /api/assets?thread_id=` (ownership via `ListForThread`→`GetForIdentity`, sorted newest-first **client-side** — the server list order stays `created_at ASC` and MUST NOT change, it is load-bearing for the existing user-upload fold). Rows are icon + name + "Categoria · EXT" + a trailing per-row download; the row body opens a **click-to-preview modal** (Radix `Dialog`, ~90vw/90vh). Per-row + "Scarica tutto" downloads use the 37A-proven same-origin `<a href="/api/assets/{id}/download" download>` path. **No new backend endpoint, no new source of truth** — the server stays authoritative; the React Query cache is the derived view, refreshed by an `onArtifact` invalidate (mirroring the shipped `onUsage`/`invalidateRuntimeReads` pattern), which also drives the one-time auto-open.
> **(3) Preview renderer set + two new web deps (lazy-loaded per D-08).** MIME-gated renderers: images (png/jpg/gif/webp) → blob `<img>`; **SVG is EXCLUDED → download-only** (a blob `<img>` of SVG can execute embedded script — the one XSS edge, gated first); PDF → native `<iframe>` on the blob URL (zero dependency, no pdf.js/react-pdf); text family (txt/md/csv/json/log/sh/yaml/xml/etc.) → raw monospace `<pre>` (no rendered markdown, zero injection surface); **HTML → sandboxed `<iframe srcDoc>` (see (4))**; **docx → `docx-preview` (Apache-2.0**, pulls transitive `jszip`) rendered client-side from the fetched `ArrayBuffer` (no public URL, no server); **xlsx → SheetJS Community Edition `xlsx` (Apache-2.0) → `sheet_to_html`**; pptx → download-only card (no good free client-side renderer). **Supply-chain record (T-37B-01): SheetJS `xlsx` MUST be installed from the CDN tarball `https://cdn.sheetjs.com/xlsx-0.20.3/xlsx-0.20.3.tgz`, NOT `npm i xlsx`** — the public-npm copy is frozen at 0.18.5 carrying **CVE-2023-30533** (prototype pollution, HIGH; fixed 0.19.3) + **CVE-2024-22363** (ReDoS; fixed 0.20.2); the CDN ≥0.20.2 (same publisher, current, both CVEs fixed) is the required, patched source. **License correction:** `docx-preview` is **Apache-2.0** (an earlier discussion note said MIT; both are permissive, the record is corrected here per the phase research). Both renderer libs are lazy-import chunks (mirroring the `GraphExplorer`/Governance lazy pattern) so they never enter the main bundle — fetched only when a user opens that file type.
> **(4) HTML sandbox policy (T-37B-02, null origin).** Untrusted HTML renders in `<iframe srcDoc={text} sandbox="allow-scripts">` **with NO `allow-same-origin`** — i.e. a **null origin**: scripts run, but `document.cookie` is empty, `window.parent` is cross-origin, and `fetch('/api/…')` carries no ambient session, so the markup cannot reach our cookies/DOM/session/Garage. The `allow-scripts` + `allow-same-origin` combination is **explicitly forbidden** (together they let sandboxed script remove its own sandbox); `allow-scripts` alone is the approved posture. The frame `src` cannot point at the download URL (its `Content-Disposition: attachment` forces a download, not a render) — the bytes go `fetch()`→`srcDoc`. This works **WITH** 37A's D-10 `attachment` + `octet-stream` + `nosniff` guard, not against it: untrusted bytes render only inside a blob-URL/iframe/DOM element, **never as a top-level document from our origin**.
> **(5) Saved-conversation download persistence (D-14 + D-15).** **D-14** — because the panel's `useQuery` is keyed on `threadId`, opening any saved conversation refetches the server's asset list, so downloads are present with **no reload** (the durable fix, independent of the live message stream where the current inline chip loses its `asset_id`); this is the panel's core value-add. **D-15** — on history load the inline assistant `local_artifact` chip is ALSO rehydrated ("fix on touch") by **splitting `attachAssetsToUserMessages` by `source_kind`**: `source_kind='agent'` deliverables fold onto **assistant** turns (they must not attach to user turns), while user uploads (`web`/`telegram`/`cli`) keep folding onto user turns. (Root cause: send_file's `local_artifact` display is synthesized client-side from the live `aura.artifact` frame and is never persisted in the snapshot → it rehydrates without `asset_id`; the panel/D-14 is the authoritative durable surface, the chip fold is best-effort parity.) The TS `Asset.source_kind` union is widened to include `'agent'`.
> **Scope guard (D-19):** this amendment is docs-only and lands as a standalone PRD-amendment commit **before** any 37B implementation code (the `git log` ordering is the gate). Recorded out-of-scope so the PRD boundary is explicit: the "Condiviso" (shared-link) section + share-arrow → **Phase 37F**; the "Contenuto" conversation-content thumbnail grid; `.pptx` inline rendering; ONLYOFFICE/Nutrient self-hosted/paid Office viewers (the documented upgrade path for a future Office viewer/editor phase); a server-side zip endpoint for "Scarica tutto" (YAGNI); rendered-markdown preview.

> **▶ Amendment #79 (Phase 37C pre-execution gate — Web Voice Lane (Voce Web): speaker + in-place dictation parity via assistant-ui adapter seams + WEBVOICE-01..04 + `POST /api/tts` / `POST /api/stt` / `GET /api/voice/capabilities` + mp3-for-web vs opus-for-Telegram + the net-new `AURA_TTS_MAX_CHARS` knob, 2026-07-09, D-14) — BLOCKING, lands before any 37C code (CLAUDE.md PRD-first "Senza PRD completo non si scrive una riga di codice"; the `git log` ordering is the gate, same pattern as #44/#62/#63/#64/#78).** Phase 37C brings the Telegram voice experience to the web cockpit in two lanes — **(a) voice output**: every assistant message gets a speaker control that synthesizes its text on demand, plus an auto-speak "voice mode"; **(b) voice input**: the Composer Mic becomes in-place editable dictation (a transcript in the input box, NOT a voice-note attachment). Both are **cloud-only via OpenRouter** (`AURA_TTS_MODEL` / `AURA_STT_CLOUD_MODEL`, no local sidecar — the mini-PC RAM constraint) *(⚠ superseded during 37C execution → **local↔cloud selectable, local-default**; the deployment runs healthy local voice sidecars and the host is GPU-capable; operator-ratified 2026-07-09 — see **Amendment #80** below for the delivered design)*, reusing the already-shipped `internal/multimodal` `TTSClient` / `STTClient` verbatim (the handlers are thin wrappers — no ML in Go). The **spine** (research-locked against the exact installed `@assistant-ui/react@0.14.22` / `@assistant-ui/core@0.2.17` source) is that both features are **custom server-backed adapters wired into the existing `useExternalStoreRuntime`**, NOT hand-rolled `<audio>`/`MediaRecorder` plumbing. The web voice surface was undocumented in this PRD; this amendment records the WEBVOICE-01..04 requirement group, the three routes, the two adapter seams, mp3-for-web vs opus-for-Telegram, the ephemeral session-scoped voice-mode toggle, and the `AURA_TTS_MAX_CHARS` knob.
> **(1) Requirement group WEBVOICE-01..04 (REQUIREMENTS.md:78-81, locked — transcribed here as the PRD record).**
> - **WEBVOICE-01** — each assistant message exposes a speaker control that synthesizes its text via a new authenticated `POST /api/tts` (identity-scoped) over `multimodal.TTSClient`, played by an in-page `<audio>`; a "voice mode" preference enables auto-speak (parity with Telegram `ShouldSpeak`). *(Scope note — see (5): for 37C the "voice mode" preference is delivered EPHEMERAL/session-scoped; the persisted per-conversation preference the wording implies is DEFERRED.)*
> - **WEBVOICE-02** — the Composer Mic becomes dictation: record → transcribe via the existing STT pipeline → insert the transcript into the input box (editable before send), instead of attaching a voice note; on failure it falls back to today's attachment behavior.
> - **WEBVOICE-03** — *(superseded — see **Amendment #80**)* selectable **local↔cloud**: TTS/STT default to the local `aura-tts` (Kokoro) / `aura-stt` (faster-whisper) sidecars and switch to OpenRouter when `AURA_TTS_MODEL` / `AURA_STT_CLOUD_MODEL` is set; when NEITHER a local base URL nor a cloud model is configured the UI degrades gracefully (speaker hidden / mic in attachment mode) with no errors. *(Original 37C wording: "cloud-only: TTS/STT run on OpenRouter with no local sidecar" — reconciled during execution, operator-ratified.)*
> - **WEBVOICE-04** — no regression of the audio-attachment path; `RequireAuth` on the TTS endpoint; React unit tests (speaker + dictation) + e2e; web + owned-surface Go coverage ≥85%.
> **(2) Three new authenticated, identity-scoped web voice routes (`internal/agui`, mirroring `registerAssetRoutes` + the SELF-scoped `GET /api/me`).** `RequireAuth` gates all three via the whole-mux wrap in `serve_webui.go` (so WEBVOICE-04's "RequireAuth on the TTS endpoint" is satisfied structurally); the two POSTs additionally carry the cost-bearing `agent.run` capability (`RequireCapability`, the same grant `POST /agent/run` uses) since each consumes OpenRouter budget.
> - **`POST /api/tts`** over `multimodal.TTSClient.Synthesize(ctx, text)` — responds **`audio/mpeg` (mp3)** for universal `HTMLAudioElement` decoding (incl. Safari/iOS). Applies a soft character cap (`AURA_TTS_MAX_CHARS`): beyond the cap it synthesizes the capped prefix and signals truncation to the UI (an `X-Aura-TTS-Truncated` response header / a "message too long to read fully" hint) so a long report never 400s on length and per-character cost stays bounded. Returns **503 when the TTS client is unconfigured**.
> - **`POST /api/stt`** over `multimodal.STTClient.Transcribe` — **transcribe-and-discard**: audio blob in → `{text}` out, and the audio is **NEVER persisted** (no `assets.Asset`, no Garage object, no DB row, no async `AudioProcessor.ProcessAsset` poll) — the smallest, most private, lowest-latency surface. The handler maps the browser `MediaRecorder` container MIME to the STT format hint via the exported `assets.AudioFormat` (the `;codecs=` parameter stripped first — `audio/webm;codecs=opus` / `audio/mp4;codecs=…` otherwise mis-tag to `ogg`). Returns **503 when the STT client is unconfigured**.
> - **`GET /api/voice/capabilities`** — SELF-scoped like `/api/me`, read once by the SPA on load; returns `{tts:bool, stt:bool}`, each flag reflecting whether `AURA_TTS_MODEL` / `AURA_STT_CLOUD_MODEL` is configured. It answers **200 with `{false,false}` even when unconfigured — never 503** (a probe, not a cost-bearing op), so the SPA gates controls without a first-click flash: `!tts` ⇒ hide the speaker control, `!stt` ⇒ the Mic stays in attachment mode.
> - **Composition-root wiring (D-13):** a `SetVoice(tts, stt, maxChars)` setter on the AG-UI `Server` (mirroring `SetSettingsStore`), fed from `config.Config` exactly as `serve_channels.go` assembles the Telegram `MultimodalConfig` (the single OpenRouter key/base URL); clients are constructed **only when the cloud model is set**, so capabilities equal client presence. No new config plumbing beyond `AURA_TTS_MAX_CHARS`.
> **(3) The assistant-ui adapter spine (`web/src/chat/voice/` — the wiring, not bespoke audio plumbing).** Both adapters attach **directly on the `adapters` field** of the existing `useExternalStoreRuntime` call (`adapters:{speech, dictation}`); no `RuntimeAdapterProvider` is needed on this runtime, and passing **`undefined` for an adapter is the native degrade switch** (`thread.capabilities.{speech,dictation}` derive from adapter presence).
> - **`adapters.speech`** — a custom `SpeechSynthesisAdapter` (`speak(text)` → `fetch('/api/tts',{credentials:'same-origin'})` → `blob` → `new Audio(URL.createObjectURL(blob))`), with the blob **cached per message** so re-clicking Speak never re-bills the API (revoke on thread teardown). The speaker control is `ActionBarPrimitive.Speak` / `ActionBarPrimitive.StopSpeaking` dropped into the EXISTING assistant `ActionBarPrimitive.Root` next to Copy/Reload, toggled on the per-message `s.message.speech` state. Only one utterance plays at a time (a second Speak cancels the prior — defined behavior).
> - **`adapters.dictation`** — a custom `DictationAdapter` (`MediaRecorder` → on-stop `POST /api/stt` → transcript). **Transcript insertion is native to the library, via `onSpeech({transcript, isFinal:true})` — NOT `onSpeechEnd`**: the core appends `onSpeech` results into the composer text, whereas `onSpeechEnd` only tears the session down and **its `{transcript}` payload is ignored** (firing only `onSpeechEnd` inserts nothing — the #1 executor landmine, corrected from CONTEXT D-09). The transcript lands in the composer input editable-before-send (WEBVOICE-02's "editable before send" is free). The **attachment-record fallback is KEPT, not deleted**: on dictation error OR when `!stt`, the Mic reverts to today's `Composer.tsx` `MediaRecorder` → `uploads.addFiles([voice-note])` path (no regression — WEBVOICE-04); the Paperclip audio-attachment path stays intact.
> **(4) mp3-for-web vs opus-for-Telegram (D-02, RESEARCH correction).** `multimodal.TTSClient.Synthesize(ctx, text)` has **NO per-call format argument** — the container is fixed at client construction (`TTSConfig.Format`, surfaced by `AudioFormat()`). So mp3-for-web is achieved by constructing a **DEDICATED web `TTSClient` instance with `TTSConfig.Format="mp3"`** (wire content-type `audio/mpeg`, cloud `response_format=mp3`), while **Telegram's opus `TTSClient` is untouched** (opus end-to-end, `sendVoice` native — unregressed). This is a second client instance, not a signature change — the smallest-blast-radius shape. *(CONTEXT D-02's "TTSClient already takes a per-call Format" is imprecise and is corrected here.)*
> **(5) Ephemeral session-scoped voice-mode toggle + the "per-conversation" scope reconciliation (D-06 + Deferred).** The auto-speak "voice mode" is an **ephemeral, session-scoped React toggle** in the chat header that **resets on reload** — NO new persistence. **Scope reconciliation (explicit, so delivered-vs-deferred is unambiguous at the PRD level):** ROADMAP §"Phase 37C" SC#1 and REQUIREMENTS WEBVOICE-01 phrase this as a *"per-conversation voice mode"* preference, but for 37C the delivered scope is **session-scoped** — there is no per-conversation preference store today (Telegram's `VoiceModePref` is, and stays, a `false` stub), and this phase adds none. A **PERSISTED per-conversation voice-mode preference** (a `conversations.voice_mode` column or a per-thread store, wiring `VoiceModePref` for real on both channels) is explicitly **DEFERRED** to a future phase, when such a store lands. The auto-speak trigger mirrors Telegram parity: `ShouldSpeak(voiceMode || turnWasDictated)` — auto-speak a new reply when the toggle is ON **or** the user dictated that turn (`turnWasDictated` tracked client-side, echo-modality parity with Telegram's `inboundWasVoice`); it is a pure client-side boolean OR, no server round-trip.
> **(6) Env knob (net-new).** `AURA_TTS_MAX_CHARS` — the soft input character cap on `POST /api/tts`, **default 4096** (the OpenAI-compatible `/audio/speech` hard input ceiling that OpenRouter proxies — above it the provider returns HTTP 400; the planner may lower it purely for cost but must not exceed it). It is the **only** net-new env var (added to `config.Config` + the env/knob catalog, convention `AURA_<DOMAIN>_<UNIT>`); every other voice field (`AURA_STT_CLOUD_MODEL` / `AURA_STT_LANGUAGE` / `AURA_TTS_MODEL` / `AURA_TTS_VOICE` / `AURA_TTS_FORMAT`) already exists.
> **Scope guard (D-14):** this amendment is docs-only and lands as a standalone PRD-amendment commit **before** any 37C implementation code (the `git log` ordering is the gate; every code plan 37C-02..06 declares `depends_on` this commit). Recorded out-of-scope so the PRD boundary is explicit: **realtime full-duplex "hands-free voice mode"** (assistant-ui's `RealtimeVoiceAdapter` / LiveKit / ElevenLabs Conversational) → a future phase, NOT speaker+dictation parity; **persisted per-conversation voice-mode** → deferred until a per-conversation preference store lands; **browser Web Speech API adapters** as an offline/keyless fallback (the lib's `WebSpeech*` impls) → deliberately rejected now for clean degrade over inconsistent 2026 browser quality; **server-side TTS caching/prefetch** and **streaming TTS playback** → YAGNI until cost/latency proves the char cap too blunt.

> **▶ Amendment #80 (Phase 37C execution-time supersession — web voice is local↔cloud SELECTABLE, local-default; supersedes Amendment #79's cloud-only D-12 wiring, operator-ratified 2026-07-09 "Aura can be local and cloud").** During 37C execution the terminal E2E gate (37C-06) surfaced that the cloud-only composition root (D-12: `buildWebTTSClient` / `buildWebSTTClient` returned `nil` unless `AURA_TTS_MODEL` / `AURA_STT_CLOUD_MODEL` were set) reported `GET /api/voice/capabilities` `{false,false}` and degraded the whole web voice lane **off** in the actual deployment — which ships healthy local `aura-tts` (Kokoro) + `aura-stt` (faster-whisper) sidecars (`TTS_BASE_URL` / `STT_BASE_URL`), on a GPU-capable host (the "mini-PC RAM constraint" rationale in #79/D-12 no longer holds). The operator directive **"Aura can be local and cloud"** ratifies aligning the web lane with the rest of `internal/multimodal` (and the Telegram voice path), whose clients already select local-vs-cloud by presence (config comments: `AURA_TTS_MODEL` empty ⇒ local Kokoro; `AURA_STT_CLOUD_MODEL` empty ⇒ local faster-whisper).
> **Delivered design.** `buildWebTTSClient` / `buildWebSTTClient` are **selectable**: each defaults to its LOCAL sidecar (`LocalBaseURL=cfg.TTSBaseURL` / `cfg.STTBaseURL`; the web TTS keeps its `Format="mp3"` override, distinct from Telegram's opus) and switches to OpenRouter only when its cloud model is set; a client is `nil` ONLY when NEITHER a local base URL NOR a cloud model is configured. `GET /api/voice/capabilities` now reflects the presence of whichever route (local or cloud) is wired — `{true,true}` in this deployment. `POST /api/tts` / `POST /api/stt` still answer **503** when their client is `nil`. Everything else in Amendment #79 is unchanged: the ephemeral session-scoped toggle, transcribe-and-discard STT, `AURA_TTS_MAX_CHARS`, mp3-for-web vs opus-for-Telegram, and the assistant-ui adapter spine (#79 (2)–(6)). **WEBVOICE-03** is reconciled to match (REQUIREMENTS.md updated).
> **Proven live (37C-06 terminal gate).** `voice.spec.ts` 8/8 green against the rebuilt container (real local Kokoro `audio/mpeg` on the speaker + fake-media dictation → editable transcript → send + `{false,false}` degrade, no console errors); web vitest **92.46%** stmts + Stryker **≥70% killed** on both adapters (speechAdapter 86.6% / dictationAdapter 78.5%); Go owned-surface **85.4%** on the full `db_integration neo4j_integration` matrix; `-race` clean; `internal/webui/dist` rebuilt. This amendment is the PRD-first reconciliation of a design change made during execution — it lands **after** the code (the change was surfaced by the live gate, not planned) and is recorded here so the truth-source is consistent.

> **▶ Amendment #81 (Phase 37D pre-execution gate — Composer Skill & Command Picker (Picker Skill/Comandi): a `/`-triggered inline skill+command menu in the web Composer + WEBSKILL-01..03 + the new `RequireAuth`-only `GET /api/composer/skills` + the `aura.skill` run-request envelope field + Mechanism-A server-side pinned-skill application + the identity-scoped→global-snapshot reconciliation, 2026-07-09, D-11) — BLOCKING, lands before any 37D code (CLAUDE.md PRD-first "Senza PRD completo non si scrive una riga di codice"; the `git log` ordering is the gate, same pattern as #44/#62/#63/#64/#78/#79).** Phase 37D brings Aura's skills out of the admin-only Governance board and into the Composer as an inline picker: typing `/` at the start of an empty composer opens a keyboard-filterable menu of the skills any authenticated identity can invoke, plus the quick-command actions add-files/new-chat/clear (parity with Claude's own composer picker). The picked skill is **pinned to the turn** and applied deterministically server-side. 37D is built **almost entirely from reuse** — one lean new backend GET, one new frontend menu/pill, and a one-field extension to the *already-existing* `aura` run-request envelope: **no new library, no new database table, no new agent tool, and no new skills source of truth.** The composer skill-picker surface, the `GET /api/composer/skills` endpoint, and the `aura.skill` field were undocumented in this PRD; this amendment records the WEBSKILL-01..03 requirement group, the endpoint, the wire path, Mechanism A, and — critically — reconciles the "identity-scoped / via the governance skills API" phrasing with the GLOBAL active-skills snapshot behind plain `RequireAuth` that Aura actually delivers.
> **(1) Requirement group WEBSKILL-01..03 (REQUIREMENTS.md:87-89, locked — transcribed here as the PRD record).**
> - **WEBSKILL-01** — typing "/" at the start of a Composer line opens a keyboard-filterable menu listing the skills available to the authenticated identity (via the governance skills API, identity-scoped) with ↑/↓/Enter/Esc and a per-row description. *(Scope reconciliation — see (4): the "identity-scoped / via the governance skills API" wording is delivered as an authentication-scoped GLOBAL active-skills snapshot served from a NEW `RequireAuth`-only `GET /api/composer/skills` — NOT the `governance.read`-gated board route; PERSISTED per-identity skill scoping is DEFERRED.)*
> - **WEBSKILL-02** — selecting an entry injects the skill into the turn per the existing runtime contract; no new source of truth for skills (reuses the governance API). *(Scope reconciliation — see (3)/(4): "reuses the governance API / existing runtime contract" is delivered as reuse of the SAME `loader.List()` active-skills snapshot the governance board and the runtime `skill action=use` read — one source of truth — carried on the existing `aura` envelope and applied via Mechanism A, with NO new agent tool and NO new skills store.)*
> - **WEBSKILL-03** — accessible (ARIA combobox/listbox), preserves Composer paste/drop/Enter-to-send, degrades to a no-op when the skills API is empty/unreachable; unit + e2e; coverage ≥85%.
> **(2) The new authenticated read route `GET /api/composer/skills` (`RequireAuth`-only, explicitly NOT `governance.read`).** The endpoint mounts behind the whole-mux `RequireAuth` wrap (exactly like `imageProxyRoute` / `graphSchemaRoute` and the SELF-scoped `GET /api/me` / `GET /api/voice/capabilities`), **NOT** behind the `governance.read` capability. Reusing `GET /api/governance/skills` or copying its `RequireCapability(governanceReadCapability)` mount is the exact trap D-03 exists to avoid: that admin-scoped gate returns **403** to an ordinary identity without the governance grant, leaving the picker empty/broken for precisely its target audience (non-admin identities). The handler returns `{skills: [{name, description, type}, ...]}` projected from the active-skills loader snapshot — a lean sibling of the governance board's `activeSkillRows` projection, consuming the SAME `SkillsBoardProvider.ActiveSkills()` / `loader.List()` seam, mounted on a different, ungated route (so the listed set equals the invocable set — "no new source of truth"). It answers **200 with an empty list (never 403)** so the client degrades to a no-op (WEBSKILL-03) when no skills are active, and 503 when the provider is unavailable (the client also treats that as empty). It is registered as a specific `GET /api/composer/skills` method+path sibling (Go 1.22 precedence) — never a bare `/api/` subtree — so it does not shadow `/api/integrations/` or the SPA fallback; to respect the 600-LOC cap on `serve_webui.go` the mount lands in a small `serve_webui_composer.go` (mirroring `serve_webui_voice.go` / `serve_webui_musr.go`).
> **(3) The D-01 pinned-skill wire path (`aura.skill` envelope + Mechanism A, zero runner change).** The pinned skill rides the **existing** `aura` run-request envelope. Today `streamRun` POSTs `/agent/run` with `{ aura: { attachment_ids } }`; 37D folds a `skill` field into the SAME object (`{ aura: { attachment_ids?, skill? } }`, symmetric with `attachment_ids` — one field each side), the server decodes `req.Aura.Skill`, and applies it via **Mechanism A**: it resolves the skill body from the loader and prepends the exact `useAuthorityFrame` string ("Follow these skill instructions for the current task:") + body that the `skill action=use` tool already emits, onto the **model-visible** user message through the existing `TurnWithModelUserMessage` context-prepend seam. The user's raw text stays the persisted/visible turn; the model deterministically receives the authority-framed skill first (byte-identical to what `action=use` produces, framed server-side). This reuses the existing runtime contract with **NO new agent tool, NO new skills store (satisfying WEBSKILL-02's "no new source of truth"), and NO runner change** — the `TurnWithModelUserMessage` seam already exists for attachment/doc-catalog context injection.
