An **unknown or empty pinned name is a no-op** (the name is only ever a loader key resolved via `loader.Get`, never a filesystem path — the loader's `SanitizeName` grammar + symlink-strip + body-cap + injection-blocklist scan already guard it; no client-supplied path is ever accepted). **Mechanism B** — a forced first `skill` tool call rendering a visible tool card in the transcript — is the **REJECTED** alternative: it matches D-01's literal "first tool action" wording but would require a NEW runner seam to force a first tool call (none exists today), a larger blast radius for no functional gain (the effect is byte-identical to Mechanism A).
> **(4) The D-04 reconciliation — "identity-scoped" is delivered as a GLOBAL active-skills snapshot behind `RequireAuth`; per-identity scoping DEFERRED.** WEBSKILL-01/02 phrase the list as "identity-scoped / via the governance skills API", but for 37D the **delivered** scope is authentication-scoped (`RequireAuth`) over a **GLOBAL** active-skills snapshot — there is no per-identity skill scoping in Aura. Evidence (the D-04 gate, resolved decisively — five converging lines): (a) the skills `Loader` is process-global and mutex-guarded with **no identity/MUSR/principal field**; (b) the governance board's `ActiveSkills()` is literally `loader.List()` over the fixed global roots `skillLoaderRoots(cfg)`; (c) the LIVE agent-run skill tool (`newSkillTool`) resolves `skill action=use` against those **same** global roots — so the picker's list and the runtime's invocable set are guaranteed identical; (d) the per-identity rooting primitive `NewSkillToolForIdentity` is **DORMANT — zero production callers** (defined + unit-tested + referenced only in Phase-36 planning docs; its execution/tool-assembly wiring is itself a deferred later plan); (e) **no skill-grant/scope/binding table exists in any migration** (0001-0035 — the only skill table is `skill_audit`). Consequently the picker reads the SAME source of truth as the board and the runtime (so "no new source of truth" holds), and a **PERSISTED per-identity skill scoping/grant capability is explicitly DEFERRED** to a future phase — introducing it (wiring the dormant `NewSkillToolForIdentity` + a grants store/migration) is out of 37D scope and would be scope creep.
> **(5) The D-02/D-06 UI surface — `/`-triggered ARIA combobox + removable pill + pure-client quick actions.** The `/` menu opens **only when `/` is the first character of an empty composer** (a `/` typed mid-text is literal); the filter query is the text after the leading `/`. It renders **above** the input as a W3C-APG **ARIA combobox + listbox** (the textarea keeps DOM focus with `aria-expanded` / `aria-controls` / `aria-activedescendant` pointing at the highlighted option — focus does NOT move into the list — with `↑`/`↓`/`Enter`/`Esc` + typeahead and a JS-scroll of the active option into view), listing skills grouped by category plus the quick-command actions. The selected skill shows as a **removable pill above the input** (mirroring the existing attachment-chip pattern), which the user can remove before sending; on send the turn carries the pinned skill (3). The quick-command actions are **pure client UI with NO agent round-trip**: `add-files` reuses the existing Paperclip file-picker (`fileInputRef.click()`), `new-chat` reuses the existing `startNewConversation`, and `clear` resets the composer input + pinned pill + pending attachments (it does NOT delete the conversation — that would be a server mutation behind a confirm dialog). The picker composes the Composer's existing `onChange`/`onKeyDown`/`onPaste` handlers, intercepting keys only while the menu is open, so paste/drop/Enter-to-send are untouched when the menu is closed; an empty/unreachable skills list means `/` simply never opens a menu (degrade-to-no-op — WEBSKILL-03), preserving normal `/` typing.
> **Scope guard (D-11):** this amendment is docs-only and lands as a standalone PRD-amendment commit **before** any 37D implementation code (the `git log` ordering is the gate; every code plan 37D-02..05 declares `depends_on` this commit). Recorded out-of-scope so the PRD boundary is explicit: a **PERSISTED per-identity skill grants/scoping** capability (wiring the dormant `NewSkillToolForIdentity` + a grants store/migration) → a future phase, DEFERRED (4); a **Cmd+K global command palette** → its own phase; **conversation/artifact sharing** → already Phase 37F; **Mechanism B**'s visible-tool-card / forced-first-tool-call variant → rejected as an unnecessary new runner seam (3).

> **▶ Amendment #82 (Phase 37E pre-execution gate — Composer Reasoning-Effort Selector (Selettore Sforzo-di-Ragionamento): a per-turn `auto·off·low·mid·high·extra·max` "thinking" selector in the web Composer + the WEBMODEL-01..03 effort-only reconciliation + the `aura.effort` run-request field + two-stage (enum+capability) server validation + the dual-backend wire map (OpenRouter `reasoning:{effort}` unchanged / llama.cpp `thinking_budget_tokens`) + per-conversation `conversations.metadata` persistence + the OpenRouter `/models` capability source + `GET /api/composer/reasoning-capabilities` + the net-new `AURA_LLM_PROVIDER` knob, 2026-07-10, D-11) — BLOCKING, lands before any 37E code (CLAUDE.md PRD-first "Senza PRD completo non si scrive una riga di codice"; the `git log` ordering is the gate, same pattern as #44/#62/#63/#64/#78/#79/#81).** Phase 37E brings Claude's reasoning-effort ("thinking") control to the web Composer as a per-turn selector, mapped onto Aura's existing provider-neutral `internal/llm` `ReasoningConfig`. **This is a SCOPE REDUCTION of the chartered WEBMODEL-01/02** (which promised a model selector + effort selector): per the operator's explicit decision the **model dropdown is DROPPED** — model selection stays operator-scoped in the Settings page (`AURA_LLM_MODEL`, already shipped) — and 37E delivers the **reasoning-effort selector only** (D-01). This amendment records the WEBMODEL-01..03 effort-only rewrite, the 7-level capability-gated scale (superseding the stale same-day "no Max" resolution, D-09a VOID), the `aura.effort` wire field, the two-stage server governance, the empirically-settled dual-backend wire map, the persistence target, the capability-auto-detection subsystem, and the one net-new env knob.
> **(1) Requirement group WEBMODEL-01..03 (REQUIREMENTS.md:95-97, effort-only rewrite — transcribed here as the PRD record).**
> - **WEBMODEL-01** — the Composer exposes a reasoning-effort selector whose levels are auto-detected per active model from the set `auto·off·low·mid·high·extra·max` (never a hard-coded or placebo list — D-12/D-13); the choice is persisted per-conversation (`aura.conversations.metadata` jsonb, no migration) and restored on reopen.
> - **WEBMODEL-02** — `/agent/run` accepts an optional symbolic `effort` override; the server maps the symbol → `llm.ReasoningConfig` and validates it in two stages (syntactic enum, then capability against the active model's advertised `supported_efforts`); a non-enum OR non-advertised value → 400; absent/`auto` → today's adaptive default (no regression). Effort takes effect on BOTH OpenRouter AND a local llama.cpp backend (D-08).
> - **WEBMODEL-03** — no bypass of governance: the client sends a symbol, never a raw `ReasoningConfig`/budget/model; the server owns the symbol→config map and the capability gate; every UI level maps to a real spike-validated wire knob (D-12, no placebo — `reasoning.max_tokens` is NOT resurrected as a hard cap). Unit + e2e; coverage ≥85%.
> **(2) The seven-level symbolic scale + the level→wire map for BOTH backends (D-02 revised / D-03 / spikes 095+096 — VOIDs the earlier same-day "no Max" D-09a).** The selector's full vocabulary is the 7 symbols `auto · off · low · mid · high · extra · max` — Aura's adaptive `auto` (retained DEFAULT, zero-regression) plus the Claude-parity graduated scale. These are **symbolic UI values**; the client NEVER sends a raw provider reasoning payload — the server owns the symbol→`llm.ReasoningConfig` map (D-05). ⚠ **The earlier same-day D-09a resolution (which capped the scale at five levels and excluded an unlimited-budget top level) is VOID** and is deleted/superseded across ROADMAP.md + REQUIREMENTS.md + this PRD by the 7-level capability-gated scale (D-02 revised). Level→wire map (empirically frozen — do not re-probe): **auto** → no `reasoning` object (adaptive policy, OpenRouter-only) / no llama.cpp reasoning fields (default thinking ON); **off** → OpenRouter `reasoning:{effort:"none"}` (or `{enabled:false}`) / llama.cpp `chat_template_kwargs:{enable_thinking:false}`; **low** → `effort:"low"` / `thinking_budget_tokens:512`; **mid** → `effort:"medium"` / `thinking_budget_tokens:2048`; **high** → `effort:"high"` / `thinking_budget_tokens:8192`; **extra** → `effort:"xhigh"` (`ReasoningEffortXHigh`, exists) / `thinking_budget_tokens:16384` *(planner-tunable)*; **max** → `effort:"max"` (`ReasoningEffortMax`, NET-NEW const) / `thinking_budget_tokens:-1` (unlimited). `exclude` on the OpenRouter rows stays `boolPtr(!AURA_SHOW_REASONING)` — the selector controls **effort, not visibility** (D-10). The OpenRouter wire SHAPE is unchanged (spike 096: OFF already works; `buildWireReasoning` already serializes `Effort: string(r.Effort)`, so `xhigh`/`max` project once the `max` const exists); the llama.cpp branch is net-new (spike 095: Aura's `reasoning:{effort}` object is a NO-OP on llama-server).
> **(3) The `aura.effort` run-request field + two-stage server validation (D-05/D-12/D-13).** The pinned effort rides the **existing** `aura` run-request envelope (symmetric with 37D's `aura.skill`): `POST /agent/run` `{ aura: { …, effort? } }`; the server decodes `req.Aura.Effort` and runs, after the owner-scope `GetForIdentity` gate, **two stages**: (1) **syntactic** — `parseEffortSymbol` accepts ONLY the 7-symbol enum, anything else → **400**; (2) **capability** — a fixed level must be in the ACTIVE model's advertised `supported_efforts` (else **400**), so the UI can never request a placebo (D-12/D-13). `""`/`auto` → no override → today's adaptive `ApplyAdaptiveReasoning` path, byte-identical (D-04, no regression). A **fixed** level bypasses the adaptive classifier and forces `req.Reasoning` via a new `ApplyFixedReasoning` seam gated on a **generalized** reasoning-target recognizer (OpenRouter **or** llama.cpp, D-08). The client sends a **symbol**, never a `ReasoningConfig` — this is the WEBMODEL-03 no-bypass control.
> **(4) llama.cpp server ops contract (spike 095, MANDATORY for the graduated path).** The llama.cpp `thinking_budget_tokens` path is unlocked ONLY when llama-server runs **WITH `--jinja`** (else `chat_template_kwargs` is ignored) and **WITHOUT `--reasoning-budget`** (else per-request `thinking_budget_tokens` is locked out — llama.cpp discussion #21445). `off` uses `chat_template_kwargs:{enable_thinking:false}`; graduated uses `thinking_budget_tokens:N`. Validated local model: unsloth `gemma-4-E2B-it-qat` UD-Q4_K_XL (spike-095 launch: `-ngl 99 -c 4096 --temp 0 --jinja --reasoning-format auto`). To positively identify a llama.cpp backend at request time (the DGX/vLLM local path also emits `reasoning`), 37E keys on the explicit **`AURA_LLM_PROVIDER=llamacpp`** knob (net-new, (6)), NOT a baseURL heuristic.
> **(5) Per-conversation persistence — `aura.conversations.metadata` jsonb, NO new migration (D-06).** The chosen level is written into the **existing** `metadata jsonb` column of `aura.conversations` (added in migration **0005** `0005_conversations.up.sql`) via a parameterized owner-scoped `jsonb_set` update — so **NO new migration is required and the migration numbering is UNCHANGED** (the truth-source migration ledger in §Persistence is untouched by 37E). On thread open the level hydrates from the same column onto the `Conversation` projection (already SELECTed but dropped in `conversationFromRow` today), restoring the selector (Claude parity); a stored level no longer advertised by the active model clamps back to `auto`. New conversations default to `auto` (zero regression, D-07). A typed column is NOT justified (read once on open, never filtered/sorted).
> **(6) Capability auto-detection + `GET /api/composer/reasoning-capabilities` + the net-new `AURA_LLM_PROVIDER` knob (D-12/D-13).** The selector's available levels are **auto-detected per active model**, never hard-coded, never a placebo. **Cloud source of truth:** `GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models` — each model carries a `reasoning` object with `supported_efforts` (⊂ `{max,xhigh,high,medium,low,none}`), `default_effort`, `default_enabled`, `mandatory` (verified live 2026-07-10). Those tokens map 1:1 onto the UI symbols (none→off … max→max; auto = no override). The fetch is **TTL-cached + warmed at boot, never per-turn**, body-capped, with a defensive allowlist-clamp of unknown tokens; on failure it returns the **safe fallback `{auto, off}`** (`detected:false`) — the feature degrades, never breaks. **Local source:** llama.cpp `GET {baseURL}/props` (best-effort narrowing) plus the explicit `AURA_LLM_PROVIDER=llamacpp` + spike-095 ops contract (which authorizes the full graduated set). The detected set reaches the Composer through a new `RequireAuth`-only **`GET /api/composer/reasoning-capabilities`** (mirroring 37D's `GET /api/composer/skills`; returns `{levels, default, backend, detected}`, never the models list / model id / base URL / API key), wired by setter-injection (`SetReasoningCapabilitySource`) at the composition root; a nil source → safe fallback, never 503. The net-new **`AURA_LLM_PROVIDER`** env (`openrouter|llamacpp`, default `openrouter`) is added to `internal/settings` `AllowedKeys` + the env catalog — it selects the wire branch and the capability source (today `Provider` is settable only via `~/.aura/llm.json`; `applyEnvOverrides` never set it).
> **(7) Honest backend-dependent fidelity caveat (D-09, MANDATORY in plan + UAT).** `supported_efforts` is the model's **advertised** capability (the best available source of truth) — advertised support ≠ guaranteed graduated fidelity. Reliable on EVERY backend = **off vs on vs auto**. True low/mid/high/extra/max gradation is **backend-dependent**: REAL and monotonic on budget-capable local llama.cpp (`thinking_budget_tokens`, spike 095), but on the default OpenRouter **DeepSeek-V4-Flash the graduated labels collapse to on/off** (spike 096: effort labels don't track; `reasoning.max_tokens` is NOT honored as a hard cap — which is why it is NOT resurrected, D-12). The UI may present the advertised levels, but the plan + UAT MUST state that graduated fidelity is guaranteed only where the backend truly supports it — do not sell graduated effort as uniform.
> **Scope guard (D-11):** this amendment is docs-only and lands as a standalone PRD-amendment commit **before** any 37E implementation code (the `git log` ordering is the gate; every code plan 37E-02..07 declares `depends_on` this commit). Recorded out-of-scope so the PRD boundary is explicit: the **Composer model dropdown** → dropped, model selection stays in Settings (D-01); **per-message** effort granularity → 37E locks per-conversation (D-06); a user-facing **numeric reasoning-budget** knob → stays symbolic (server picks the token count per level); resurrecting **`reasoning.max_tokens`** as a hard cap → REJECTED (spike 096 refuted it, D-12); an **in-UI model-specific effort hint** ("this model collapses low→high") → a future nicety (D-09 documents the reality).

> **▶ Amendment #83 (Calm Prism chat refinement pre-execution gate, 2026-07-15) — BLOCKING, lands before any Calm Prism production code.** Aura's existing chat keeps its backend, AG-UI stream, typed-display, artifact, voice, approval-resolution, and composer-effort contracts, while its browser presentation is refined as follows. (1) Workspace Voice/Artifacts controls move from absolute overlay to a reserved normal-flow lane. Assistant roots are `w-full min-w-0`; only plain prose is capped at exactly `48rem`; typed displays, tools, tables, sources, and artifacts remain fluid. Coarse-pointer/touch layouts expose Voice, Artifacts, Edit, Copy, Reload, Speak/Stop, document/audio actions, and both branch arrows at a minimum 44 × 44 CSS px. (2) The existing `aura.chat.reasoning.shown` key and `'1'`/`'0'` encoding remain, but missing, invalid, or unreadable storage now defaults hidden. Readable explicit values stay authoritative across write failures, current-session toggles still work, disclosure IDs are unique, and reasoning uses `aria-expanded` without `aria-pressed`. (3) Tool raw detail preserves the seven-case running/raw/settled/manual state matrix; output remains escaped `<pre>` text and settled duration is locale-aware. (4) Active-thread approvals render after activity and before a visible locked composer. One shared selector controls cards and lock state. `kind="approval"` receives generic approval-risk framing only: the client must not invent skill-install, container, activation, source, hash, preview, or subtype claims and must not render the resume token as a dedicated field. Resolution URLs and `{action, content?}` verb bodies stay unchanged. Intermediate Accept/Decline resolutions do not re-drive; after refetch, the final locally accepted/declined approval triggers exactly one no-message `/agent/run`; Cancel never re-drives. Questions preserve whitespace and overflow safely; confirmation focus/Escape and one-time terminal announcements are required. (5) Empty-thread Research/File/Artifact/Automation starters are client-owned English/Italian copy. They replace and focus the editable composer through AppShell's sole nonce-backed draft event, never submit, and never open the file picker automatically. (6) Usage remains frontend-only: each new/edit/reload/resume run emits an unsettled undefined reset, live updates for that run, and exactly one settlement from its shared `finally`; cancel only aborts and thread changes clear state. Visible telemetry updates live, while a separate non-interactive status region announces only settlement. Mobile starts with labeled Cost/Context plus a visible disclosure cue; desktop remains complete. This amendment supersedes conflicting earlier cockpit presentation language but introduces no dependency, backend field, endpoint, protocol, raw color, or unsafe HTML path.
>
> **Acceptance gates.** Failing-first Vitest coverage pins reasoning storage/IDs, all seven tool states, generic approval framing/token transport, approval order/lock/focus/three-token resume behavior, exact bilingual starters, run-scoped settlement, live-versus-announced telemetry, semantic width/touch hooks, and resource parity. An explicit Playwright `channel: 'chrome'` project collects console, page, request, and same-origin HTTP failures; deterministic 1440 × 1000 and 393 × 852 dark/light states assert bounding-box nonintersection, viewport containment, 44 × 44 coarse targets, and no horizontal overflow. Reference and implementation screenshots are reviewed in the same comparison input, accepted screenshots become `toHaveScreenshot` baselines, the contrast/typecheck/lint/build/file-size gates pass, and the generated `internal/webui/dist` diff is reviewed separately.

> **▶ Amendment #84 (Phase 37F pre-execution gate — Conversation & Artifact Sharing / Export: WEBSHARE-01..04, the three fail-closed share tiers, the redacted snapshot model, the `shared_links`/`share_audit` schema on migration 0040, the D-08 and D-13 amendments, and the OQ#4 internal-vs-public link-format resolution, 2026-07-17) — BLOCKING, lands before any 37F code (CLAUDE.md PRD-first "Senza PRD completo non si scrive una riga di codice"; the `git log` ordering is the gate, same pattern as #44/#62/#63/#64/#78/#79/#81/#82/#83).** Phase 37F lets a conversation owner (1) **export** a thread as a downloadable Markdown/JSON file and (2) mint a **share link** that respects Aura's MUSR identity isolation, across three fail-closed tiers, and builds the "Condiviso" section + share-arrow Phase 37B explicitly deferred here. 37F additionally carries two operator-approved amendments that **contradict this PRD's own prior text** — D-08 (reasoning/thinking traces) and D-13 (the token-lookup mechanism) — so this amendment is not optional documentation-after-the-fact: shipping 37F code against a PRD that still states the old D-08/D-13 text would let a later reviewer "fix" the code back into a privacy regression or a pointless table scan. This amendment records the WEBSHARE-01..04 requirement group, the three tiers, the capability + kill-switch gate, the snapshot/redaction model, the schema, the audit + lifecycle design, a bootstrap-capability fact surfaced at plan time, and — the item the whole plan set depends on — the resolution of RESEARCH's Open Question #4.
> **(1) Requirement group WEBSHARE-01..04 (REQUIREMENTS.md:99-106, locked — transcribed here as the PRD record).**
> - **WEBSHARE-01** — the owner can export a conversation (Markdown/JSON of the thread) downloaded via an identity-scoped endpoint (`GetForIdentity`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`).
> - **WEBSHARE-02** — sharing is either (a) revocable + capability-gated toward Aura identities, or (b) — if public is chosen — an explicitly opt-in expiring opaque token with a warning, never default; the owner can revoke.
> - **WEBSHARE-03** — no host/container path and no other identity's data reach a recipient; the share act is audited.
> - **WEBSHARE-04** — unit + e2e + a cross-identity deny test on the shared link; coverage ≥85%.
> **(2) The three tiers, fail-closed (D-01).** (a) File export is always available — no gate beyond ownership. (b) An **internal-identity revocable link** is the default "Condividi" affordance — bearer-within-auth, no capability required. (c) A **public opt-in expiring opaque token** — never the default, minted only behind an explicit warning. All three derive from the same redacted snapshot (5); only the addressing and the audience differ.
> **(3) The capability name `share.public` (D-02, RESOLVED — net-new, rejecting the `governance.write` fallback).** Public-link minting is gated on a net-new, per-user-grantable, off-by-default, admin-grantable capability `share.public` — the `identity.create` precedent (`serve_webui.go:271-277`: "the name becomes load-bearing for provisioned identities, which never get '*' nor `identity.create` unless the creator explicitly grants it AND holds it"), not the `governance.write` fallback. The RESEARCH-OQ3 reuse precedent does NOT transfer: `0026_local_admin_caps.up.sql:1-3` reused `governance.write` for the D-02/D-03 **model-settings** capability because that action was an admin-scoped duplicate already covered by `governance.write`; public sharing is a per-user, non-admin action, and collapsing it into `governance.write` would mean "to share your own chat publicly you must be a full org admin who can install MCP servers and risky supply-chain skills" — a privilege-escalation smell that contradicts D-02's per-user-grant semantics. A net-new capability name costs **zero schema**: `capability` is a free-text column (`0004_identity.up.sql`), the only gate is the grammar `capNameRe = ^[a-z][a-z0-9._-]{0,63}$` at `internal/identity/store.go:33`, and `share.public` matches it trivially.
> **(4) The org kill-switch `AURA_SHARE_PUBLIC_ENABLED`, default `false` (D-02/A2, RESOLVED).** It is an env knob, deliberately NOT an `aura.settings` row: `internal/settings/settings.go`'s `AllowedKeys` is a static 16-key **model-backend-only** allowlist whose package doc states it exists precisely "so a settings row can never clobber connection/security env" — a share kill-switch IS security env, and putting it in `aura.settings` would contradict that seam's own stated purpose. It is re-checked **inside the share-create handler**, not only at the route mount, because `RequireCapability` returns `next` unchanged when `!deps.SecretConfigured` (`internal/agui/auth.go:282`) — on loopback the capability gate does not exist at all, so a default of `false` re-verified in-handler is what closes that fail-open; without it, loopback dev could mint public links with no gate whatsoever.
> **(5) The snapshot model (D-06/D-07).** A shared conversation is a **static snapshot** frozen at creation, refreshable only via an explicit owner "Update" (re-snapshot, same token). Turns added after sharing never retroactively appear on an existing link. Export (MD + JSON) and the rendered public page all derive from **ONE canonical redacted `Snapshot` model** — a single serializer core plus format adapters — so redaction cannot diverge across surfaces.
> **(6) [AMENDMENT — supersedes prior PRD text] D-08: reasoning/thinking traces are DROPPED from the snapshot, permanently — never persisted, never exported, never present in any share surface.** This is verified three independent ways: `aura.conversation_turns` has no reasoning column (`0005_conversations.up.sql:23-36` — the columns are `content`, `content_sidecar_path`, `tool_call_id`, `tool_calls`, token counters; no `reasoning`/`thinking` field of any kind); `llm.Message` (`client.go:24-30`) has no reasoning field; `llm.Chunk.Reasoning` (`client.go:78-79`) is explicitly documented as "STREAM-ONLY and never folded into accumulated content." `LoadHistory` structurally cannot produce a reasoning trace because none is ever written to a row it reads. The only "reasoning" persisted anywhere is `conversations.metadata.reasoning_effort` — the operator's chosen effort **setting**, not a chain-of-thought trace — and it MUST NOT be confused with or exported as reasoning content. `internal/reasoningtrace` is a separate, operator-only debug JSONL written to disk (`AURA_REASONING_TRACE`) that may carry host paths and raw prompts at `full` verbosity; it is diagnostic tooling, not conversation data, and MUST NOT be read by the share exporter under any circumstance. Rationale: no reference product ships chain-of-thought in a share (Claude keeps tool-call data private; open-webui stores only the chat JSON), and adding reasoning persistence now would put chain-of-thought at rest and then export it — a privacy regression inside a phase whose entire purpose is redaction discipline. This decision is final and permanent, not a placeholder pending a future data source.
> **(7) What the snapshot DOES carry (D-08).** Visible `user` + `assistant` text, agent-produced artifacts (8), and tool-call provenance as **tool NAMES only**, per turn (`ToolCall.Function.Name` survives; `Function.Arguments` never does). The HARD SC3 redaction is non-negotiable and NOT a toggle: raw tool-call arguments, raw tool-call results, and any host/container filesystem path are ALWAYS stripped. Nine verified leak sources feed this rule: `ToolCall.Function.Arguments` (verbatim tool args, e.g. `send_file`'s literal `{"path":"/abs/…"}`); `Message.Content` on `role="tool"` (the raw tool result); the artifact descriptor's `path` field (host **or** container path, `send_file.go` → `Actions.ArtifactDelta map[string]any`, `agent/event.go:72`); `tool_invocations.args_raw`, `.result_preview`, `.result_sidecar_path`, `.error`, and `.meta` (all present on the append-only ledger, `0011_tool_invocations.up.sql`); `Turn.ContentSidecarPath` (a host path on the domain struct); `Conversation.IdentityID` (the owner's internal identifier, no recipient value); and `Message.ToolCallID`/`ToolCall.ID` (needless enumerable correlation IDs). The structural rule is **allowlist projection, never denylist**: the `Snapshot` type has no field able to hold args/results/paths, so the leak becomes a compile error, not a review miss. This is explicitly a **server-side** allowlist, not a reuse of the existing client-side one: 37A's D-13 path strip runs **in the browser** (`web/src/chat/sseAdapter.ts:346-360` — the comment there states "`path` stays a backend/Telegram-only field"), while the backend still ships `path` over the wire in `Actions.ArtifactDelta` (`agent/event.go:72`); a share recipient's browser is not a trust boundary the way an authenticated Aura session's browser implicitly is, so the Go serializer implements its own independent, tested allowlist rather than assuming the frontend already stripped anything.
> **(8) [AMENDMENT — narrows prior PRD text] D-09: delivered artifacts are agent-produced ONLY.** The server mirrors `selectAgentArtifacts` (`web/src/chat/artifacts/useThreadArtifacts.ts:33-37`: `source_kind === 'agent' && status !== 'deleted' && status !== 'canceled'`) at the trust boundary. A user's own upload (`source_kind='web'` — potentially a passport scan, a bank statement, anything the user attached) MUST NEVER enter a share, above all a public one. **Copy, never reference:** the recipient's token addresses `share/{id}/…` blobs only and has no path to `identity/{owner}/asset/…`; the share service never resolves a share's bundled artifact through the identity-scoped `assets.Service` — the industrial precedent for this exact failure mode is open-webui, which shipped a bug granting **write** access to files through a share link before fixing it.
> **(9) [AMENDMENT — supersedes prior PRD text] D-13: hash-indexed equality lookup on the public token, NOT a constant-time table scan.** The lookup is `WHERE token_hash = $1` against a unique partial index (`shared_links_token_hash_idx`), never a full-table scan with a per-row `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`. The literal reading of the superseded text — scan every row and constant-time-compare each — is strictly worse: slower, and no more secure. This is safe because the lookup key is already `SHA-256(token)`: exploiting a timing signal on the indexed-equality probe to recover the plaintext token would require inverting SHA-256, which the index-probe timing signal cannot do. D-13's intent — no plaintext token at rest, a DB/backup leak never exposes a live link, no enumerable IDs — is fully preserved by hash-indexed equality; `crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare` remains the correct tool only where a secret is compared in Go process memory, and this design has no such comparison site. **This is recorded as a decision, in these words, so that a later reviewer reading only the phrase "constant-time" does not "fix" the hash-indexed lookup into a table scan.**
> **(10) Storage (D-12/A1, RESOLVED).** Snapshot content and bundled artifact bytes are token-scoped Garage blobs (reusing 37A's `internal/objectstore`) under a `share/` prefix that is **lexically disjoint** from the existing `identity/` prefix (`AssetKey(identityID, assetID)` → `"identity/"+…`, `types.go:60-62`), keyed on `share_id` + `snapshot_id` — deliberately **NOT** `token_hash`, because the internal tier has no token at all (D-11's `token_hash` is public-only) and D-10 requires internal shares to resolve artifacts through the same snapshot mechanism as public ones. **"Public-readable" in this design means reachable without an identity principal THROUGH Aura — it is explicitly NOT an S3-public bucket ACL.** The Garage bucket stays private in every tier; Aura's own handler streams the bytes, following the 37A D-09 precedent that a download is "never presigned/redirected" (`internal/objectstore/identity_store.go` doc comments; `internal/agui/assets_api.go:34`). An S3-public bucket would leave blobs reachable by anyone who ever saw the URL even **after** revoke or expiry, breaking D-09's and D-15's revoke/expiry guarantees outright — this is why the bucket-private-plus-server-streamed shape is load-bearing, not a style preference.
> **(11) Schema: `aura.shared_links` + `aura.share_audit`, landing together on migration `0040`.** Migrations `0036`–`0039` were shipped by Phase 42 (`llm-conversation-compaction`) on 2026-07-14 — `0036_compaction_checkpoints`, `0037_content_parts`, `0038_compaction_memory`, `0039_compaction_rollout` — one day after this phase's CONTEXT.md was first gathered, which is why any earlier reference to "migration 0036" for `shared_links` is **stale and rejected**; 37F's slot is **`0040`**, verified on disk at plan time (`ls internal/db/migrations/ | tail` shows `0039` as the floor and no `0040*` file). The PRD's own §Persistence "Migration numbering — fonte di verità" block is updated by this same amendment to reserve `0040` for 37F, so a concurrently in-flight phase cannot also claim it. Both tables land in the **same** migration, atomically: a partial apply that created `shared_links` without `share_audit` would let a share be created **unaudited**, which is itself an SC3 violation, so splitting them across two migrations is rejected as unsafe, not merely inconvenient.
> **(12) Audit (D-14).** A dedicated identity-keyed `aura.share_audit` ledger captures **create / update-snapshot / revoke / expire / public-access(open)**. It joins the existing three-leg audit union in `internal/agui/audit_store.go` as a **4th leg** with `source='share'`, and surfaces for free in the existing admin audit UI (`audit_api.go`) — no new admin surface is built. Public-link opens are audited with timestamp + coarse info and **NO recipient PII** (no IP, no user-agent, no identity) — the open event proves the link was used, not who used it.
> **(13) Lifecycle (D-15).** Deleting a conversation revokes and drops all its shares through the existing single conversation-delete entry point, `Runner.DeleteConversationLifecycle` (`internal/runner/runner_delete.go:38`) — share revoke + Garage-blob deletion is inserted as an ordered step **before** step 5, the persistence delete (`:73`), so a deleted conversation never leaves a resolvable share behind. Expiry is enforced **lazily at every resolve** (`WHERE token_hash = $1 AND revoked_at IS NULL AND (expires_at IS NULL OR expires_at > now())`) — this is the fail-closed security gate, correct even if a sweep never runs — **and** independently reclaimed by a `share_expiry_sweep` scheduler kind, which is the **byte-reclamation GC**, not a second security gate; these are not alternatives to each other, they solve different problems (D-09's "revoke/expiry drops the bundled copy" is unmet by lazy enforcement alone, since lazy-only makes a link unreachable but leaves its Garage bytes forever). The FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` from `shared_links.conversation_id` to `aura.conversations` removes the row on a raw delete but **cannot** drop the associated Garage bytes, which is exactly why the `Runner` lifecycle hook is mandatory rather than optional — the FK is the backstop, the hook is the primary mechanism.
> **(14) [NEW — verified at plan time, recorded as a deliberate decision] The bootstrap operator holds the `*` wildcard and therefore auto-holds `share.public`.** `cmd/aura/serve_bootstrap.go:176-180` grants the literal `"*"` capability to the first real bootstrap identity, and `HasCapability` (`internal/db/queries/capability_grants.sql:22`: `WHERE identity_id=$1 AND (capability='*' OR capability=$2)`) passes **any** capability name — including `share.public` — against that wildcard. This is **intended**, on the same rationale as the seeded `local` identity's `*` in migration `0004`: the bootstrap identity is the operator/admin. The contrast that makes D-02's per-user semantics real: **provisioned (onboarding) identities receive only explicit named capabilities**, never `*` (`cmd/aura/serve_onboarding.go:152-165` grants each requested capability individually through `identity.ValidateCapabilityName`, an escalation-validated per-name grant loop — no wildcard path exists there at all). It is also recorded that `retireLegacyLocalIdentityForAuthulaUser` (`cmd/aura/serve_auth.go`) — the Authula cutover's local-identity retirement — migrates `conversations`, `assets`, `telegram_accounts`, `identity_auth_links`, `scheduler_tasks`, and `pending_notifications` onto the new operator identity, but does **NOT** migrate `capability_grants` at all: it deletes the `local` identity row outright, and `capability_grants.identity_id` cascades away with it (`ON DELETE CASCADE`). The test consequence: any capability-gated assertion in this phase's test suite MUST use a provisioned, non-wildcard identity, or the assertion passes vacuously against a `*`-holding identity regardless of whether the capability check actually works.
> **(15) Expiry cap (D-04, RESOLVED under Claude's discretion).** Default public-token expiry is 7 days; the owner may pick 1d/7d/30d/custom up to a hard cap; the cap is the operator-tunable env knob `AURA_SHARE_MAX_EXPIRY_DAYS`, default **90**, so the policy ceiling needs no code change to adjust per deployment.
> **(16) Out of scope**, restated from CONTEXT.md's `<deferred>`: standalone single-artifact share links; single-message share links; explicit per-recipient-identity internal grants + a recipient-picker UI (D-10 ships bearer-within-auth instead); remix/re-import of a shared JSON export; interactive AI-powered shared artifacts requiring live sign-in compute.
> **(17) [RESOLVES RESEARCH OQ#4 — the internal-tier link format; the whole 37F plan set depends on this resolution] Decision: the two tiers are addressed differently, on purpose.** RESEARCH's Open Question #4 asked what an internal link actually *is*, and flagged a real tension: if it is `/api/shares/{id}` keyed on a UUID, D-03's "no enumerable IDs" language reads as arguably weakened even behind auth. This was never resolved before now, and left D-10's internal tier — which D-01 designates the **default** share action — with no route a recipient could actually open. It is resolved here as a stated decision, not left implicit:
> - **Internal = an id-addressed authenticated route.** `GET /api/shares/{id}/data` and `GET /api/shares/{id}/asset/{assetID}`, behind `RequireAuth`, with **no capability and no owner predicate**, audited against the caller's own identity. The human-facing link the owner copies is `/shared/{id}`. This route is explicitly **NOT** a member of the public allowlist.
> - **Public = a hashed opaque token.** `GET /s/{token}/data` and `GET /s/{token}/asset/{id}`, unauthenticated, where the token predicate (hash-indexed equality, item 9) is the entire gate.
>
> Four reasons this is correct, recorded so a reviewer who reads only D-03 does not "fix" the internal UUID into a `/s/`-style token:
> 1. **D-03's "no enumerable IDs" is textually scoped to the public, unauthenticated surface.** Its subject is the rendered read-only page at `/s/{token}` and the XSS/enumeration discipline that new unauthenticated HTML surface must inherit; it was never a statement about a route sitting behind `RequireAuth`.
> 2. **D-10 makes the authenticated surface itself the gate:** "being logged into Aura is the gate, the link is the capability." A `shared_links.id` UUIDv4 carries 122 bits of entropy; an attacker must already hold a valid Aura session to probe one at all, every probe returns an oracle-free 404 whether the id is unknown, revoked, expired, or belongs to the public tier, and every resolve is audited against a first-class caller identity — materially different from the anonymous surface D-03 actually governs.
> 3. **It is the codebase's own established pattern, not a deviation.** Phase 36's D-17 already establishes "identity-keyed audit ledgers + random-unguessable IDs bound to owner" as how Aura addresses authenticated resources; `/api/shares/{id}/data` is that same pattern, not an exception to it.
> 4. **It is structurally SAFER than OQ#4's own suggestion, which is therefore explicitly REJECTED.** OQ#4 proposed giving internal links a hashed token too and unifying resolution through one `ResolveByToken` path. But `isPublicShareRoute` admits **every** `GET /s/...` request as unauthenticated by design; the moment an internal share carries a resolvable token, a single handler bug on the `/s/` lane serves it to an anonymous caller — precisely the failure the SC4 cross-identity deny suite exists to catch. Keeping the internal tier **structurally token-less**, enforced by the `shared_links` table's own `shared_links_tier_shape` CHECK constraint (`tier='internal' AND token_hash IS NULL`), makes anonymous resolution of an internal share **impossible by construction**, not merely prevented by a correct handler — the same CHECK that forbids an internal share from ever carrying a token is what makes the separate id-addressed authenticated route necessary in the first place.
>
> **Consequence for D-11:** this resolution keeps its locked wording — `token_hash` **(public only)** — intact and unamended; no sixth operator-approved amendment is needed, because OQ#4's own alternative is rejected on its own security merits, not merely because it would have required one.
> **Scope guard.** This amendment is docs-only and lands as a standalone PRD-amendment commit **before** any 37F implementation code (the `git log` ordering is the gate; every downstream 37F code plan declares `depends_on` this commit). It records, together with ADR 0039 (sharing vs. identity isolation), every 37F design decision — including the two (D-08, D-13) that contradict this PRD's own prior text and the one (item 14, bootstrap `*`) discovered at plan time — before a single line of `internal/share` is written.

> **▶ Amendment #85 (Governance skill-catalog search performance, operator-approved 2026-07-17) — BLOCKING, lands before implementation.** A live Playwright audit of Governance → Skills → Install skill proved that the cockpit starts one `npx skills find` process for every non-empty keystroke: typing `docx` issued four requests in 243 ms and returned the final result after about 7.3 s. One Aura CLI-backed request cost about 2.5 s, while the current skills.sh JSON search endpoint had a measured median near 0.49 s. The approved design is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-17-skill-catalog-search-performance-design.md`.
>
> **(1) Scope boundary — cockpit only; Amendments #51/#52 stay authoritative for the model path.** The existing privileged `GET /api/governance/skills/catalog?q=` may use a native Go HTTP catalog transport because it is a human-facing cockpit read endpoint. This does NOT restore the deleted model-facing `skill action=catalog`, add an agent tool, or change `find-skills-aura`: model-driven self-extension still uses `npx skills find` on the host terminal. Installation is also unchanged and remains `npx skills add <source> --copy -y` with the existing validation, activation, and audit path.
>
> **(2) Frontend request discipline.** `SkillInstallPanel` trims input, requires at least two characters, debounces for 250 ms, keys TanStack Query on the debounced value, and forwards the query function's `AbortSignal` through `searchSkillCatalog` to the existing abort-capable `getJSON`. Prefix results are hidden while a newer value is debouncing. The panel renders localized accessible loading, empty, disabled, and error states; query retries stay off because the backend owns the controlled fallback.
>
> **(3) Backend direct-primary/fallback contract.** The cockpit search first calls `GET https://skills.sh/api/search?q=<encoded>` with a two-second timeout, `Accept: application/json`, a 1 MiB response cap, non-2xx rejection, and lax decode of `skills[].{source,skillId,installs}`. Unknown fields are ignored, but the top-level `skills` array must be present (an absent/malformed field is schema failure; a present empty array is a valid empty result). It preserves upstream fuzzy order, drops incomplete rows, returns at most 20 hits, and keeps Aura's existing `SkillsCatalogResult` wire shape. Successful direct or fallback results enter a process-local 60-second, 128-entry bounded cache; concurrent same-query misses coalesce with `singleflight`, while an individual cancelled caller may stop waiting without corrupting the shared operation. On timeout/network/status/body/decode failure, Aura falls back once to the existing ANSI-parsed `npx skills find`, with CLI telemetry disabled. If both paths fail, the existing sanitized 502 contract is preserved. `AURA_SKILLS_EXTERNAL_DISCOVERY=false` short-circuits before all cache, HTTP, and CLI work.
>
> **(4) Performance and verification contract.** From the final keystroke, a cold live `docx` result must render within 1.5 s and a repeated cached result within 500 ms. Rapid `docx` typing must emit exactly one catalog request, one-character input emits none, stale requests cannot replace the latest result, and the current top result remains selectable as `anthropics/skills@docx`. Implementation is test-first across the Go catalog client, Installer fallback, API signal propagation, and panel debounce/state behavior. Final acceptance is a live Playwright audit against the rebuilt `http://localhost:9080/` with the ten-point rubric in the design spec; shipping requires 10/10 plus clean relevant Go/frontend tests, typecheck, lint, build, and zero unexpected browser console/page/same-origin HTTP failures.
>
> **(5) Rejected mirror.** `mastra-ai/skills-api` is not adopted: its local snapshot search was fast but its audited snapshot was stale, the package was unpublished, its refresh path adds an operated service, and its production dependency audit was not clean. A mirror remains future scope only if the direct source can no longer meet the measured cockpit SLO.

> **▶ Amendment #86 (Compaction SPIKE resolution — REMOVE the dark Phase 42 durable-compaction engine; L4 archival recall is the anti-rot core, operator-ratified 2026-07-20) — BLOCKING, gates the removal phase (CLAUDE.md PRD-first: the durable-compaction engine was the context strategy this PRD once implied, so deleting it is an architectural deviation that lands only after this amendment — same `git log` gate pattern as #78/#79/#81/#82/#84).** The compaction SPIKE (the hard ordering gate for Slices 1.9 + 2.3) resolved to **REMOVE**. Full analysis + the 2026 industrial landscape survey (Anthropic native `compact-2026-01-12` compaction + `clear_tool_uses` context-editing, mem0 v3, tokenjuice, Letta/MemGPT, neo4j agent-memory) live in `docs/audit/compaction-spike-2026-07-20.md`.
>
> **(1) What is removed and why.** The durable semantic-compaction engine shipped by **Phase 42** (`llm-conversation-compaction`; migrations `0036_compaction_checkpoints` … `0039_compaction_rollout`; the `FinalizeCompaction` CAS chain in `internal/conversations/store_compaction.go`; the `internal/conversations/compaction_eval` rollout evaluator; `compaction_reconstruct`/`rebase`/`manifest`/`claims`/`budget`/`metrics`; the `internal/agui/compaction_memory_api.go` surface; `internal/config/config_compaction.go`; the `internal/memory/compaction_*` policy files) is **dark end-to-end**: `FinalizeCompaction` has **zero non-test callers**, the rollout windows are never populated by telemetry, Preview/Restore act on a never-filled table, the trigger enum values are dead, and the engine already produced one P0 (BUG-6a — the `23505` evaluator crash-storm, Wave 0.1/0.2). It delivered **zero** value while costing a P0; the burden of proof for keeping it is not met.
>
> **(2) It is redundant, not load-bearing.** Aura's shipped, provider-agnostic anti-rot defense is the **amendment #21 five-layer policy** (L0 KV-cache discipline · L1 microcompact tool-result eviction · L2/L2.5 budget-trim + picobot hard buffer · tool-result sidecar · L4 archival retrieval), all wired in `internal/conversations/context.go` `applyContextLadder`. The Phase 42 engine is an **unused optional layer built on top of a complete defense**, not the defense itself. **Amendment #21's five layers are UNCHANGED by this decision** — the removal touches none of L0–L4.
>
> **(3) Verdict.** Slice **1.9** (compaction wiring) = **NO-GO**; Slice **2.3** (compaction UI mount) = **NO-GO**. The engine + its four migrations are deleted in a **dedicated removal phase**: the drop migrations take the next free integer at landing (`ls internal/db/migrations/ | tail -1`, per §Persistence — never deduce); the Wave 0.1 no-observation crash-guard **stays until the delete lands** so the live deployment never bleeds in the interim.
>
> **(4) The replacement — L4 extractive graph memory is the anti-rot core (shipped).** The durable win against context rot is **retrieval of salient long-term facts**, not transcript compaction — and Aura is uniquely positioned for it (Neo4j + the neo4j-agent-memory MCP already in-stack). This is now wired as **L4 archival recall**: the runner's `ArchivalRecaller` seam (`internal/runner/interfaces.go` + `runner_context.go`) injects the owner's long-term entities/preferences/facts into messages[1] via the existing always-block seam, scoped by the identity id (the same value the memory-MCP write path keys on), keyed by the current-turn query for top-K relevance, fail-soft, LONG-TERM ONLY (short-term is already carried by the ladder; reasoning stays with Aura's own learner — no memory-bucket duplication). Gated by **`AURA_CONTEXT_MEMORY_RECALL`** (bool; **binary default off, deployed compose default on**) + **`AURA_CONTEXT_MEMORY_RECALL_MAX_ITEMS`** (int, default 8). Shipped commits `340d6966` (recall) + `9c171a0d` (ADR). Live-proven: a fresh conversation recalled a past-session fact and cited the source entity. **[PLACEMENT SUPERSEDED #93.4]** The provider/MCP seam and fence remain; the query-dependent recall block moves from stable `messages[1]` into the dynamic tail.

**Goal.** Aura passa da CLI-only a multi-channel agnostico, con **Telegram come main user-facing channel** (gli utenti finali non usano CLI). Architettura `internal/channels/<name>/` permette di aggiungere WhatsApp/Discord/Signal futuri come slice incrementali. CLI rimane debug-only per dev. Setup completo via web wizard (paste bot token + scan QR del deep link Telegram), niente codici testuali.

Slice 9 risolve Area #16 (transport agnostico) all'altezza prodotto: Slice 8 ha esposto AG-UI come standard, Slice 9 ne cabla il primo client production-grade (Telegram in-process subscriber).

### Pre-requisiti

- Slice 1 LLM client + ToolResult sidecar (riusato per content > cap)
- Slice 1.5 ask_user + multi-pause FIFO (HITL via inline keyboard)
- Slice 1.7 identities + capability_grants (telegram_accounts FK)
- Slice 1.8 conversation persistence (threadId mapping)
- Risk-Based Governance (sezione cross-cutting, rendering risk_tier in messaggi approval)
- Slice 8a AG-UI translator + fanout channel per in-process subscribers (NON l'HTTP server 8b, deferito — amendment #35)

### Decisioni cumulate (chiusura Punti 1-8 discussione 2026-05-28)

| Punto | Aspetto | Decisione |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Activation trigger | `aura serve` boot di tutti i channel configurati (Telegram main user-facing, env-driven, flag `--no-telegram` per debug). |
| 1 | Setup wizard | Sempre on `http://<bind>:9081/setup?token=<AURA_SETUP_TOKEN>`, one-time token `AURA_SETUP_TOKEN` (random UUIDv4) generato + stampato a stdout primo boot (`aura serve`), gated middleware su tutti i `/setup/*` endpoint. Paste bot token + valida via getMe + mostra QR del deep link `t.me/<bot>?start=<onboarding_token>`. Per amendment #10 — previene unauthorized access se `AURA_SETUP_BIND=0.0.0.0:9081`. |
| 1 | Onboarding flow | User scan QR → Telegram apre → `/start <token>` → bot match in `aura.telegram_setup_pending` → INSERT `aura.telegram_accounts`. No codici testuali, full QR/deep-link. |
| 2 | Rate limit | Adaptive con 429 `retry_after` parse + exponential backoff fino a 30s. |
| 3 | Status pane | Pattern master B (2 msg per turn: status pane edited + content reply). LOC ridotti a ~180 (vs master 563). |
| 3 | Throttle status | `AURA_TELEGRAM_STATUS_THROTTLE_MS=1500` (info di servizio, lento) |
| 3 | Throttle content | `AURA_TELEGRAM_CONTENT_THROTTLE_MS=500` (token streaming, veloce) |
| 3 | Chat rate hard | `AURA_TELEGRAM_CHAT_RATE_LIMIT_MS=1000` (queue drain serializzato per chat_id, sopra il debounce per-pane, rispetta 1/sec Telegram) |
| 3 | Markdown library | Custom ~80 LOC MarkdownV2 escaper in `internal/channels/telegram/mdv2.go` (per amendment #4 — promotes port to default. Rationale: `eekstunt/telegramify-markdown-go` is 4-star supply-chain risk per SUMMARY.md Stack P2; in-tree escaper covers MarkdownV2 reserved-char subset, zero external dep) |
| 4 | Approval UX | Renderer agnostico: legge `ask_user.options`. Assenti → 2 button hardcoded `✅ Approva / ❌ Rifiuta`. Presenti → render exact. Agente decide 2/3/N-way via options. |
| 4 | Reply testuale | Reply quote a un pending = nuovo turn user **parallelo** (multi-pause FIFO Slice 1.5 #4 coda i due). Tappare button = resume del pending originale. |
| 5 | Voice failure | 2 retry exponential (1s/2s), poi bot risponde `❌ Trascrizione non disponibile. Invia testo o riprova.` + reaction 😵 sul voice message. |
| 6 | Document size | Tiered: sync ≤5 MB inline / async background 5-50 MB con `📄 Convertendo nome.pdf...` follow-up / refuse >50 MB. |
| 6 | Convert lifecycle | Bot intermediario: niente INSERT in `conversation_turns` finché conversione ready. A done: 1 sendMessage real + AG-UI user message con contenuto convertito. |
| 7 | Vision model | ~~Gemma 4 multimodal sidecar (`aura-llama-multimodal`, llama.cpp).~~ **[SUPERSEDUTO #59: `aura-ocr-vl` = **GLM-OCR** su llama.cpp CPU (DECISO operatore 2026-06-07; PaddleOCR-VL fallback latency-only). IT OCR 7/7, 0 VRAM. vLLM+Gemma OUT su 4GB.]** |
| 7 | Whisper | ~~**Rimosso** (Gemma 4 audio unifica STT).~~ **[SUPERSEDUTO #59: Whisper TORNA — `aura-stt` = faster-whisper `hwdsl2/whisper-server` large-v3-turbo int8, OGG/Opus diretto, 0.7× realtime CPU. La premessa "Gemma unifica STT" è morta con Gemma OUT.]** |
| 7 | Voice (TTS) | **[NUOVO #59: `aura-tts` = Kokoro-82M via Kokoro-FastAPI, voce `if_sara` (IT femminile, locked on-device), opus=voice note nativo. Aura PARLA. `tts.go`→`sendVoice`.]** |
| 7 | Vision fallback | ~~markitdown OCR se Gemma down.~~ **[SUPERSEDUTO #59: fallback = `minimax/minimax-m3` cloud (OpenRouter) opzionale; markitdown resta SOLO per `documents.go` (doc→md), non per le immagini.]** |
| 8 | Bot commands MVP | 10 commands: `/start /help /whoami /cancel /new /conversations /resume /reset /cost /search` (amendment #8 adds `/cost`; amendment #7 adds `/search`). |
| 8 | Command dispatch | Bot-intercept (no LLM call per commands). `/cancel` chiama direttamente `Loop.Cancel`, `/new` crea conv via Slice 1.8 `Create`, ecc. Solo `/start <token>` ha logica onboarding speciale. |

### Migration 0008 (Slice 9a)

```sql
CREATE TABLE aura.telegram_accounts (
  telegram_user_id bigint PRIMARY KEY,
  identity_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES aura.identities(id),
  username         text,
  first_name       text,
  added_at         timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  last_seen_at     timestamptz
);

CREATE TABLE aura.telegram_setup_pending (
  onboarding_token text PRIMARY KEY,
  identity_id      uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES aura.identities(id),
  generated_by     text,                     -- bot username when generated via /setup
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  expires_at       timestamptz NOT NULL,     -- created_at + 1 hour
  consumed_at      timestamptz NULL
);
CREATE INDEX telegram_setup_pending_active
  ON aura.telegram_setup_pending (expires_at)
  WHERE consumed_at IS NULL;
```

### Sidecar compose.yaml changes (Slice 9c) — **emendato #59 (vLLM/Gemma OUT, 3 sidecar CPU)**

```yaml
# RIMOSSO: aura-whisper (mai shippato) E aura-llama-multimodal (Gemma 4) — #59
# AGGIUNTI: 3 sidecar CPU OpenAI-compat, GPU a 0. Verdetto spike session 6 (020-029).

# Vision/OCR — GLM-OCR (DECISO 2026-06-07; PaddleOCR-VL = fallback latency-only via env override)
aura-ocr-vl:
  image: ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:${OCR_VL_IMAGE_TAG:-server}   # CPU; se GPU, pin cuXY-match-driver MAI latest
  command:
    - -m /models/${OCR_VL_MODEL:-GLM-OCR-Q8_0.gguf}                # GLM-OCR (deciso); PaddleOCR-VL-1.5.gguf = override fallback
    - --mmproj /models/${OCR_VL_MMPROJ:-mmproj-GLM-OCR-Q8_0.gguf}
    - --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8082 --temp 0 -c 8192 --threads 4
  volumes: [aura-models:/models]
  ports: ["127.0.0.1:${OCR_VL_HOST_PORT:-8082}:8082"]
  healthcheck: { test: ["CMD","curl","-f","http://localhost:8082/health"] }

# STT — faster-whisper (ingerisce OGG/Opus diretto)
aura-stt:
  image: hwdsl2/whisper-server:${STT_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
  environment:
    - WHISPER_MODEL=${STT_MODEL:-large-v3-turbo}
    - WHISPER_COMPUTE_TYPE=int8
    - WHISPER_DEVICE=cpu
  volumes: [whisper-data:/var/lib/whisper]
  ports: ["127.0.0.1:${STT_HOST_PORT:-9000}:9000"]

# TTS — Kokoro (voce di Aura: if_sara), opus = voice note Telegram nativo
aura-tts:
  image: ghcr.io/remsky/kokoro-fastapi-cpu:${TTS_IMAGE_TAG:-latest}
  ports: ["127.0.0.1:${TTS_HOST_PORT:-8880}:8880"]
  healthcheck: { test: ["CMD","curl","-f","http://localhost:8880/v1/audio/voices"] }
```

Env propagati al container Aura (#59):
```
MULTIMODAL_BASE_URL=http://aura-ocr-vl:8082/v1     # OCR-VL /v1/chat/completions (riusa il nome)
MULTIMODAL_MODEL=glm-ocr                            # o paddleocr-vl
MULTIMODAL_API_KEY=no-key
STT_BASE_URL=http://aura-stt:9000/v1               # faster-whisper /v1/audio/transcriptions
STT_MODEL=large-v3-turbo
TTS_BASE_URL=http://aura-tts:8880/v1               # Kokoro /v1/audio/speech
TTS_VOICE=if_sara
TTS_FORMAT=opus
# Opzionale vision fallback cloud: OPENROUTER_API_KEY + MULTIMODAL_FALLBACK_MODEL=minimax/minimax-m3
```

### Acceptance

#### 9a (Channel framework + Setup wizard)
- [ ] `Channel` interface in `internal/channels/channel.go`. ~~CLI implementata come `internal/channels/cli/cli.go` (refactor di Slice 1.8 `cmd/aura/chat.go` — file creato in 1.8 dedicato per i sub-command chat, ora migrato a channel abstraction).~~ **[ANNULLATO #58(6): la CLI resta in `cmd/aura` debug-only; Channel interface + registry servono i daemon channel (Telegram + futuri).]**
- [ ] `Registry` orchestration: `StartAll` boot tutti i channel enabled (env `AURA_CHANNEL_<NAME>_ENABLED`, default true); `StopAll` graceful drain.
- [ ] Flag override per debug: `aura serve --no-telegram`, `aura serve --only=cli`.
- [ ] Setup wizard HTTP server bind `127.0.0.1:9081` (override `AURA_SETUP_BIND=0.0.0.0:9081` per setup remote con QR scan).
- [ ] ~~`GET /setup` serve `page.html` embedded.~~ **[DEFERITO #58(5): frontend → prossima milestone; `GET /setup` può ritornare un JSON di cortesia `{status, endpoints}` o 404 — il wizard 9a è API-only.]**
- [ ] **One-time token gate (amendment #10)**: `AURA_SETUP_TOKEN` env var. If unset at boot, `aura serve` generates a random UUIDv4 and prints `AURA_SETUP_TOKEN=<value>` to stdout (single line, parseable). Token persists in memory only (no disk). Middleware `requireSetupToken` on `/setup/*` returns 401 if `?token=` query param or `X-Aura-Setup-Token` header does not match. After successful Telegram onboarding (POST /setup/onboard-link completion event), the token is invalidated and a second navigation returns 401. Acceptance test: 401 without token, 200 with token, 401 after onboarding-complete.
- [ ] `POST /setup/token` body `{token}`: valida via Telegram `getMe`, persiste in secrets store, restart bot goroutine (se già attivo).
- [ ] `POST /setup/onboard-link`: genera UUID onboarding_token, INSERT `telegram_setup_pending` (TTL 1h), ritorna `{deep_link: "https://t.me/<bot_username>?start=<token>", qr_svg: "..."}`.
- [ ] `GET /setup/events` (SSE): emette `{type:"onboarding_completed", telegram_user_id, username}` quando `telegram_setup_pending.consumed_at` viene scritto. **Implementazione: poll DB ogni 2s** (default proposto chiuso per Slice 9a, vedi Open Questions sotto). LISTEN/NOTIFY è ottimizzazione futura, non bloccante.
- [ ] `GET /setup/status`: ritorna `{bot_configured, account_count, last_activity}`.
- [ ] Smoke: setup flow end-to-end senza CLI (paste token → QR → Telegram → completo).
- [ ] Test integrazione `db_integration`: round-trip onboarding token + cleanup expired.

#### 9b (Telegram impl)
- [ ] `internal/channels/telegram/bot.go` implementa `Channel` interface, polling `tele.Bot` via telebot.v4.
- [ ] `agui_subscriber.go` riceve eventi da `agui.Emitter.Subscribe()` (fanout channel, in-process).
- [ ] `renderer.go`: 2 msg per turn (status + content), throttle differenziato + chat queue serializzata + 429 backoff. Markdown via in-tree custom MarkdownV2 escaper `internal/channels/telegram/mdv2.go` (~80 LOC, per amendment #4 — promotes the port to default, eliminates `eekstunt/telegramify-markdown-go` dep). Acceptance: fuzz 10K random Unicode inputs → every output round-trips through Telegram `sendMessage` without `400 Bad Request: can't parse entities` (Pitfall #18 mitigation). Fallback plain text if escaping fails.
- [ ] `hitl.go`: `ask_user.options` → InlineKeyboardMarkup; assenti → ForceReply. Callback handler chiama `Resume(token, answer)`. Reply quote = new turn parallelo (multi-pause FIFO).
- [ ] `commands.go`: 10 commands MVP (incl. `/cost` + `/search`), bot-intercept, no LLM call per dispatching.
- [ ] **`/cost` command (amendment #8)**: returns today's cumulative USD spend (`aura.cost_aggregator.TodayUSD()`) + per-conversation breakdown top 5. Uses `aura chat cost` shared logic in `cmd/aura/cost.go` (~30 LOC, single source). Telegram-side: bot-intercept, no LLM call.
- [ ] **`/search` command (amendments #7+#8 cross-ref)**: bot-intercept calling `internal/conversations/search.Search(ctx, query)` from Slice 1.8.5. Result: top 5 turn excerpts with conversation links.
- [ ] `onboarding.go`: `/start <token>` matcher → consume `telegram_setup_pending` → INSERT `telegram_accounts` + send SSE event a /setup web.
- [ ] `renderer.go` mappa esplicitamente i seguenti AG-UI event types (definiti in Slice 8): `RUN_STARTED` (open status pane), `STEP_STARTED`/`STEP_FINISHED` (status pane update), `TEXT_MESSAGE_START`/`CONTENT`/`END` (content streaming), `TOOL_CALL_START`/`ARGS`/`END`/`RESULT` (status pane tool list con glyph 🟡→✅/❌), `REASONING_START`/`CONTENT`/`END` (status pane "💭 Reasoning..." line, collapsed se troppo lungo), `STATE_DELTA` (running cost USD su status pane footer), `STATE_SNAPSHOT` (no-op nel rendering, solo audit), `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` (no-op, solo HTTP responses), `RUN_FINISHED` (status pane finalize + content reply send), `RUN_ERROR` (status pane shows ❌ + error message).
- [ ] **Microcompact pointer handling**: il renderer riconosce `tool_call_result` content che inizia con `[tool_call_id=X: evicted from context...]` (formato L1 microcompact eviction Slice 1.8b) e lo rende come line "🗄️ Tool result evicted (X bytes archived)" invece di dump del puntatore raw nel Telegram message.
- [ ] Test renderer: golden fixture per ogni event type AG-UI → Telegram message expected. Almeno 1 fixture per type, incluso microcompact pointer case.
- [ ] Test commands: ogni command produce output atteso senza LLM call.
- [ ] **[#58(2)] `tables.go`**: markdown table nel reply → gridded PNG via `sendPhoto` (prosa circostante = MarkdownV2 normale); fallback pre-block se il render fallisce; key-value card solo per 2-col `key|value`. Golden test: fixture tabella 4-col e 6-col → PNG deterministico (dimensioni + grid); live test (tag `telegram_integration`): sendPhoto round-trip con `msg.Photo` non-nil.
- [ ] **[#58(3)] `send_file` tool**: emette evento artifact channel-agnostic; Telegram lo consegna via `sendDocument` (path+filename, MIME auto). Live test: xlsx/pdf round-trip con `msg.Document.{FileName,MIME,FileSize}` esatti (ground truth = response Bot API, MAI getUpdates). Path qualsiasi leggibile; >50 MB → errore UX.
- [ ] **[#58(4)] mdv2.go entity-aware**: l'escaper preserva le entity intenzionali (bold/code/pre); il fuzz 10K (Pitfall #18) resta l'acceptance; in più: fixture con tabella dentro pre-fence → pipe/dash NON escapati dentro il fence.

#### 9c (Multimodal) — **emendato #59**
- [ ] `voice.go`: POST a **`aura-stt` (faster-whisper)** `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, **OGG/Opus diretto** (no ffmpeg pre-step). 2 retry + hard fail messaggio UX + reaction 😵.
- [ ] **[NUOVO #59] `tts.go`**: POST a **`aura-tts` (Kokoro, `if_sara`)** `/v1/audio/speech` `response_format=opus` → `sendVoice`. Trigger `voice_mode` (Slice 10 preferences) o auto su input vocale. Caption ASCII-safe. Live test: `sendVoice` round-trip con `msg.Voice` non-nil (ground truth = response Bot API).
- [ ] `documents.go`: tiered sync/async via markitdown sidecar. ≤5 MB sync, 5-50 MB async background. Output > `AURA_CONVERSATION_TURN_CAP_BYTES` → sidecar. **[#59 invariato]**
- [ ] `photo.go` **vision routing su `AURA_VISION_CLOUD` [#60]**: `false` (default) → POST a **`aura-ocr-vl` (GLM-OCR — DECISO 2026-06-07)**; `true` → image_url al loop LLM primario se `Model.SupportsVision` (es. `minimax/minimax-m3`), altrimenti a `MULTIMODAL_FALLBACK_MODEL` — entrambi OpenRouter, nessun sidecar. Lo switch = solo la variabile `.env`, zero codice. Registry `models.go` marca `SupportsVision` (`minimax/minimax-m3`=true, `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`=false). PaddleOCR-VL via `OCR_VL_MODEL` override solo se latenza critica. Test: `AURA_VISION_CLOUD` false→sidecar mock chiamato, true→cloud chiamato (no sidecar).
- [ ] Test integration `multimodal_integration` build tag: requires i 3 sidecar up. Skipped in CI senza container. Live: voice note IT round-trip (STT) + photo IT OCR (recall) + sendVoice (TTS).

## Slice 10 — User onboarding + `Agent.md` profile (per identity)

> **Amendment #87 (2026-07-21): Agent.md retired — the agent-memory graph is the profile store. SUPERSEDES this whole slice's `Agent.md` mechanism.** Operator decision "no more, no less": (1) **Remove Agent.md** — the static `~/.aura/agents/<id>/Agent.md` profile and its `messages[1]` injection are deleted: drop leg1 of `renderContextBlock`, retire `profileContextProvider` + its injection (`chat_boot.go`), delete `internal/profile/*`, trim the `<profile_context>` prompt block. Recall is governed by the already-shipped **D-03 pull-on-demand** `<memory>` doctrine (`internal/agent/prompt.go`); the agent stores + recalls the profile itself via the memory tools (live-observed, conv `03b9c7c2`). No always-injected profile block, no projection budget, no cache-boundary change, no new env var. The archival-recall injection leg (`AURA_CONTEXT_MEMORY_RECALL`) is unchanged and stays default-off. **[PLACEMENT SUPERSEDED #93.4]** Its provider/MCP behavior remains, but query-dependent recall no longer shares the stable always-block. (2) **Rewrite onboarding** — instead of writing `Agent.md`, a **deterministic Go mapping** of the already-structured interview answers (the per-step interview extraction is the sole LLM work; neither web nor Telegram holds a `Runner`) stores the operator profile (entities, facts, preferences) into Neo4j through the **dedicated agent-memory MCP** via one shared `ProfileMemoryStore` port, using the existing `memory_add_entity`/`memory_add_fact`/`memory_add_preference` tools (a batched `memory_save_profile` fork tool is deferred as an optional optimization only). **Every memory write and the status read MUST set `user_identifier=identityID` (the UUID)** — `callMemoryToolText` does not auto-inject it, and a bare call leaks into the fail-open global scope across tenants in MUSR mode. Raw answers are also `store_message`'d; re-running onboarding is idempotent via the existing exact-text + 0.95 dedup. The **onboarding-complete flag** moves from `Metadata.OnboardingCompleted`/`Skipped` to sentinel Facts (`predicate=onboarding_completed`|`onboarding_skipped`, subject=identityID) read by `/api/onboarding/status` — a UX gate, not a "profile complete" claim (no migration). Two symbols are relocated verbatim BEFORE deleting `internal/profile` (mechanically required, not Agent.md concerns): the D-20/D-21 per-identity path guard → `internal/idroot`, and `Preferences` + the draft renderer → `internal/onboarding`. This reverses the line-189 note ("il profile utente (Agent.md) NON va su Neo4j") and the `messages[1] = Agent.md profile` claims (§L0 table, §Prompt layering). Design + live-behavior evidence + 7-commit plan: `docs/audit/agentmd-supersession-design-2026-07-21.md`. The `Agent.md`-based text below is retained for historical record only.

> **Slice 0.9 amendment**: l'interview state machine in `interview.go` (~180 LOC custom Go) viene rimpiazzata da `LoopAgent[InterviewStepAgent]` (Slice 0.9 built-in). Ogni step = un `InterviewStepAgent` (~40 LOC ciascuno) che genera la prossima domanda LLM-adattiva. Termination via `event.Actions.Escalate=true` emesso da `SummaryConfirmAgent` su "Conferma". `maxIterations=8` cap hard. Saving stimato: **−120 LOC** (no state machine custom, riusa LoopAgent runtime + escalation).

**Goal.** Aura conosce l'utente. Al primo Telegram message post-setup (Slice 9), il bot avvia un **LLM-driven interview free-form** (5-8 domande adattive) e genera un file `Agent.md` per quella identity. Il file viene iniettato come secondo system message nei prompt successivi, dando ad Aura context persistente su nome, lingua, tone, interessi, boundaries.

Pattern derivato da:
- **ChatGPT Custom Instructions** ("what to know about you" + "how to respond")
- **ChatGPT Memory** (estrazione fatti continua, ADD-only, mem0-style)
- **CLAUDE.md** (file markdown leggibile, iniettato come context)
- **AGENTS.md** standard (Linux Foundation, ma adattato a user preferences invece di coding project)

Per-identity (Slice 1.7): multi-user supportato strutturalmente. Filesystem-based per ispezionabilità + git-friendly + edit manuale possibile.

### Pre-requisiti

- Slice 1.5 ask_user (per approval gate degli updates)
- Slice 1.7 identities (per per-identity scoping)
- Slice 1.8 conversation persistence (per memory extraction da turn passati)
- Slice 4 PromptBuilder (per injection cache-friendly come secondo system message)
- Risk-Based Governance (sezione cross-cutting, per gating delle update uncertain)
- Slice 8 AG-UI emitter (per emit STATE_DELTA quando profile cambia)
- Slice 9 Telegram bot (transport principale dell'interview e degli updates)

### Decisioni cumulate (chiusura discussione 2026-05-28)

| Aspetto | Decisione |
|---|---|
| Filename | **`Agent.md`** (custom Aura, non AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md). User-facing, non coding-oriented. |
| Trigger | **Auto al primo Telegram message** post-setup (no esistente `Agent.md` per quella identity). Skip option `[Salta, dopo]` disponibile, `/onboard` command per recovery. |
| Storage | **Filesystem** `~/.aura/agents/<identity_id>/Agent.md`. Git-friendly, editable manualmente, ispezionabile. Plus `preferences.json` (structured) + `metadata.json` (version, timestamps) + `changelog.md` (audit). |
| Interview style | **LLM Q&A free-form**. Bot chiede domande adattive (l'agente decide quale chiedere dopo in base alle risposte precedenti), utente risponde libero, LLM interpreta. |
| Auto-update | **Hybrid**: fatti **certi** (osservati `N≥AURA_PROFILE_CERTAINTY_N` volte consistenti, default 3) → auto-add silenzioso + changelog entry. Fatti **incerti** (1-2 osservazioni, conflicting, nuova categoria) → ask_user approval gate via Risk-Based pipeline (tier RISKY per modifiche preferences). |
| Auto-revert | `/forget <fact>` command rimuove specific fact + changelog REVERT entry. Idempotente. |
| Injection nel prompt | Agent.md content come **secondo system message** (dopo main Aura system prompt). Prefix cache-friendly (Slice 4): cambia raramente, sotto il main system. |

### File layout

```
~/.aura/agents/<identity_id>/
  Agent.md              # personalizzazione utente, markdown leggibile
  preferences.json      # structured: lang, timezone, voice_mode, can_proactive_message,
                        # tone_preference (formale/informale/tecnico), response_length
  metadata.json         # version (schema rev), generated_at, last_updated_at,
                        # onboarding_completed (bool), observation_counts (per-category)
  changelog.md          # append-only log delle modifiche (timestamp, fatto added/removed,
                        # source: onboarding|auto-extract|manual|forget)
```

### Esempio output `Agent.md` (post-onboarding)

```markdown
# Agent profile for Davide (local)

Generated 2026-05-28T14:32Z via onboarding interview.
Last updated 2026-05-28T16:08Z (auto-extract: "lingua=italiano" confirmed).

## About me

- Nome: Davide
- Occupazione: Software engineer, AI/agents
- Fuso orario: Europe/Rome (UTC+1)
- Lingua: italiano (auto-detect inglese se scrivo in EN)

## How I prefer responses

- Tono: informale, diretto
- Niente: "Spero questo aiuti!", "Certo!", preamboli
- Lunghezza: sintetica
- Code blocks: con linguaggio specificato
- Italiano: tu, non lei

## Areas of interest

- Coding agentic (Aura, Claude Code, agent frameworks)
- AI/ML systems design
- Backend Go + databases

## Boundaries

- NON proporre cron irreversibili senza approvazione esplicita
- NON salvare info personali in memoria senza chiedere
- OK proactive notification: news tech daily 09:00, reminder calendar

---
<!-- This file is auto-generated and updated by Aura. Edit freely;
     Aura preserves manual edits and only adds new facts via
     /onboard interview, /edit-profile, or auto-extract Risk-Based gate. -->
```

### Onboarding flow (LLM-driven, Telegram)

```
Trigger: primo Telegram message da nuovo telegram_account post-setup
         AND ~/.aura/agents/<identity_id>/Agent.md non esiste

Bot: 👋 Ciao! Sono Aura. Posso conoscerti meglio prima di iniziare?
     [✅ Sì, 5 minuti] [⏭️ Salta, dopo]

Se "Salta":
  → metadata.json onboarding_completed=false
  → Agent.md vuoto creato con placeholder
  → /onboard command disponibile per rifare interview
  → procedi a normal chat (no profile injection)

Se "Sì":
  → InterviewLoop = LoopAgent[InterviewStepAgent] (Slice 0.9 built-in)
  → maxIterations=8 cap hard, ogni iter = 1 step domanda+risposta
  → 5-8 domande adattive scelte dall'LLM in base alle risposte
  
  Domanda 1 (sempre): "Come ti chiami?"
  Domanda 2 (sempre): "Che lingua preferisci che parli? IT / EN / auto?"
  Domanda 3-6 (LLM-adaptive based on previous answers):
    es. "Qual è la tua occupazione?" → se "developer", chiede "che stack?"
    es. "Hai preferenze sul tono? (formale, informale, tecnico)"
    es. "Aree di interesse principali? (es. coding, news tech, finanza, salute...)"
    es. "C'è qualcosa di importante che dovrei sapere su di te?"
  Domanda 7 (sempre): "Posso scriverti spontaneamente con reminder/news?
                       [✅ Sì] [⏰ Solo reminder] [❌ No]"
  Domanda 8 (sempre, riassunto): bot mostra Agent.md generato:
    "Ecco cosa ho capito:
     [...content...]
     È corretto? Vuoi correzioni o aggiungere qualcosa?
     [✅ Conferma] [✏️ Modifica] [🔄 Rifai]"

  Se "Modifica" → bot chiede free-text "Cosa correggo?" → applica diff
  Se "Conferma" → Agent.md salvato + metadata.onboarding_completed=true
  Se "Rifai" → torna a domanda 1

  → bot risponde: "✅ Perfetto, Davide. Sono pronto. Cosa posso fare per te?"
  → procede a normal chat con Agent.md injected
```

### Auto-update flow (mem0-style hybrid)

Durante ogni turn user, Aura osserva il messaggio e tenta extraction di fatti rilevanti per il profile:

```
LoopTurn observer (post-LLM response):
  facts = extractor.Extract(user_message, agent_response)
    # LLM-driven extraction: returns []FactCandidate
    # FactCandidate{ category, key, value, confidence_0_1, evidence_quote }
  
  for each fact:
    counter = metadata.observation_counts[fact.category][fact.key]
    counter++

    if counter >= AURA_PROFILE_CERTAINTY_N (default 3):
      if fact already in Agent.md:
        # Already known, no action
      else:
        # CERTAIN new fact → auto-add
        Agent.md → append/update relevant section
        changelog.md → append "AUTO_ADD: <fact> (source: <evidence>, count: <N>)"
        metadata.last_updated_at = now()
        # No user prompt, silent
    
    elif counter < AURA_PROFILE_CERTAINTY_N AND fact.confidence > 0.7:
      # UNCERTAIN but high-confidence → approval gate
      compute risk_tier (Slice 5): typically RISKY for new preferences
      if tier == RISKY:
        emit ask_user(
          kind=approval,
          question="Ho notato che: {fact}. Devo salvarlo nel tuo profilo?",
          options=["✅ Sì", "❌ No, ignora", "✏️ Modifica"]
        )
        # User decides; ResumeContext applies update if approved
    
    else:
      # Low confidence or low count: keep tracking, no action
```

`/forget <fact>` command:
- User: `/forget` o `/forget italiano`
- `/forget` senza args: bot mostra lista facts recenti, user seleziona via inline keyboard
- `/forget <text>` con args: fuzzy match nei facts, mostra candidate + conferma
- On confirm: rimuove dal Agent.md + append "FORGET: <fact>" in changelog

### Injection nel prompt (cache-friendly)

```
Prompt structure (Slice 4 PromptBuilder + Slice 10):

System message 1 (stable across turns, all conversations):
  "You are Aura, a personal AI assistant..."
  [main Aura system prompt + tool manifest]

System message 2 (stable across turns, per-identity):
  [Agent.md content for current identity]

User/assistant/tool message history (variable)
```

`messages[0]` byte-identico turn-su-turn (Slice 4 invariant rispettato): main system non cambia.
`messages[1]` (Agent.md) byte-identico finché profile non viene updated. Cache hit drop solo on update (raro).
