### Acceptance

- [ ] `internal/onboarding/interview.go` definisce `InterviewLoop = LoopAgent[InterviewStepAgent]` (Slice 0.9 built-in). `maxIterations=8` cap hard. Skip option gestita pre-spawn. `SummaryConfirmAgent` emette `Event{Actions.Escalate=true}` su "Conferma" → LoopAgent termina naturalmente. No state machine Go custom.
- [ ] `store.go` filesystem atomic write (temp + Rename), per-identity directory `~/.aura/agents/<identity_id>/` (UUID).
- [ ] `injector.go` aggiunge Agent.md come second system message in PromptBuilder. Cache invalidation hash basato su `metadata.last_updated_at`.
- [ ] `extractor.go` LLM-driven fact extraction post-turn. Prompt template strutturato che restituisce JSON `[{category, key, value, confidence, evidence}]`.
- [ ] `updater.go` hybrid auto-update: counter ≥ `AURA_PROFILE_CERTAINTY_N` (default 3) → silent add, altrimenti ask_user via Risk-Based pipeline.
- [ ] `/onboard` command rifa interview (skip already-completed con conferma "vuoi sovrascrivere?").
- [ ] `/edit-profile` apre edit mode (ForceReply per section: about-me, preferences, areas, boundaries).
- [ ] `/forget [fact]` rimuove fact + changelog REVERT entry. Senza args → lista facts paginata.
- [ ] `/profile` mostra Agent.md current con markdown rendering.
- [ ] Trigger auto: primo Telegram message senza Agent.md esistente per identity → start interview.
- [ ] CLI `aura profile show/edit/reset <identity_name>` per debug/admin.
- [ ] Test integration `onboarding_integration` build tag: interview round-trip end-to-end.
- [ ] Test fact extraction: 5 conversation turn esempio → fatti attesi extracted.
- [ ] Test hybrid update: 3 osservazioni consistenti → auto-add. 2 osservazioni + 1 conflicting → ask_user gate.

### File targets cumulativi

(Vedere "Architettura componenti" sopra. Totale ~580 LOC src + ~250 test + 50 LOC migration — saving −120 LOC riapplicato da Slice 0.9 amendment via `LoopAgent[InterviewStepAgent]` vs state machine Go custom.)

### Open questions

1. **AURA_PROFILE_CERTAINTY_N**: 3 è sweet spot? Pre-merge calibrare su corpus di test conversations. Default 3, env override.
2. **Conflicting facts handling**: se osservato 2 volte "lingua=IT" + 1 volta "lingua=EN" → cosa fare? *Default proposto*: keep current (no override automatic), log osservazione conflicting in changelog per analisi. Se 3+ conflict → ask_user explicit.
3. **Schema versioning Agent.md**: come gestire breaking change al template (es. nuova section)? *Default proposto*: `metadata.json.schema_version` int, migration script tra versions in `internal/onboarding/migrations/`.
4. **Privacy / forget compliance**: `/forget --all` per GDPR right-to-delete su single user → cancella `~/.aura/agents/<identity_id>/` + persists deletion log per audit. Out of scope qui, future slice multi-user/auth.

### Mini-PC RAM budget — delta vs pre-Slice 10

Negligibile. Slice 10 è puro filesystem + LLM call extraction (riusa LLM Slice 1). Nessun nuovo sidecar.

> **▶ Amendment #98 (2026-07-29 — P0 Agent Memory tenant-bound authentication; SUPERSEDES the single-user/fail-open assumptions in #61/#87).** The Agent Memory MCP is an internal privileged service and MUST reject every unauthenticated HTTP request before MCP initialization. Aura and the sidecar share the required secret `AURA_AGENT_MEMORY_MCP_AUTH_SECRET` (no default; startup/configuration fails closed when absent). Aura signs a short-lived HS256 delegation JWT for each request with `iss=aura`, `aud=agent-memory`, scope `memory:access`, a maximum 60-second lifetime, and `sub`: service-only operations use `aura-service`, while every tool call uses the already-authorized Aura `identityID`. The sidecar validates signature, issuer, audience, scope, and expiry; on a tool call it rejects the service subject and overwrites any caller-supplied `user_identifier` with the validated `sub`. Therefore payload scope is never an authorization credential, and a forged argument cannot cross tenant boundaries. The shared signer is intentionally a service credential: only the trusted Aura process may delegate an identity.
>
> Authenticated mode exposes the 13 Aura tool capabilities and prompts but registers **no MCP resources**: `memory://entities`, `memory://preferences`, `memory://graph/stats`, and `memory://context/{session_id}` have no authenticated tenant component and Aura has no resource consumer. The deployment MUST set Agent Memory `multi_tenant=true`; missing identity fails closed at both the MCP boundary and memory layer. Existing owned graph data remains readable. Legacy global/unowned data is quarantined from authenticated tenants and is neither claimed nor reassigned implicitly.
>
> **Correction #98.1 (same day, protocol evidence before the remediation code commit): authenticated HTTP is stateless.** FastMCP stateful sessions bind the credential that initialized the session and correctly reject a later request whose credential differs; that is incompatible with a service-subject initialize followed by per-tenant tool tokens, and token rotation would also invalidate a long-lived session. The authenticated sidecar therefore runs Streamable HTTP with `stateless_http=true`: Aura still constructs one transport and performs one initialize for a multi-write operation, but the server emits no `Mcp-Session-Id` and requires no session `DELETE`; every request is independently authenticated. This supersedes #95's transport-level “one MCP session”/one-DELETE assertion only. #95's actual performance invariant survives as one Aura transport + one initialize for the whole submission, with no per-item reconnect or discovery.
>
> Short-term conversation identity is the composite `(user_identifier, session_id)`, protected by a Neo4j composite uniqueness constraint and an atomic tenant-qualified create/lookup. An explicit `conversation_id` MUST resolve under the authenticated owner before a message can be appended. Owner assignment is immutable: a second identity using the same `session_id` receives a distinct conversation, cannot relink the first conversation, and cannot fetch or append through its ID. No destructive data migration or graph wipe is permitted.
>
> **Acceptance / release gate (SEC-001 + SEC-002):** (1) no bearer, invalid signature, wrong issuer/audience/scope, and expired token all fail before a tool executes; (2) a valid identity-A token with a body claiming identity B executes only as A; (3) identities A and B using the same short-term `session_id` can retrieve only their own messages and cannot append by foreign `conversation_id`; (4) tool/list discovery still works for Aura under a service token while resource/list is empty; (5) Python unit/integration tests, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, affected Go tests, and affected race tests pass; (6) a rebuilt live stack proves both adversarial isolation and a real `LlmAgent` tool-search/recall turn, with no mocked model or memory backend. This gate is blocking and must score >9.8/10 before the P0 audit is closed.

> **▶ Amendment #99 (2026-07-29 — P1 Wave 1: source-bound MCP policy, protected context, valid token configuration, and active preference recall).** This amendment closes the first dependency-free group from the industrial Agent Memory/context audit: `MCP-001`, `CTX-001`, `CTX-002`, `CTX-003`, `CTX-005`, `MEM-002`, plus their `TST-001` regression rows. It does not weaken #98 and introduces no feature flag.
>
> **MCP policy is semantic, never a display-name convention (`MCP-001`).** A managed server whose `ManagedServer.Source == SourceRecipeMemory` carries a typed memory bridge policy from `MountManagedServer` through initial bridge construction and reconnect refresh. That policy — not the namespace string — controls identity injection, the hidden model surface, and default/deferred visibility. An alias may change only the model-facing prefix (`mem__*`); it receives exactly the same memory policy as `memory__*`. The shared catalog may contain at most one `SourceRecipeMemory` instance; load, save, import, and runtime validation reject duplicates before any transport is opened. Direct generic `Bridge` tests/callers retain the historical namespace-derived default only when no managed source exists. `bridge.go` is already at the 600-LOC boundary, so the memory-policy map/helpers move to `bridge_memory.go` before new logic lands.
>
> **The exact current user model form is already repaired (`CTX-001`).** `currentRoundModelHistory` mutates by index, not a ranged copy. The existing recording-client regression is the release assertion: the persisted turn remains the visible form, exactly one richer model-only form reaches the LLM, and the visible duplicate does not. No additional production change is required; the passing race-enabled test is closure evidence.
>
> **The unresolved active round is protected (`CTX-002`).** For L2.5, the active round begins at the final real `RoleUser` message and includes every following assistant/tool message. The protected head remains the leading system turn plus the synthetic always block. Only complete historical rounds strictly between the protected head and active round are droppable. The active round is byte-identical after the ladder. If protected head + active round + dynamic tail exceed the hard cap, the ladder returns `ErrContextWindowExceeded`; it never succeeds with an empty body and never emits a rot event for a failed reduction. The previous test that pinned deletion of a sole oversized body is superseded by this contract and becomes an explicit overflow assertion.
>
> **BeforeModel hooks are constrained deltas (`CTX-003`).** Hooks may short-circuit/deny and may adjust only request sampling/reasoning fields (`Temperature`, `MaxTokens`, `Reasoning`). They may not change `Model`, `Messages`, `Tools`, `SessionID`, `ToolsCacheControl`, or `ToolChoice`. `HookManager.BeforeModel` snapshots the request before each hook, validates the protected fields after it returns, and restores the complete pre-hook request on every fail-open fault or invariant violation; fail-closed returns an explicit error. This applies equally to in-process and command hooks, so a malicious hook cannot delete/reorder system, current-user, assistant/tool pairs, or the tool manifest. Rejections use the existing hook outcome metric and reasoning-trace audit event without recording prompt bytes or secrets.
>
> **Token configuration is semantically validated after all overlays (`CTX-005`).** `llm.Config.Validate` runs from both `Load` and `LoadAllowEmptyKey`, and from settings/config mutation validation before persistence. `ContextWindow`, `MaxTokens`, and `MaxOutputTokens` must be positive; `MaxOutputTokens >= MaxTokens`; and `ContextWindow - max(MaxOutputTokens, 20000) - 13000 > 0`. Zero never means unlimited. Every env/file/settings violation names the invalid field and relationship and prevents boot/update. Hand-constructed unit-test configs remain constructible, but every production load path validates.
>
> **Normal preference recall is active-only (`MEM-002`).** Every default embedding and category query, scoped and unscoped, requires `valid_until IS NULL` and no outgoing `SUPERSEDED_BY` edge. `get_preferences_for(as_of=...)` remains the only time-travel surface and keeps its deterministic validity interval behavior. Automatic `memory_get_context` therefore cannot return a superseded preference even when its embedding score is higher than the replacement.
>
> **Gate 1 / Definition of Ready — COMPLETE.** Preconditions: #98 is committed and live-verified; `CTX-001` is independently race-green. Open questions: none. Risk: security/correctness fix, no new model-facing tool and no migration/env/sidecar/RAM delta. File targets: `internal/agent/mcptools/bridge.go` (split below 600 LOC), new `bridge_memory.go`, `mount.go`, `internal/mcp/managed_config.go`, their tests; `internal/conversations/context.go` and boundary/property tests; `internal/agent/hooks.go`, `hooks_command.go`, new invariant tests; `internal/llm/config.go`, settings/config tests; vendored `graph/queries.py` and focused Python tests. Commit template: `fix(<scope>): close <finding IDs> — <reason>` with project co-author trailer.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance / smoke.** (1) a managed memory server mounted as `mem` injects the context identity, hides the same seven host-only tools, keeps the same non-deferred model tools, and a duplicate memory source fails before `OpenServer`; (2) a sole or resumed oversized active round returns `ErrContextWindowExceeded`, while an older round is dropped and the active round remains byte-identical under property-generated histories; (3) malicious hooks that remove, rewrite, reorder, or inflate protected state never reach the recording client under either fail policy, while a sampling-only rewrite succeeds; (4) env, file, and settings values that are zero, negative, under-reserved, or mutually inconsistent fail with actionable errors; (5) a superseded high-score preference is absent from both direct search and exact automatic-recall output while the replacement is present; (6) `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, affected tests and race tests, focused vendored pytest/Ruff, managed-memory live alias E2E, and the existing model-only context test are green. The wave must score >9.8/10 before these P1 rows close.

> **▶ Amendment #100 (2026-07-29 — P1 Wave 2: cancellable MCP lifecycle, profile-bound egress, and one hardened stdio substrate).** This amendment closes `MCP-002`, `MCP-003`, `ARC-001`, and their `TST-001` regression rows. It supersedes the explicit infinite MCP timeout accepted by Phase 22: `AURA_MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC=-1` is invalid, unset/zero remains the bounded 60-second default, and every positive value is a finite deadline. No production MCP operation may wait forever.
>
> **Transport serialization is context-selectable and shutdown-first (`MCP-002`).** Both stdio and Streamable-HTTP clients serialize sessions through one shared lifecycle gate whose acquisition selects among permit, caller cancellation/deadline, and closing state. A waiter rechecks closing after acquiring the permit. `Close` atomically marks the client closing before it waits, cancels the active request, and completes within the five-second close budget; calls arriving after closing receive a typed closed-transport error. Cancelling a sent stdio request poisons and aborts that process/pipe, while HTTP cancellation aborts the request context. Close remains idempotent. Tests must hold a first call, prove a short-deadline second waiter returns on its own deadline, race concurrent close against the first call, and show no process/goroutine leak under `-race`.
>
> **Strict runtime profiles own the complete MCP egress policy (`MCP-003`).** The composition root derives a typed MCP `EgressPolicy` from the already-resolved runtime profile and the managed server's typed source/trust; the strict profiles `single_user_hardened` and `server_production` always enforce it and cannot be weakened by `AURA_MCP_SSRF_ENFORCE`. Non-strict local/dev profiles retain private-sidecar compatibility, but the metadata/link-local barrier remains unconditional. In strict mode a trusted built-in recipe may authorize only its exact configured destination authority (`host:effective-port`), never a hostname-wide private bypass; `remote_http` receives no implicit private allowance. The policy validates the initial URL, every DNS answer, the pinned dial target, and every redirect destination. Metadata, mixed public/private DNS, alternate-port private redirects, and DNS rebinding fail closed; an exact trusted recipe destination remains reachable. Custom `http.Client` injection may be used by tests only and must not bypass redirect validation.
>
> **Knowledge uses the common hardened stdio transport (`ARC-001`).** `knowledge.Client` becomes a narrow Cypher adapter over `mcp.Client`/the common `mcp.Transport`; it owns no second JSON-RPC framing loop, scanner/read buffer, mutex, process wait, or cancellation policy. `mcp-neo4j-cypher` is launched with non-secret argv (`--transport stdio` only where needed) and receives `NEO4J_URL`, `NEO4J_USERNAME`, `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, and `NEO4J_DATABASE` through the generic client's explicit filtered child environment. The password must be absent from `exec.Cmd.Args`, diagnostics, and stderr; the common bounded-frame, context-cancellable permit, process-group kill, and bounded-close behavior applies unchanged. Cypher query and params remain structurally separate and the public `Read`/`Write` result contract remains compatible.
>
> **Gate 2 / Definition of Ready — COMPLETE.** Upstream `mcp-neo4j-cypher==0.6.0` was inspected before this amendment and its `process_config` natively consumes all four `NEO4J_*` environment variables, including `NEO4J_PASSWORD`, when their CLI flags are absent. No wrapper, shell launcher, new dependency, migration, feature flag, or extra sidecar is required. File targets: `internal/mcp/client.go` plus a small lifecycle helper, `http_client.go`, `transport.go`, `ssrf.go`, `transport_ssrf.go`, composition-root/mount wiring and focused tests; then `internal/knowledge/client.go` and its tests. Each finding lands in its own implementation commit after this PRD-only commit.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance / smoke.** (1) blocked stdio and HTTP waiters honor a short context deadline while another request owns the session; concurrent close cancels the owner and returns within budget, repeatably under race/leak checks; `AURA_MCP_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC=-1` fails at mount before tool registration; (2) both strict profiles enforce identical initial/DNS/dial/redirect policy, exact built-in private sidecars pass, remote/private and redirect/rebind adversaries fail, and permissive dev still cannot reach metadata; (3) a fake `mcp-neo4j-cypher` proves the password is absent from argv and present only in the explicit child env, oversized frames/cancellation/close use the common behavior, and live Neo4j read/write still decode to the existing row shape; (4) `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, affected tests and race tests, plus a live real-agent memory recall on the strict runtime profile are green. The wave must score >9.8/10 before these P1 rows close.

> **▶ Amendment #101 (2026-07-29 — P1 Wave 3: atomic memory outcomes, deterministic concurrency, and verified erasure).** This amendment closes `MEM-001`, `MCP-004`, `CON-001`, `PRIV-001`, and their `TST-001` regression rows. It introduces no feature flag and permits no destructive repair of existing graph data. Existing ambiguous duplicates are reported for operator review; new writes converge through database-enforced keys.
>
> **One public mutation has one Neo4j transaction (`MEM-001`).** Entity, preference, fact, short-term message, correction, supersession, and onboarding-profile writes must commit their node, owner edge, temporal/version metadata, required relationship edges, and corpus epoch in one `session.execute_write` unit. The graph client exposes a bounded transaction callback/batch primitive instead of making callers sequence independent autocommit calls. `memory_store_profile` is a host-only atomic MCP operation used by onboarding for all preferences, facts, and its completion sentinel; it is never model-visible. Embedding/extraction may run before the transaction, but a failure may not leave a graph write. Post-commit enrichment remains derived, explicitly non-authoritative work. A transaction error rolls back completely; a lost response after commit is an indeterminate operation, never an asserted success.
>
> **Canonical active keys, serialized message sequence, and optimistic correction (`CON-001`).** New owner-scoped facts, preferences, and entities carry a SHA-256 canonical key built from a versioned kind tag, authenticated owner, normalized semantic fields, and deduplication scope. Neo4j uniqueness constraints back those keys; legacy rows may keep a null key until a deterministic matching write adopts one. Concurrent identical writes `MERGE` one canonical active record and owner edge. Supersession retires the old active key in the same transaction before the replacement becomes active. Corrections carry `expected_version`; a stale value returns a typed conflict and changes nothing. Each conversation owns a monotonic `next_sequence`: the message transaction locks/increments it, stores `Message.sequence`, and links only sequence `n-1 -> n`; reads order by sequence with a stable legacy fallback. No concurrent append may create multiple `FIRST_MESSAGE` edges or a branched tail.
>
> **MCP transport success is not domain success (`MCP-004`).** Agent Memory raises FastMCP `ToolError` with a bounded JSON outcome envelope for `rejected`, `partial`, and `error`; successful tool content remains compatible. The common Go MCP client returns a typed `ToolCallError` for `isError=true`. The bridge propagates that error through `tool.Execute` (the agent loop still renders a model-visible error observation) and never converts it into a successful `ToolResult`. A deterministic pre-effect rejection transitions the operation registry to a new terminal `rejected` state and is replayed as a rejection, never as success. Partial outcomes, transport loss, cancellation after send, and any uncertain post-effect failure transition to `indeterminate`. Only an explicit domain-success result may call `CompleteOperation`; onboarding stamps completion only after the atomic profile tool succeeds.
>
> **Every required data plane acknowledges erasure before identity deletion (`PRIV-001`).** Production composition wires an owner-scoped Postgres conversation purger and an Agent Memory graph purger in addition to the existing adaptive, object-store, filesystem, identity, and Authula legs. The conversation adapter deletes all owned conversations/turns and verifies zero remain. The graph adapter executes one owner-scoped transaction that deletes private conversations/messages, facts, preferences, traces/steps, direct ownership edges and the user anchor; entities reachable by another owner are preserved, while owner-private entities are deleted. It then performs an owner-reachability verification query. Successful postconditions are durable saga-step acknowledgements. When identity deletion is configured, missing required conversation or graph purgers is a hard preflight error before any purge step; the identity row cannot be removed until both acknowledgements are journaled. Every adapter and the saga remain idempotent across crash/retry.
>
> **Gate 3 / Definition of Ready — COMPLETE.** The current graph schema, sidecar mutation paths, Go bridge/registry, deprovision saga, Postgres conversation store, and production composition root were inspected before this amendment. The chosen path reuses Neo4j transactions, the existing saga journal, the common MCP transport, and the existing idempotency registry. It adds the next append-only Postgres migration for `rejected`, Neo4j constraints through the existing schema manager, and focused adapters/tests; it adds no store, daemon, wrapper process, secret, or operator-facing configuration. Each finding lands in its own implementation commit after this PRD-only commit.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance / smoke.** (1) fault injection at every semantic sub-step and retry leaves either the complete mutation or zero graph state, and onboarding exposes no sentinel/profile subset; (2) 100 barrier-synchronized identical writes yield one active canonical memory, concurrent messages produce one deterministic sequence with one head/tail, and stale-version corrections return conflict without mutation; (3) semantic rejection, partial, server error, transport loss, bridge execution, registry retry, onboarding, and metrics fixtures prove that no domain failure is cached or rendered as success; (4) a two-owner live graph fixture plus owned Postgres conversations is purged with shared entities preserved, crash/retry converges, and identity deletion is impossible before both verified receipts; (5) focused Python/Go tests, vendored Ruff, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, affected race tests, and a rebuilt strict-profile real-agent write/recall/correction turn are green. The wave must score >9.8/10 before these P1 rows close.

> **▶ Amendment #102 (2026-07-29 — clean-slate Neo4j reset and one native 1024-dimensional embedding contract).** The operator explicitly authorizes a one-time destructive reset of the complete live Neo4j application database because no legacy graph state is to be retained. This supersedes Amendment #101 only where it prohibited destructive repair of existing graph data; every atomicity, concurrency, privacy, and failure-semantics requirement in #101 remains binding. The reset is scoped to Neo4j: it must not delete Postgres data, object-store data, filesystem artifacts, source files, repository state, or unrelated Docker volumes.
>
> **Clean slate means empty graph and rebuilt application schema.** Before reset, all graph-writing services are stopped. The reset deletes every Neo4j node and relationship and drops every user-created constraint and index; Neo4j system databases and unavoidable token-lookup indexes remain. No backup, compatibility path, legacy re-embedding, or data backfill is required. The append-only knowledge migration ledger is graph data and is intentionally removed, so migrations replay from the beginning against the empty database. Agent Memory then recreates its constraints and indexes from its schema manager. The operation must be convergent: interruption followed by the same reset/rebuild sequence still produces the same empty, valid schema.
>
> **1024 is the sole active embedding width.** `AURA_EMBED_DIMENSIONS`, Compose defaults, the Go knowledge default, immutable Cypher DDL, Agent Memory defaults/CLI, tests, examples, and operator documentation all declare `1024`. The live embedding endpoint must return exactly 1024 values. All application vector indexes — knowledge, adaptive-memory, and Agent Memory — must be created at 1024 dimensions with cosine similarity. Normal startup remains fail-closed on a populated schema whose managed vector width differs; the destructive action is authorized only for this explicit clean-slate maintenance event and is not an automatic mismatch repair policy.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance / smoke.** (1) a pre-reset read proves the target graph contains application state, then post-reset `MATCH (n) RETURN count(n)` and `MATCH ()-[r]->() RETURN count(r)` both return zero before schema bootstrap; (2) post-bootstrap every user schema element belongs to the checked-in knowledge migrations or Agent Memory manifest, and every vector index reports `vector.dimensions = 1024`; (3) the real embedding endpoint returns a 1024-value vector; (4) a new authenticated Agent Memory write stores only 1024-value embeddings and is recalled semantically; (5) a real Aura agent performs a fresh write/recall turn through the rebuilt MCP service with no seeded legacy data; (6) focused Python/Go tests, Ruff, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, affected race tests, coverage and mutation gates are green, with final real-scenario score >9.8/10. The PRD-only commit for this amendment must precede runtime edits and the live reset.

> **▶ Amendment #103 (2026-07-30 — direct-production tool correction and industrial release gate).** A production tool is not accepted because its package test passes, its transport returns HTTP/MCP success, or Cockpit renders a settled card. Aura must provide a non-LLM direct execution path over the same resolved registry and live dependencies used by chat/serve, and every release audit must distinguish live success, guard-only rejection, environment-blocked, partial, and failure. A capability counts as live success only when its domain postcondition is observed. Guard-only and environment-blocked calls remain explicit non-passes. This amendment ratifies the 58-tool direct audit in `docs/audit/direct-production-tool-audit-2026-07-30.md` and closes its P1/P2 defects without adding a model-facing tool, database migration, sidecar, secret, or feature flag.
>
> **Contract and failure honesty.** The official Memory relationship command maps its positional `from/type/to` values to the mounted tool schema's `source_name`/`relationship_type`/`target_name` fields. The common MCP decoder treats a top-level structured domain outcome with `success:false` as a typed tool-call error even when a non-conforming sidecar emits `isError:false`; ordinary data fields such as `resolved:false` are not failures. A missing required `swarm_spawn` execution context returns a Go/tool error, never a successful `ToolResult` containing an error sentence. These rules extend #101 `MCP-004` across every mounted MCP source while preserving valid protocol success content.
>
> **One production-equivalent direct runner and doctor.** `aura toolpipe` composes the resolved production registry through the same MCP-aware composition root as chat/serve, with a live Postgres-backed task store, operator identity context, conditional `document_index`, and owned cleanup of MCP transports and database resources. It may bypass the model but may not replace stores with nil, omit default-on managed recipes, or claim context-bound capabilities succeeded. `aura doctor` probes the same resolved default-on + managed + environment-overridden MCP set that runtime mounting consumes; it may not report “no HTTP MCP servers configured” while those servers are mounted. Direct-run output remains machine-readable and reports unknown, typed error, model-visible rejection, and success as distinct states.
>
> **CLI and latency behavior.** `aura docs search <query> [--document-id id] [--limit n]` accepts the documented trailing options without appending them to query text and rejects unknown/missing option values. Exact repeated document retrieval and mounted Memory search receive explicit warm-path SLOs: p95 at or below 2 seconds over at least 20 calls after one warm-up, with zero wrong/empty exact-match results. Cold dependency initialization is reported separately and must remain at or below 5 seconds p95. A document job with unavailable embeddings is `degraded` or failed, never an unqualified `complete`; semantic quality is not accepted until the live corpus has non-zero correctly-sized embeddings.
>
> **Gate 1 / Definition of Ready — COMPLETE.** Root causes and file seams were reproduced against the deployed appliance before this amendment. File targets are `cmd/aura/memory.go`, `internal/mcp/client.go`/`tool_methods.go`, `internal/swarm/runner_adapter.go`, `cmd/aura/toolpipe.go`, `cmd/aura/doctor.go`, `cmd/aura/docs.go`, the existing document retrieval/status seams, their focused tests, the direct audit/checkpoint, and the quality snapshot rows selected by the repository gate. Risk is correctness/operability; no migration or external destructive action is authorized. Calendar/email and WhatsApp mutations require dedicated operator-owned test accounts/recipients and reversible fixtures; absent credentials or an unpaired device remain blockers and may not be scored as pass.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance / smoke.** (1) the live Memory entity→relationship→get→forget lifecycle succeeds using the advertised schema; (2) fixtures covering MCP `isError:true`, `structuredContent.success:false`, text JSON `success:false`, valid `resolved:false`, and ordinary success prove domain failures never render/cache as success; (3) direct missing-context swarm returns `ERR`; (4) direct registry inventory exactly matches chat/serve inventory for the same resolved configuration, including task, `document_index`, and all enabled MCP tools, and every acquired resource closes; (5) generic doctor and dedicated MCP doctors agree on the resolved server names and reachability; (6) documented trailing docs-search flags parse correctly and retrieval meets the warm/cold SLO with embeddings present; (7) all 58 tools are rerun directly, external mutators complete reversible real-account/device lifecycles, no temporary fixture remains, and the evidence-backed final score exceeds 9.8/10; (8) `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, affected unit/integration/race tests, full tagged coverage at or above 85%, mutation spot-check at or above 70%, and quality-snapshot gate are green. The PRD-only commit for #103 must precede every runtime implementation commit.

> **▶ Amendment #104 (2026-07-30 — interactive web-fetch latency and complete direct evidence).** A direct production probe found that the deployed Compose path still forces `AURA_CONTEXT_PREVIEW_CAP_BYTES=2048`, contradicting the 30000-byte default ratified above, and that `aura toolpipe` discards everything after 500 preview bytes even when `ToolResult` already provides bounded preview plus pageable spillover. A real Wikipedia fetch completed in 1.7 seconds and produced 25629 result bytes, yet the live agent spilled after 2048 bytes and the audit surface displayed only 500. The Compose default must equal the canonical 30000-byte code and `.env.example` default, and the direct runner must emit the complete bounded `ToolResult.Preview` with `bytes`, `truncated`, and duration metadata; it may not apply a second content cap.
>
> **The interactive fetch deadline is ten seconds by default.** `AURA_WEB_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SEC` remains the sole override and still bounds DNS, connect, redirects, retry, body read, and extraction as one wall-clock budget. The old 30-second default is too slow for an agent turn and is superseded in code, Compose, `.env.example`, the active env catalog, tests, and operator documentation. Timeout remains a typed sanitized `timeout` result, never a false success or an unbounded wait. The raw 5 MB body ceiling and SSRF protections are unchanged.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance / smoke.** (1) default config and rendered Compose both resolve fetch timeout 10 and preview cap 30000; (2) a deterministic slow endpoint returns typed timeout within 10 seconds plus bounded scheduling margin and is not retried past the shared deadline; (3) a real public HTML page returns useful markdown inside the deadline; (4) a 25–30 KB direct result is not marked truncated at the canonical cap and `toolpipe` emits every preview byte plus truthful byte/truncation/duration fields; (5) an over-30 KB result spills once and remains fully pageable through `read_tool_output`; (6) focused web/toolpipe tests, race, vet, build, and the direct 58-tool rerun are green. This PRD-only commit precedes the runtime correction.

> **▶ Amendment #105 (2026-07-30 — SEC-09 deterministic recovery-token hashing).** The Phase-40 requirement that prescribed a randomly salted KDF for `identity_recovery_tokens.token_hash` is superseded because that column is a deterministic PRIMARY-KEY lookup: a per-token random salt cannot reproduce the lookup key. The accepted remediation is HMAC-SHA-256 with a server-side pepper derived from `AURA_AUTHULA_SECRET` through HKDF and a reset-token-specific domain label. If the CodeQL query still reports the underlying SHA-256 primitive, the alternative closure is a documented false-positive dismissal: the input is a 256-bit CSPRNG bearer token, not a password and not a limited input space. Either route must resolve the SEC-09 alert; neither permits a plain unkeyed hash regression.
>
> **Deployment boundary.** Online mint, lookup, and offline break-glass recovery must derive the same pepper and fail closed when the source secret is absent or malformed. Introducing the pepper invalidates only reset tokens already in flight; their existing lifetime bounds that compatibility window to at most ten minutes and requires no migration or backfill.

> **▶ Amendment #105.1 (2026-07-30 — SEC-01 configured-secret at-rest scope).** The unqualified requirement to pattern-redact every secret-like value before persistence is superseded. Aura must exact-match and redact its own configured secret values before every at-rest write: inline conversation turn, conversation spill, and full tool-result sidecar. Unknown secret-like values discovered or manipulated by the agent are working data and remain faithful at rest; they are pattern-redacted only when they cross an outbound display, export, ledger, or trace boundary. This exact-match-inbound/pattern-outbound split prevents Aura's credentials from persisting without corrupting legitimate agent working data.
>
> **▶ Amendment #105.2 (2026-07-30 — SEC-02 same-origin-only cockpit).** The earlier permissive-CORS-for-development contract and the `AURA_AGUI_CORS_PERMISSIVE` environment knob are removed and superseded. Aura serves the embedded cockpit and privileged APIs on one origin and emits no CORS headers. There is no production cross-origin consumer, while the session cookie's `SameSite=Strict` and `Secure` posture assumes this same-origin boundary. Any future cross-origin client requires a new PRD amendment, an explicit credentialed allowlist, and a fresh SameSite/CSRF analysis; it may not revive a wildcard path. A separate-port Vite development workflow is an explicit local-development proxy concern, never a production runtime mode.
>
> **▶ Amendment #105.3 (2026-07-30 — SEC-04 enforcement versus resistance).** The Phase-40 sentence requiring every shell, file, network, or MCP request described as “injected” to be denied is superseded because the policy engine receives a tool call and arguments, not trustworthy prompt-provenance metadata. Blanket-denying every mutating call under `server_production` would disable the product's intended Memory, Calendar, WhatsApp, filesystem, and terminal work and contradict Amendments #96/#97. The deterministic acceptance gate instead proves that destructive or irreversible actions are denied or withheld, while ordinary mutations can proceed only through the already-ratified per-identity sandbox or tenant-scoped connector, egress controls, durable policy decision/reservation, and idempotency boundaries. Model resistance to adversarial text remains a separate manual live-LLM eval and may not be inferred from the deterministic enforcement test.

> **▶ Amendment #106 (2026-07-30 — production audit convergence, semantic Memory readiness, and bounded recall).** The June audit documents under `docs/audit/` are evidence captured at their stated commit/date, not live status databases. A single dated closure ledger must map every finding ID to `closed`, `superseded`, `retired`, `external_blocked`, or `open`, with current code/test/live evidence; older indexes receive a historical/superseded notice instead of being silently rewritten. `external_blocked` is not a pass: Calendar/email and WhatsApp delivery remain uncertified until operator-owned reversible fixtures are available. A release score is computed only from executed, evidence-backed rows and must disclose blocked rows separately.
>
> **Confirmation is proportional to consequence, not to the presence of a write.** Amendment #105.3 is the final policy contract: destructive, irreversible, broad-scope, credential/security-boundary, or externally costly actions require an explicit user confirmation/resume. Ordinary tenant-scoped or sandbox-contained mutations do not prompt merely because they mutate; they require authorization, a durable policy decision/reservation, bounded egress, and idempotency. Reversible connector writes such as creating a test calendar event or sending to an already-authorized destination therefore remain usable without universal confirmation, while deletion, account/device unlink, credential rotation, broad publication, and equivalent high-impact operations remain withheld or confirmed. MCP annotations are advisory input only; Aura's source/tool semantic classification is authoritative.
>
> **Agent Memory is one bounded long-term service, not a second hidden context engine.** The Aura deployment permanently disables automatic preference detection and removes the unserved observational-memory prototype from its MCP lifespan: `memory_store_message` acknowledges only its atomic stored message and launches no fire-and-forget observer or preference task. Dormant consolidation/retention APIs are not activated by the Aura MCP profile; any unsafe or unreachable prototype surface is removed or explicitly unavailable rather than shipped as dark code. Aura's existing owner-deletion saga remains the authoritative erasure path.
>
> Long-term automatic recall has one aggregate `max_items` contract across preferences plus entities. Each kind may retrieve and rerank a bounded candidate list, after which a deterministic alternating merge admits at most the selected aggregate K; no per-kind interpretation may inject 2K items. Every model-visible item carries its immutable kind and ID inline, and the out-of-band ordered result list must describe the exact admitted sequence. Recall metadata records the configured reranker model/revision and the observed outcome of the ranking calls (`applied`, `disabled`, or `degraded`); a degraded or unknown ranking cannot be marked adaptive-eligible. Preference and entity searches run concurrently under the caller deadline. The Go consumer rejects a response whose aggregate result count, order, per-kind counts, or effective limits disagree with the selected K.
>
> **MCP mount is a validated, process-owned capability.** Stdio and Streamable HTTP use one typed initialize-result validator: the negotiated version must be in Aura's explicit supported set, `serverInfo.name`/`version` must be non-empty, and `capabilities.tools` must be present before the initialized notification. Malformed or incompatible servers fail at mount. A reconnect may refresh schemas only when the exact accepted raw tool-name set is unchanged; any add/remove/rename/collision drift suppresses that server with a typed restart-required error, so a removed capability is never callable through a stale bridge.
>
> The managed Memory mount additionally exposes one non-model-facing process-owned host client to automatic recall and readiness. Automatic recall must not initialize a raw MCP transport per turn. Strict production readiness runs a bounded functional `memory_search` through that same authenticated/reconnecting client using an isolated synthetic owner and validates the typed result; a mount, Neo4j, embedding, protocol, or semantic failure produces stable `memory_unavailable` readiness state and the existing readiness alert path. Health remains cheap process liveness. The host client shares shutdown, breaker, egress, authentication, domain-error, and idempotency behavior with model-facing Memory tools.
>
> **Application bounds and history work are real, not labels.** The Agent Memory boundary rejects oversized strings/collections/nesting, out-of-range limits, and oversized results before expensive work or response emission, and the Compose service has explicit CPU/memory limits. `AURA_HISTORY_HARD_CAP_TURNS` must be wired into the managed-history query/path before the context ladder: it preserves the protected root and complete newest active round/tool group while bounding rows rehydrated/tokenized per turn. If that cannot be proven for both linear and selected-branch histories, the misleading knob is removed rather than advertised as protection.
>
> **Machine-checkable closure gate.** Fail-first tests cover aggregate 8+8 recall, exact inline provenance, reranker applied/disabled/degraded evidence, no post-return tasks, oversized inputs/results, protocol mismatch/malformed/missing tools capability, reconnect add/remove/rename, one process-owned Memory lifecycle, semantic readiness failure/recovery, and >N linear/branch history. Focused Python tests plus full pytest/Ruff/mypy, focused and race-enabled Go tests, `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, the full tagged coverage gate at or above 85%, mutation spot-check at or above 70%, quality-snapshot gate, rebuilt Compose deployment, direct tool audit, and real retrieval/latency E2E must all pass. The closure ledger records exact commands, postconditions, and measured p50/p95; the final evidence-backed score must exceed 9.8/10. This PRD-only commit precedes every #106 runtime implementation commit.
>
> **▶ Amendment #106.1 (2026-07-31 — residual quality convergence).** The definitive ledger may close a quality finding only after the reported duplicate, dead, or divergent implementation is absent from the current tree and its behavior is covered. The remaining high-confidence residuals are closed as follows: remove the unpopulated `scoring.TaskArgs.AgentTier` modifier while preserving the gateway's unconditional `agent_job >= Risky` floor; centralize the five `pgtype.UUID` string boundaries in `internal/db` while retaining the intentionally different raw-`uuid.UUID` share boundary; centralize PostgreSQL NUL replacement there; name the conversation spill default in `internal/conversations` and use it at the composition/config defaults; centralize strict boolean coercion in `web/src/api/json.ts`; and make function-component skeleton translation reactive through `useTranslation`. Existing focused package tests gain fail-first assertions for the shared boundaries/defaults, strict boolean behavior, and language re-render. No schema, environment, external API, or confirmation-policy change is introduced.
>
> **▶ Amendment #106.2 (2026-07-31 — definitive scheduler, backup, CLI-catalog, and XLSX closure).** Four residual production findings remain implementation work rather than historical evidence and must close before the definitive ledger can score them. First, scheduler cancellation is split semantically: `Scheduler.Start(ctx)` uses `ctx` as the admission lifecycle, but a task already claimed before cancellation runs on a cancellation-detached context bounded by its registered `HandlerMeta.MaxDuration`; the dispatcher enforces that maximum for every handler, even when the handler does not create its own timeout. A canceled admission context may not claim or dispatch another task, while `Start` still joins all work already admitted. Focused tests must prove both halves with a blocking handler: admission cancellation does not cancel the handler, canceling the handler's own deadline does, and no post-cancel sweep or new dispatch occurs.
>
> Second, every database backup writes to a unique sibling partial file and promotes it to the timestamped final name only after the dump succeeds and the artifact is stat-able. Error or cancellation removes the partial and never creates the final artifact. `deploy/aura-scheduler.service` grants 1,860 seconds, exceeding the 30-minute longest handler budget plus terminal-write grace; ordinary shutdown still returns immediately when no backup is active. A static regression test parses the unit and asserts its stop budget exceeds `backupMaxDuration`, while handler tests prove failed and canceled dumps cannot be promoted.
>
> Third, `aura docs ingest` creates one owner-scoped logical catalog entry for the resolved operator identity, with `search_document_id` and ingestion-job provenance, before reporting the CLI ingest successful. It begins in `processing`, becomes `ready` only when every embedding batch lands, and becomes `failed` with a reason on terminal embedding failure. This catalog writer is wired only into the standalone CLI composition: asset/channel ingestion retains its existing asset-version recorder and cannot create a duplicate logical document. The CLI passes the identity already resolved onto its context into `IngestRequest`; an empty identity remains an explicit uncatalogued legacy/test path rather than inventing ownership.
>
> Fourth, XLSX extraction derives coordinates from enumerated row/column positions and `openpyxl.utils.get_column_letter`, never from `ReadOnlyCell`/`EmptyCell.coordinate` or `.column`. A workbook fixture with an internal empty cell must extract the surrounding populated cells with stable coordinates. The live Neo4j repair for retrieval finding R-08 is narrowly scoped: delete only `:Chunk` nodes with no incoming `:HAS_CHUNK`, remove only the erroneous `:Document` label from nodes that are also `:Entity` and have no document-chunk ownership, then assert both anomaly counts are zero. These changes introduce no schema, environment knob, connector mutation, or confirmation-policy change.

> **▶ Amendment #106.3 (2026-07-31 — production-operations and release-evidence closeout).** Phase 41 is not closed by the existing advisory scripts. A restore run that prints success after skipping Neo4j, sidecar state, or object storage is a failed drill; a chaos step marked `continue-on-error` is evidence collection, not a gate. The definitive closeout therefore adds one non-destructive production-readiness harness whose CI fixture mode and operator live mode share the same assertions and machine-readable report. Every run owns uniquely prefixed fixtures and disposable restore targets, records per-plane elapsed time and the newest protected fixture timestamp, and cleans only those fixtures. It may never clear or restore over a live Postgres database, Neo4j database, sidecar tree, or Garage bucket.
>
> **Disaster recovery has four mandatory planes.** Postgres is dumped and restored into a fresh uniquely named database with sentinel row and checksum verification. Neo4j 5.26 Community is stopped only in an explicitly selected maintenance/live run, dumped with `neo4j-admin database dump`, restarted immediately, and loaded into an isolated disposable Neo4j data volume for sentinel/count verification; CI uses the same offline dump/load commands over a seeded disposable source volume. Conversation sidecars are archived with a manifest and restored into a fresh directory with path, byte count, and SHA-256 equality checks. Garage/S3 is exercised through its authenticated data plane: a uniquely prefixed object set is exported with a manifest, deleted only inside that fixture prefix, restored, byte/hash verified, and removed. Missing credentials, missing services, missing artifacts, a skipped plane, cleanup outside the owned prefix, or a failed postcondition fails the run. The JSON evidence exposes per-plane `rpo_seconds`, `rto_ms`, restored item/byte counts, checksum verdicts, and cleanup verdicts.
>
> **Load and chaos are blocking capability checks.** A pinned Vegeta workload drives the real `/healthz` and `/readyz` appliance endpoints at the documented supported concurrency and records requests/sec, p50, p95, p99, success ratio, and bounded resource use. A pinned Toxiproxy harness covers database outage/recovery, an MCP timeout storm, and Garage outage/recovery; the atomic-backup kill/cancel tests cover process termination during a write. Each scenario asserts the documented degraded result, bounded deadline, recovery, no false readiness, no duplicate side effect, and no partial promoted artifact. Shared-runner budgets may be wider than appliance budgets, but neither tier is optional or advisory and neither may use `continue-on-error` or skip-as-green.
>
> **Capability evaluation is deterministic by default.** One report-producing suite executes named golden, adversarial, and failure scenarios for shell containment, filesystem ownership, MCP domain errors/timeout/trust, Memory ownership/provenance/bounds, pause-resume atomicity, terminal-error truthfulness, idempotent mutation, and multi-step workflow completion. Every class must execute at least one positive and one negative assertion; the report includes executed/failed/blocked counts and exact scenario IDs. Optional live-LLM judging remains a separately authorized paid tier and cannot turn a deterministic failure green.
>
> **Governance and release gate.** ADRs record loop semantics, tool consequence policy, Memory provenance/erasure, MCP trust/lifecycle, deployment profiles, and the already-selected sandbox boundary. A release-readiness checklist is machine-checked and names the immutable evidence artifacts for security, coverage, mutation, load/chaos, DR, observability/readiness, rollback, and the definitive finding ledger. CI runs every new tier, uploads the JSON reports, and fails when a required class or plane did not execute. The pre-push hook at least compiles every tagged integration tier so it cannot remain invisible locally; CI performs the live execution. OPS-01/04/05/06 and REL-01/03 remain open until their reports are produced successfully. REL-02 closes only with current owned-surface coverage at or above 85% and mutation scores at or above 70% for the named critical boundaries. External Calendar/email and WhatsApp delivery remain disclosed `external_blocked`, never scored as passed. This PRD-only commit precedes every #106.3 harness, workflow, ADR, or release-gate commit.

> **▶ Amendment #106.4 (2026-07-31 — bad-image retirement and fail-closed rollback baseline).** The operator explicitly retires `v1.0.1` and every pre-current Aura appliance image as invalid rollback targets after the exact-candidate rehearsal proved that the old daemon cannot satisfy the current authenticated Memory and readiness contracts. No workflow, runbook, default input, compatibility environment, or score may revive a retired image merely to make rollback evidence pass. Local cleanup removes only Aura image/container artifacts after the exact current image is healthy; it never removes application volumes, databases, object-store data, or sidecar images. Registry cleanup is a separate authenticated administrative action and must be reported blocked unless the remote package versions are observably absent.
>
> **No baseline bypass.** Until a new approved immutable Aura image is published, release readiness has no valid previous-image target and therefore remains fail-closed. The production-readiness workflow requires an operator-supplied immutable digest, rejects a missing/tag-only/retired target, and the release gate continues to require distinct previous/candidate digests plus a real previous→candidate restoration. An identical-image restart, candidate-only boot, local deployment, or explicit “baseline reset” cannot be scored as version rollback. The current source may be deployed locally for direct E2E validation, but it cannot be called release-ready or used to publish a release until a valid baseline exists under a separately evidenced promotion.

> **▶ Amendment #106.5 (2026-07-31 — current-only audit register and historical document retirement).** At the operator's explicit direction, Amendment #106 is superseded only in its retention model. `docs/audit/` contains one current register, `README.md`, and no historical finding register, plan, handoff, experiment, benchmark helper, superseded index, closed-item ledger, or past score snapshot. The pre-retirement tree remains recoverable from Git history; it is not duplicated in the active working tree. Historical references elsewhere in this PRD identify past decisions, not live files, and this amendment is their archival pointer.
>
> **Only unresolved state is active audit data.** The current register contains every genuinely unresolved issue as one machine-readable Markdown table row with a unique ID, state (`open` or `external_blocked`), present evidence, concrete closure condition, and owner. Closed, superseded, and retired rows are absent rather than carried forward. The register must disclose release readiness separately from implementation quality: an audit-disclosure gate may pass while unresolved rows exist, but it emits `release_ready:false` and may not convert an external blocker into a pass or an implementation score. The last historical closure result and direct-tool score may be named only as archival context, never as current release certification.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance.** (1) `git ls-files docs/audit` returns exactly `docs/audit/README.md`; (2) the audit gate rejects a missing required current ID, a duplicate ID, any terminal/unknown state, blank evidence, blank closure condition, or blank owner; (3) its JSON report lists every current row, exact state counts, `open_total`, and `release_ready:false`; (4) repository-owned live code, workflows, and current dashboards contain no broken dependency on a retired audit path; (5) the gate tests, workflow contract, link scan, build, vet, and normal pre-push gates pass. This PRD-only commit precedes the purge and gate rewrite.

> **▶ Amendment #107 (2026-08-03 — row-level security becomes the enforcement, and D-06's 403-on-known-foreign is retired).** Postgres row-level security was written to fail OPEN: every policy carried `NULLIF(current_setting('app.current_identity', true), '') IS NULL OR owner = …`, so an unset session variable made the whole table visible. Measured as `aura_app` with no identity: all 32 conversations, all 648 turns and every document. Migrations `0087` and `0089` remove that escape and add, per identity-scoped table, one `AS RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL TO aura_app` floor requiring the variable to be set — restrictive policies combine with AND, so no future permissive policy can widen past them. Child tables name the PARENT'S OWNER directly instead of deferring to the parent's policy, because that indirection is why `conversation_turns` ceded together with `conversations`. `db.WithCallerIdentityTx` carries the identity from the context; the three genuinely cross-tenant sweeps (`ScanOrphans`, `ListReservedDeletes`, `aura paused-states`) enumerate identities and run one scoped transaction each — never a bypass, never a service role. `VerifyRLSEnforced` refuses to boot when the resolved role carries `rolsuper` or `rolbypassrls`.
>
> **D-06's 403-on-known-foreign is RETIRED; conversation mutations and approval resolutions now answer 404.** It was implementable only through an unscoped existence probe — "does this row exist for somebody else?" — which is precisely the read fail-closed RLS must deny. Keeping it would mean keeping a query the security model forbids, i.e. dark code with a security label on it. The collapse is toward the safer side (a foreign id is indistinguishable from a nonexistent one) and matches the rule `share_api.go` already applied.
>
> **Deliberately NOT scoped, each for a stated reason, not an omission.** Pre-identity authentication lookups — `password_reset_tokens`, `password_reset_challenges`, `identity_recovery`, `identity_auth_links`, and `telegram_accounts` — because the query that ESTABLISHES who you are is the one a policy would deny. Append-only audit ledgers, because owner-filtering destroys the cross-identity forensics they exist for. And the genuinely cross-identity paths, of which `serve_auth.go`'s migration of rows from the retired `local` identity to the enrolled one is the sharpest: two identities by definition, and no single `set_config` can authorise it. `shared_links` takes a different predicate again — `mine OR (no identity set AND not revoked)`, SELECT-only — because `ResolveByToken` is anonymous by design and `DueForExpiry` must still see rows whose expiry has already passed, or the sweep leaks object-store bytes forever.
>
> **Two defects the change surfaced, both fixed.** Migration `0016`'s tamper guard distinguished a legitimate cascade from tampering by asking whether the parent conversation still existed, through a `SECURITY INVOKER` probe; under fail-closed RLS that answers "absent" for an invisible parent, so any identity-less connection could DELETE from the append-only `tool_invocations` ledger. It is `SECURITY DEFINER` with a pinned `search_path`. And `PgAuditStore.ListActivityForIdentity`, scoped to the caller rather than to the read's subject, silently returned nothing when an operator inspected another identity.
>
> **The regression this amendment also records.** `0087` made `documents`, `idempotency_operations`, `storage_objects` and `identity_object_store` fail-closed while their stores never set an identity — `idempotency.Store` takes a bare `sqlc.DBTX`, so every `Begin` fails `42501` on a deployed daemon. Reproduced on the live database before it was written down. A policy is only as shippable as the store beneath it, and a fail-closed migration must land WITH the identity plumbing of every store it covers, never before it.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance.** As `aura_app` with no `app.current_identity`: a scoped table returns zero rows and a cross-identity INSERT is refused `42501`; with identity A set, exactly A's rows are returned; a share link still resolves anonymously by token while a revoked one resolves to nothing and identity B sees zero. The `db_integration` tier carries the regression test. `VerifyRLSEnforced` fails boot under a `rolbypassrls` role.

> **▶ Amendment #108 (2026-08-03 — restore the cockpit memory graph on ArcadeDB and adopt Studio's bounded incremental exploration).** The Neo4j removal intentionally replaced the drawable Graph Explorer with a schema-only `ArcadeGraphView`: graph reads returned HTTP 200 with empty `nodes`/`edges` and prose saying traversal was not implemented. That is now a product defect, not an accepted reduction. This amendment supersedes both that schema-only posture and the old conversation-footprint contract. ArcadeDB memory stores `Entity` vertices and bitemporal `FACT` edges in one database per Aura identity; it does not store `Conversation`/`Message` vertices, and `source_run_id`/`source_memory_ids` are not a guaranteed thread-to-graph join. The Graph surface therefore represents **all memory belonging to the authenticated Aura identity**, never a fabricated graph “linked to this thread.” The API exposes exactly two operations, `overview` and `expand`, with `node_id` required only for `expand`. The removed `seed`, `schema_overview`, `seed_id`, and `session` request shapes are rejected rather than retained as aliases: Aura carries no legacy compatibility branch or dark graph contract.
>
> **Read contract and isolation.** Aura reuses ArcadeDB 26.7.3 Studio's documented HTTP graph envelope: a read-only database query with `serializer: "studio"` yields compact vertices `{r,t,p,i,o}` and edges `{r,t,p,i,o}`. Aura calls only `/api/v1/query/{database}` through the tenant-specific database/user/password derived for the authenticated identity; the browser never receives an ArcadeDB credential, database name, arbitrary-query endpoint, or raw server response. `overview` compiles to a bounded edge-first read over schema-validated edge types, then uses schema-validated vertex types to include isolated vertices. `expand` accepts only an ArcadeDB RID in `node_id` matching `^#[0-9]+:[0-9]+$` and loads that vertex's direct incoming/outgoing edges, optionally narrowed to schema-validated relationship types. User values remain bind parameters; the only interpolated tokens are a validated RID, live schema type names escaped as identifiers, and server-owned numeric limits. Caller caps default to 75 nodes / 200 edges and are clamped to those maxima. The projection maps edge `o→source` and `i→target`, vertex `i+o→degree`, stable RID→ID, type→label, and human properties (`name`, then `title`, then type)→caption; vector/embedding payloads never cross into cockpit JSON. `FACT.predicate` is the visible edge caption while `FACT` remains the filterable relationship type. Output capping drops dangling edges rather than emitting a renderer-crashing partial reference.
>
> **Studio-informed cockpit behavior, deliberately read-only.** Aura adopts the parts of Studio that fit an evidence workspace: the initial bounded graph is drawable; selecting a node exposes an explicit **Expand neighbors** action; an expansion is cumulatively merged by RID into the current canvas instead of replacing the operator's context; duplicates are discarded; filters issue a fresh structured server read; visible status reports node/edge counts and cap truncation; and the read-only provenance affordance says **ArcadeDB SQL**, never “Cypher.” Copying Studio's arbitrary query editor, record editing/deletion, import, or database administration is explicitly out of scope and forbidden on this surface. The primary action and empty-state copy say “Load/refresh memory graph,” not “Explore this conversation.” Desktop and mobile keep the existing accessible parallel DOM, inspector, 44 px touch floor, reduced-motion handling, and non-canvas interaction path.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance.** (1) transport tests pin the `serializer:"studio"` payload, the query endpoint, compact envelope decoding, server-error detail, omission of credentials from errors, and the hard 200-record maximum; (2) compiler/projector tests pin default/max caps, identifier escaping, strict `node_id` RID rejection before I/O, directionality, degree, captions, embedding omission, de-duplication, isolated vertices, filters, and dangling-edge removal; (3) AG-UI tests prove `overview` returns drawable nodes and edges, `expand` stays identity-scoped, and every removed operation/field is rejected as an unknown request rather than routed through compatibility code; (4) jsdom tests prove the ArcadeDB copy, conversation-independent initial load, explicit expand action, cumulative merge, and replacement-on-filter behavior; (5) Playwright on desktop and mobile drives the real authenticated `dvdmarchetto@gmail.com` database, observes its non-empty memory graph, expands a real RID without losing prior nodes, records zero serious/critical accessibility violations and zero browser errors, and performs no ArcadeDB write. Focused Go unit/race, web lint/typecheck/Vitest/build, repository vet/build, the live ArcadeDB read smoke, and a rebuilt embedded bundle must all pass before closure.

> **▶ Amendment #109 (2026-08-03 — ArcadeDB Studio-style graph captions are part of the canvas, not inspector-only metadata).** Amendment #72's dense-overview suppression is superseded for the identity memory graph: a node whose projected caption is non-empty MUST render that caption on the canvas, including the bounded 75-node overview, and a relationship whose projected caption is non-empty MUST render it along its edge. Aura adopts Studio's presentation semantics rather than its administration surface: captions are centred inside circular nodes, wrapped and contrast-adjusted; node diameter grows with the compact caption using Studio's `25 + 6 × label length` rule capped at 200 px while retaining degree as a minimum-size signal; relationship captions follow the edge with a background outline; and directed relationships keep an arrowhead. Technical identifiers remain compacted and human captions are capped at Studio's 45-character limit with the complete value preserved in the inspector and accessible DOM. Nodes are coloured by ArcadeDB vertex type and, where available, entity `kind`; relationships are coloured by edge type, with text remaining the primary encoding. Path highlighting may dim off-path elements but MUST NOT erase their captions. Aura uses the same Cytoscape + fCoSE renderer/layout stack as Studio; the former Sigma/Graphology/ForceAtlas2 stack is deleted rather than retained as a second implementation. Studio's query editor, mutable actions and administration surface remain forbidden.

> **▶ Amendment #110 (2026-08-03 — conversation memory is automatic context, not a model-selected retrieval maze).** A live trace for conversation `019fc955-43a6-78ac-b6da-e0a14a61f20d` proved that the memory graph contained `Davide located_in Caraglio`, every fact had an EmbeddingGemma vector, and the mounted MCP was healthy, yet Aura answered that the location was absent. The model first selected `memory_search`, whose generic first-person query abstained, and only after the operator objected did it spend two more model rounds on `memory_entities` and `memory_facts_about` to recover the exact fact. The failure is the agent-facing contract: eight deferred memory tools make the model choose an internal retrieval plan that Aura already owns. This amendment supersedes the pull-on-demand-only posture and the deleted adaptive `memory_get_context` contract. Before every model round, the Runner reads the authenticated identity's bounded `memory_digest` through the already-mounted host MCP client and injects it exactly once as a non-persisted, untrusted reference item immediately before the current user message (or at the tail on resume). The deterministic context ladder reserves its tokens before L2/L2.5 and omits the item rather than truncating it when it cannot fit. A sidecar failure is explicit in logs and must never be misreported as an empty memory.
>
> The model-facing read surface is one deferred `memory_recall` operation. It accepts free text or an exact entity and internally chooses hybrid search versus graph traversal. Raw `memory_search`, `memory_facts_about`, `memory_entities`, `memory_digest`, `graph_schema`, and `memory_reembed` remain active host/operator primitives for the CLI, readiness, graph UI, and automatic context, but are hidden from the model; they are not compatibility aliases. The model retains only `memory_recall`, `memory_upsert_fact`, `memory_merge_entities`, and `memory_forget`. No legacy tool name or dual model-facing path survives. Acceptance: the live "dove vivo?" scenario answers Caraglio on the first turn without a memory tool call; a nonexistent fact still returns `facts:[]` with explicit abstention; the injected block is owner-scoped, fenced, non-persisted, budget-counted, byte-preserved, and absent on sidecar error; model-visible memory tools are exactly the four names above; focused unit/race tests, live MCP/ArcadeDB tests, MRS >96.5, full coverage >=85%, and final-request budget checks pass.

> **▶ Amendment #111 (2026-08-03 — OTLP is the trace path; daemon metrics have one Prometheus scrape path).** The live acceptance run for amendment #110 exposed that `aura serve` constructed both its private Prometheus reader and an unconditional OTLP metric exporter whenever `AURA_OTEL_EXPORTER=otlp`. The configured local endpoint is Tempo, which accepts OTLP traces but does not implement the OTLP `MetricsService`; every periodic metric export therefore failed with `Unimplemented` even though the same measurements were already available on the private Prometheus endpoint. This amendment removes that duplicate, unconfigurable metric path rather than suppressing its errors. `AURA_OTEL_EXPORTER` and `AURA_OTEL_ENDPOINT` continue to configure traces only, exactly as their existing env catalog states. The long-lived daemon exposes metrics only through its private `AURA_METRICS_BIND` handler, scraped by Prometheus in Aura's shared network namespace. The unused OTLP metric exporter code and dependency are removed; no dormant dual-fanout switch remains. Acceptance: the private metrics handler and Prometheus scrape tests stay green, a real agent turn produces no `MetricsService`/OTLP metric error, and Tempo receives the turn trace.
>
> **▶ Amendment #112 (2026-08-03 — MRS validates the Go test JSON protocol on stdout, not unrelated toolchain diagnostics on stderr).** The first `master` CI run for amendment #110 completed every memory scenario, scored **100.00/100**, and passed all hard gates except `suite_integrity`: a successful `cmd/aura` test process emitted one Go module/toolchain diagnostic on stderr, while the evaluator had merged stderr into the `go test -json` stdout stream and therefore reported `line 1 is not go test JSON`. The evaluator must capture and parse stdout independently as the protocol stream. Malformed or non-JSON stdout, a non-zero process exit, package failure, skip, missing scenario, malformed marker, or absent coverage remains fail-closed. Non-empty stderr from a zero-exit Go invocation is retained as a diagnostic line count but is not itself a protocol violation. Acceptance: a regression test feeds valid passing Go JSON on stdout plus a toolchain message on stderr and the suite stays green; the existing malformed-stdout test remains red; the full live evaluator returns `PASS: MRS=100.00` in GitHub Actions.
>
> **▶ Amendment #120 (2026-08-12 — proactive memory preload complements the always-on digest).** Amendment #110 injects the query-less `memory_digest` before every model round; recall of a fact ABSENT from that bounded index still depends on the model choosing to call `memory_recall`. Inspired by Google ADK's `preload_memory`, the Runner now OPTIONALLY runs a relevance `memory_search` over the CURRENT user text and injects the top-k facts as a second fenced `<memory_recall>` section inside the SAME pre-user transient block (the deterministic ladder stays single-item; the two sections share one budgeted block, inserted before the current user message). Both legs are fail-soft — a search error, timeout, or explicit abstention drops the recall section and keeps the digest; a nil user message (resume/branch continuation) skips the preload entirely. Knobs: `AURA_MEMORY_PRELOAD_ENABLED` (**default false** — it adds an MCP round-trip per turn), `AURA_MEMORY_PRELOAD_TOP_K` (5), `AURA_MEMORY_PRELOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` (1500). `memory_search` stays a host/operator primitive (not model-facing), consistent with #110. **Cosa la misura NON dimostra**: verificato SOLO con unit test offline (fake `MemoryContextProvider` + fake MCP host client) — la QUALITÀ del retrieval (ArcadeDB hybrid search sui fatti reali) e il costo/latenza per turno NON sono misurati, perciò il knob è dark-by-default finché un E2E su stack acceso non lo misura (poi l'emendamento registra la misura, non prima).
>
> **▶ Amendment #113 (2026-08-03 — forgetting memory never pauses for gateway approval).** `memory_forget` is an ordinary identity-scoped memory mutation, not an approval-gated action. Its existing empty-filter refusal, tenant-isolated ArcadeDB credential, bounded filter validation, idempotency, tool-invocation audit, and optional `dry_run` remain the safety boundary. The MCP tool advertises `DestructiveHint=false`, the trusted memory recipe classifies it as mutating/non-destructive, and the gateway executes it in the same turn without creating an `ask_user` approval. There is no intent classifier, confirmation exception, compatibility route, or second model loop. Acceptance: the bridged spec remains `Mutating=true` and becomes `Destructive=false`; `memory_forget` reaches execution without a gateway pause; other destructive tools retain their existing approval policy; focused unit/race tests and the full quality gates remain green.
>
> **▶ Amendment #114 (2026-08-04 — industrial document ingestion, provenance-bearing passage retrieval, and durable erasure).** A full-stack audit of every ingress, catalog, object-store, worker, retrieval, open, retry, and delete path proved that Aura's current document feature is a file-card router, not document RAG. Web and Telegram uploads normally persist an asset and an original, but `aura docs ingest` and `document_index` create searchable catalog rows without an asset/version and therefore cannot satisfy their own `document_open` contract. Search exposes rows with no active openable version, jobs cannot reclaim expired `running` leases, automatic and manual retry cannot recover the failed asset/job state pair, document deletion marks assets deleted before invoking the object deleter and consequently leaves Garage bytes ledgered forever, and the model is instructed to call the nonexistent shape `document_search(document_id=...)`. The card is capped and PDF extraction stops at the first bounded pages, so facts later in prose and exact sheet/page/cell provenance are unsearchable. Amendments #62's doc-RAG deferral, #89's Neo4j document graph, #106.2's CLI-only catalog success, #107's classification of identity-less document job/ledger tables as harmless global control plane, and every MarkItDown/Neo4j chunk promise are superseded for the document plane by this contract.
>
> **Evidence and BUILD-vs-REUSE decision.** Primary sources were read before design and their exact source trees were preserved under `D:/tmp/aura-document-pipeline-references/`: Microsoft GraphRAG v3.1.1 at `14a00ad88fc33cf2b52f4f113f25807556f8e25e`, Docling v2.118.0 at `9b454c9e88454d95fd04d538c552a3c07bc3c04d`, Docling Core v2.90.0 at `23fa247e9abeaaf3e9f378f635758ce8915b08e7`, CocoIndex at `714bbc3a7bc43ce152ed91bc0403cb9264a88518`, Docling Serve v1.29.0 at `7f2b890c5538d5ad511dce42a69af5840452b1c4`, ArcadeDB v26.7.3 at `f2f3d880597d1d2310d61267e08ff5485504b4b5`, IBM Granite-Docling-258M at `982fe3b40f2fa73c365bdb1bcacf6c81b7184bfe`, and the user-selected `onnx-community/granite-docling-258M-ONNX` conversion at `e8602580df77443fc3421cf3bae0601da601e5c6`. Aura REUSES the official Docling Serve CPU image and stable v1 asynchronous hybrid-chunk API for layout/OCR/table conversion and its `DocMeta` provenance (`origin`, `self_ref`, headings/captions, page, bounding box, char span). The ONNX community repository is Apache-2.0 and supplies fp32/fp16/int8/q4 graphs, but its supported interfaces are Transformers.js and a handwritten direct ONNXRuntime loop; Docling v2.118.0 has no ONNX VLM engine and its supported `granite_docling` preset resolves the IBM repository through Transformers. Aura therefore benchmarks the supported preset for scanned/image-heavy pages but does not ship a second JavaScript/custom ONNX inference control plane. Aura REUSES its 768-dimensional EmbeddingGemma contract and consolidates the two current OpenAI-compatible clients into one transport, and REUSES the per-identity ArcadeDB credential/database, parameterized HTTP client, `LSM_VECTOR`, `SEARCH_INDEX`, and `vector.neighbors` primitives. Aura BUILDS the lifecycle, stage ledger, outbox/reconciler, stable IDs, active-generation fencing, and retrieval contract in Go/Postgres because GraphRAG's update matches by title and omits reliable deletion/resume, while embedding CocoIndex would add a second Python/Rust/LMDB control plane outside Aura's Postgres/RLS truth source. GraphRAG's cache key and text-unit provenance and CocoIndex's desired-state/fingerprint/precommit-apply-commit patterns are design donors only; neither runtime or compatibility adapter enters the product. Authoritative references are [Docling chunking](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/concepts/chunking/), [Docling Serve v1 usage](https://github.com/docling-project/docling-serve/blob/v1.29.0/docs/usage.md), [IBM Granite Docling](https://www.ibm.com/granite/docs/models/docling), [Granite-Docling ONNX model card](https://huggingface.co/onnx-community/granite-docling-258M-ONNX), [GraphRAG dataflow](https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/index/default_dataflow/), [GraphRAG update workflows](https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/cli/), [CocoIndex stable IDs](https://cocoindex.io/docs/common_resources/id_generation/), [ArcadeDB source](https://github.com/ArcadeData/arcadedb), [PostgreSQL row security](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html), [AWS retry with backoff](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/cloud-design-patterns/retry-backoff.html), and [OpenTelemetry messaging spans](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/messaging/messaging-spans/).
>
> **One architecture, three persistence responsibilities.** Garage is the sole truth source for immutable original bytes and content-addressed derived Docling artifacts. PostgreSQL `aura.*` is the sole transactional control plane: tenant ownership, logical documents, immutable versions, active version, cards/digests/tags, object ledger, chunks and locator metadata, embedding projection metadata, jobs, stage fingerprints, events, delete state, and outbox reconciliation. The existing per-identity ArcadeDB database remains the physical tenant boundary and gains a document projection beside Memory: `DocumentProjection` vertices, immutable `Passage` vertices, and `HAS_PASSAGE` edges. It is a rebuildable retrieval projection, never the lifecycle truth source and never an additional model-visible MCP surface.
