The private tenant credential resolver/provisioner currently trapped in `cmd/arcadedb-mcp` moves to `internal/arcadedb`; both MCP memory and the Aura document worker call that single implementation, and no caller derives a weaker credential path. The memory types and document types do not share edges or retrieval queries. Entity/relation/claim extraction, community summaries, and a second graph retriever are outside this convergence: measured passage retrieval must land and pass before any such cost is authorized.
>
> **One embedding transport.** `internal/embeddings` becomes the sole OpenAI-compatible embedding transport for Memory and documents. It preserves response `index` ordering, rejects duplicate/missing indexes and dimension mismatches, applies bounded batching and deadlines, supports the configured MRL dimension, and never logs text. Callers must select the asymmetric EmbeddingGemma task: stored passages use `title: <bounded document title or none> | text: <contextualized passage>` and queries use `task: search result | query: <query>`. The model identifier, immutable model revision/artifact SHA-256, dimension, normalization, tokenizer revision, and task-prefix version enter the embedding fingerprint; changing any one forces a new projection generation rather than mixing vectors.
>
> **Canonical identity and version semantics.** The logical `documents.id` is stable across content changes and is selected from `(identity_id, source_kind, source_key)`. Connector-native stable locators are used when available; CLI and sandbox paths are canonicalized inside their allowed root and persisted only as a SHA-256 locator fingerprint, never as a host path. A new user action with no stable locator creates a new logical source key; an ingress retry MUST carry the original idempotency key. `search_document_id` becomes a typed, owner-scoped, immutable identifier with a unique live constraint `(identity_id, search_document_id)` instead of a JSON lookup. A version ID is deterministic from `document_id + raw_sha256`; allocation of monotonically increasing `version_number` occurs while the document row is locked. Same logical document + same raw SHA-256 is a replay/no-op even under concurrent writers; same logical document + different SHA-256 is N+1; an unrelated source with identical bytes remains a separate logical document unless the caller explicitly attaches it as a new version. A passage ID is deterministic from `version_id + structural_anchor + occurrence + normalized_text_sha256`, so duplicate text at distinct pages/cells cannot collide.
>
> **One ingress for every surface.** Web presign/finalize, Telegram attachments, `aura docs ingest`, and `document_index` all terminate in the same owner-scoped `assets.Service` ingestion command with `scope=library`, a durable Garage original, a typed source locator, an idempotency key, and `process=true`. Direct `documents.Service.IngestPath` is an internal processor stage only; no public/tool/CLI caller may use it to publish a searchable row. `document_index` copies from the identity sandbox into the canonical object store before deleting the staged source. `send_file` remains delivery-only and cannot silently index. The maximum document size is the single `AURA_ASSET_MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` contract on every entry point; the old 50 MiB CLI/tool split is removed.
>
> **Lifecycle state machine and visibility commit.** Ingest is `accepted → stored → queued → converting → chunking → embedding → projecting → ready`; terminal non-retryable work is `failed`, retry exhaustion is `dead_letter`, and delete is `deleting → deleted`. `searchable` is not a separate truth state: a document is visible if and only if `documents.status='ready'`, `active_version_id` names an owner-coherent `document_versions.status='ready'`, the active version names a live raw storage object and live asset, every required passage has an active projection record for the same pipeline generation, and no delete is pending. A previous ready version remains active while N+1 processes. Docling `partial_success` never replaces it automatically; for a first version it is terminal `failed/partial_conversion` unless a format-specific policy in this PRD explicitly accepts every required locator class. The final Postgres activation transaction sets version ready, active version, pipeline generation, document ready, asset searchable, job succeeded, and the corresponding event atomically. Every search candidate is revalidated against that active generation before emission, making an ArcadeDB projection lag a temporary miss rather than a stale or cross-version answer.
>
> **Durable stage DAG, cache, and delta.** Required stages are `identify → convert → chunk → embed → project → activate`; card generation is a deterministic parallel derivation and cannot publish early. `document_pipeline_stages` stores owner, document/version, stage, `input_fingerprint`, `producer_version`, artifact object key/SHA-256/size, status, attempt count, lease generation, error class, and timestamps, unique on `(identity_id, version_id, stage, input_fingerprint)`. Fingerprints are canonical and versioned: conversion = raw SHA-256 + Docling image/version + model artifact digest + conversion options; chunking = converted artifact SHA-256 + chunker/version + tokenizer identity + chunk options; embedding = contextualized passage SHA-256 + model/revision/dimension/normalization; projection = chunk manifest SHA-256 + embedding manifest SHA-256 + Arcade schema version. Secrets, URLs, timeouts, trace IDs, and retry policy never enter a content fingerprint. Successful artifacts are immutable and cacheable; errors are never cached. A changed producer/config invalidates only downstream stages. The worker writes derived artifacts first, records their hashes, idempotently upserts candidate passages, commits the new Postgres active generation, then tombstones the prior Arcade generation and unreferenced derived objects. Crash recovery is roll-forward through the ledger/outbox; no cross-store transaction is pretended.
>
> **Docling boundary.** Compose pins the official multi-arch index `quay.io/docling-project/docling-serve-cpu:v1.29.0@sha256:51c18e0e0fec8a13ab858f03d5e9a140178d8d95962400553cb2644ad5ee84da`; mutable `latest`/`main` tags and tag-only production resolution are forbidden. Aura calls `/v1/chunk/hybrid/file/async`, persists the returned task ID as diagnostic resume state, polls `/v1/status/poll/{task_id}`, fetches `/v1/result/{task_id}`, and requests `include_converted_doc=true` so the canonical `DoclingDocument` and chunks derive from one conversion. An unavailable/expired result may cause recomputation but cannot duplicate a stage result. The standard Docling pipeline is the fixed default for born-digital PDF/Office/HTML/text because it preserves native structure without generative transcription. The `granite_docling` preset is the sole allowed VLM candidate for scanned/image-heavy PDF and image fixtures; its IBM revision and downloaded artifact SHA-256 are pinned in the model manifest, and it is promoted only when the conversion calibration shows higher exact text/table/reading-order/locator accuracy with no hard-gate regression. The winning per-format policy is checked in and immutable at runtime; a tie selects the standard pipeline. The community ONNX conversion remains an offline benchmark/export artifact until upstream Docling exposes a tested ONNX VLM engine. UI, external plugins, remote services, arbitrary custom VLM/code/formula/picture configurations, management endpoints, permissive CORS, and debug error detail stay disabled; API-key auth, an allowlist containing only the selected preset, JSON logs, `/livez`, `/readyz`, bounded file/page/time/queue limits, one local worker, and private scratch/model volumes are mandatory. All model/tokenizer artifacts are fetched during a checksum-verifying install step; production and tests run offline and fail readiness if a pinned artifact is absent. Aura supplies only bytes already authorized for the owning identity; Docling never receives Garage or tenant credentials. The contextual text embedded and indexed prepends bounded title, heading path, caption, and table header. Hybrid chunking splits oversized structural units and merges only compatible undersized peers using the pinned `google/embeddinggemma-300m` tokenizer revision. No fixed-character or blind overlap chunker survives.
>
> **Provenance contract.** Each Postgres chunk and Arcade passage carries `identity_id` implicitly by physical database and explicitly in Postgres, `document_id`, `search_document_id`, `version_id`, version number, original SHA-256, pipeline generation, ordinal, contextualized text, normalized-text SHA-256, Docling `self_ref`, heading path, captions, page number, bounding box and char span when present, plus sheet/table/row/column/cell locator when the converter exposes them. Missing locator fields are absent, never fabricated. `document_search` returns document-level score and bounded top passages with a canonical citation token `document:<search_document_id>@<version_number>#<locator>`, original SHA-256, retrieval leg evidence, and degradation status. `document_open` returns/materializes exactly that active version and reports its SHA-256/version. A factual answer may cite only tokens returned by search/open; passage text remains `TrustUntrusted`, so instructions inside a document are data, not authority.
>
> **Arcade projection and supported capacity.** The document `SEARCH_INDEX` uses Lucene `StandardAnalyzer`, not the English analyzer, because the blocking corpus is multilingual; analyzer identity is part of the schema version. `LSM_VECTOR` uses `NONE` quantization for the declared appliance envelope so the first release does not trade citation recall for compression. Each identity is limited by default to 10,000 passages in one candidate version and 100,000 active passages total; the worker checks the projected count before conversion/projection and fails the candidate version permanently without replacing the prior active version. The release gate indexes 100,000 reproducible passages in a 2 GiB ArcadeDB heap, requires steady-state heap below 75% after GC, the retrieval SLO, zero projection loss through restart, and the quality hard gates. A larger envelope or INT8/product quantization is a schema migration justified by a checked-in NONE-vs-quantized capacity/recall benchmark; it is never a runtime knob that can reinterpret an existing index.
>
> **Retrieval and API convergence.** The one host retriever accepts natural-language `query`, `limit`, and optional owner-valid `document_ids`; unknown fields are rejected before execution. It combines PostgreSQL weighted document routing (title/tags/digest/card) with ArcadeDB passage full-text and dense candidates, collapses by document while retaining top passages, validates active generation/openability in PostgreSQL, and uses deterministic tie-breaking by score then document ID then passage ordinal. The checked-in calibration evaluates dense-only, lexical-only, a confidence-gated cascade, native rank-based RRF (`k=60`), and normalized weighted fusion against the exact same corpus. Eligible profiles must satisfy recall@1 ≥99%, citation locator accuracy 100%, exact-answer accuracy 100%, the 100k capacity gate, and non-inferiority on both Italian and English subsets; the winner is chosen lexicographically by exact-answer accuracy, recall@1, MRR, p95 latency, then implementation complexity. Only that immutable winner exists in the production query path; losing branches remain test-harness code. Existing Aura evidence where equal-weight fusion reduced dense retrieval from 8/8 to 5/8 forbids assuming RRF is the winner. Query embedding failure degrades explicitly to lexical passage + card FTS; ArcadeDB failure degrades to card FTS and requires `document_open` before a factual answer; neither is reported as an empty corpus. Empty queries return a bounded recent-ready listing only when explicitly requested by the UI/list operation, never through a malformed model tool call. The agent tool, CLI search, and `/api/documents?q=` share this retriever; the title-only ILIKE API path is removed. No reranker ships unless the checked-in corpus proves a statistically significant exact-answer/recall gain while preserving every hard gate, after which it replaces rather than shadows the selected production profile.
>
> **Tenant boundary and queue correctness.** Every tenant-bearing table, including `document_ingest_jobs` during its retirement, `storage_objects`, `ingestion_jobs`, `ingestion_events`, and `delete_jobs`, gains a typed owner/FK and fail-closed RLS. JSON payloads and object keys are never authoritative identity. Cross-tenant workers enumerate identity IDs with a narrowly owned store method, then claim and mutate under `db.WithIdentityTx`; no application connection gets `BYPASSRLS`. Job uniqueness is `(identity_id, job_type, idempotency_key)`. Claim includes queued work and expired `running` leases, increments a fencing generation, and uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; heartbeats extend only the current generation and a stale worker cannot commit. Status transition plus event/outbox write is one transaction. Retryable errors use bounded exponential backoff with full jitter; policy/format/size/auth errors fail fast. Automatic retry first returns the asset/version to a processable non-visible state. Manual retry creates a new attempt generation for a terminal job with the same logical idempotency key, never a duplicate document/version.
>
> **Delete, privacy, and reconciliation.** Delete first locks the owner-scoped document, sets `deleting`, snapshots every raw/derived object and projection generation into an idempotent delete job, and immediately excludes the document from search/open. A worker tombstones/removes Arcade passages, removes the deterministic per-document sandbox directory, deletes every Garage object through the per-identity resolver, treats object-not-found as success, verifies absence with `HEAD`, and only then atomically marks ledger, asset, versions, document, job, and event deleted. A transient object/projection failure leaves the document `deleting` and retries; `dead_letter` is an operational/privacy alert, never success. Caller-selected open filenames are aliases inside the deterministic document directory and are therefore purged with it. Reconciliation scans live ledger↔object, active Postgres generation↔Arcade projection, expired job leases, dangling ready rows, and legacy pre-deleted assets. It reports unledgered objects before any repair and deletes only keys proven owned by the target identity/document.
>
> **Backfill and rollback.** The forward migration uses the next free numeric slot observed from `internal/db/migrations/` at landing; no number in this amendment reserves it. It adds nullable ownership/generation/source columns, backfills only through existing FK chains, quarantines ambiguous legacy jobs instead of assigning them to `local`, converts valid ready rows with an openable asset/version, marks irrecoverable ready-without-version rows `failed/original_unavailable`, creates cleanup jobs for assets already soft-deleted while their storage ledger remains live, then applies `NOT NULL`, unique constraints, FK and RLS together with identity-scoped stores. Existing `document_chunks`/`document_embeddings` become the active provenance/projection ledger; the legacy `document_ingest_jobs` is dropped only after zero unmapped rows and its operator history is preserved in `ingestion_events`. Before rollout, take a PostgreSQL snapshot and Garage inventory. The down migration can restore schema before any verified hard-delete; once an object reached `object_deleted`, rollback is forward-fix because deleted bytes cannot be recreated.
>
> **Observability and SLOs.** One trace links `ingress`, `object.put`, `job.enqueue`, `job.claim`, each pipeline stage, Docling submit/poll/result, embed batch, Arcade project/query, activate, search, open, retry, reconcile, and delete/HEAD verification using OpenTelemetry messaging producer/consumer links rather than pretending the queued worker is a child span. Metrics include queue depth/oldest age, lease reclaim/fence rejects, stage duration and cache hit/miss by stage/producer, retry/dead-letter/error class, Docling partial/failure, chunks and embedding batches, projection lag, retrieval mode/candidate counts/zero-result, active-generation rejects, search→open success, delete age/object verification, and owner-boundary denials. Labels never contain identity, filename, query, object key, or raw error text. Required service objectives on the checked-in corpus and local appliance are: p95 enqueue-to-ready ≤120 s for a 20-page text PDF and ≤300 s for the largest standard fixture, warm p95 search ≤750 ms, p95 open-first-byte ≤2 s for a 10 MiB original, zero lost terminal events, zero jobs stuck beyond two leases, and zero post-delete bytes/projections/search hits.
>
> **Hermetic corpus and blocking E2E.** `testdata/document-e2e/` contains real, generated reproducibly and committed fixtures plus a manifest with SHA-256, facts, locators, expected reingest policy, and prompt-injection markers: multi-sheet/formula/Unicode XLSX, CSV, DOCX with early and late facts, PDF over 20 pages, PPTX, scanned PDF, corrupted PDF/OOXML, Unicode/path-shaped filenames, and byte-identical duplicates. `make document-e2e` provisions disposable Postgres state, tenant Garage prefixes/buckets, per-identity ArcadeDB databases, Docling, embedder, and sandbox; runs migrations; ingests through Web, Telegram adapter, CLI, and `document_index`; searches, opens, answers with provenance, updates, retries, reclaims leases, reconciles, deletes, and cleans up; injects crashes after object PUT, claim, conversion result, projection, activation, and object delete; writes one JSON/JUnit report; and forbids skips under CI. Two identities concurrently ingest the same name/bytes and adversarial foreign IDs to prove zero catalog/object/passage/sandbox/answer leakage and `42501` without identity.
>
> The deterministic 100-point score is 40 lifecycle/integrity, 25 retrieval, 20 answer/provenance, 10 isolation/delete, and 5 resilience/latency. Closure requires at least 99/100 (**>9.8/10**) and all hard gates: no cross-tenant observation, dangling search hit, wrong SHA/version, invented locator, post-delete answer/object, skipped fixture, stuck lease, or missing event. Retrieval on the manifest requires recall@1 ≥99%, citation locator accuracy 100%, and exact-answer accuracy 100% for deterministic structured facts. The PR gate runs real Postgres + Garage + ArcadeDB + Docling + embedder + sandbox without a paid model; nightly/release additionally drives the real configured model at deterministic settings through Web and Telegram and cannot turn a deterministic failure green. Full `db_integration`, `garage_integration`, `arcadedb_integration`, document E2E, unit/property/fuzz/goleak and race tiers execute; changed owned-surface coverage is ≥85% over the full tag matrix and mutation kill is ≥70% on lifecycle/retrieval/delete critical files.
>
> **Implementation boundaries and atomic landing.** Files touched or added are limited to `internal/db/migrations/00NN_document_pipeline_convergence.{up,down}.sql`, `internal/db/queries/{assets,document_control_plane,document_digest,document_ingest_jobs}.sql` plus pinned sqlc output; `internal/embeddings/*.go`; `internal/documents/{pipeline_types,pipeline_store,pipeline_worker,docling_client,passage_store,retrieval,retrieval_profile,delete,open,service}.go`; `internal/assets/{service,types,document_processor}.go`; `internal/arcadedb/{tenant_clients,document_schema,document_projection,document_retrieval}.go`; `cmd/arcadedb-mcp/tenant.go`; `internal/config/` document/embed knobs; the existing `cmd/aura` asset queue/worker/indexer/version-recorder/catalog wiring split into concern files under 600 LOC; `internal/agent/tools/{document_index,document_search,document_open}.go`; `internal/assets/context.go`; `internal/agui/documents_api.go`; `compose.yaml`, deployment overlays, `.env.example`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `testdata/document-e2e/`, `testdata/document-retrieval-profile/`, `docs/audit/README.md`, and `docs/aura-quality-snapshot.md`. No edited/new implementation file may exceed 600 lines, and dark legacy code/tables/parameters/comments are removed on touch. Atomic order is: (114-0) this PRD-only commit; (114-1) schema/RLS/fenced jobs/backfill; (114-2) canonical ingress, activation, retry and durable delete; (114-3) one embedder, shared tenant resolver, pinned Docling client/compose and stage cache; (114-4) Arcade projection/calibrated retrieval/provenance/capacity; (114-5) tool/API/CLI/prompt convergence; (114-6) hermetic E2E/fault injection/CI/audit/quality evidence. Every Go sub-slice independently runs repository vet/build, focused unit and race tests before the next starts. No open question remains; Gate 1 Definition of Ready is **DoR ✅ 2026-08-04**.
>
> **▶ Amendment #115 (2026-08-04 — isolated real-production document E2E).** The operator requires the final document gate to drive the real Aura agent and production surface, while forbidding any use of personal identities, conversations, documents, credentials-as-data, or pre-existing tenant state. Amendment #114's implementation boundary therefore additionally authorizes `scripts/document_pipeline_e2e.sh`, dedicated non-secret probes under `scripts/document_pipeline_e2e_*.go`, and synthetic fixtures under `scripts/fixtures/document_pipeline_e2e/`. The gate creates two disposable E2E identities and a unique canary corpus, records their identifiers before every query, and fails closed unless the configured production LLM, Docling, embedding server, Garage, PostgreSQL, and per-identity ArcadeDB projection all execute without mock, skip, fallback, or degraded status. Hard checks cover canonical ingest through ready activation, exact ground-truth answer and citation locator/version/SHA through a natural agent prompt, cross-tenant non-disclosure, retry/restart recovery, delete plus Garage absence, post-delete non-recall, and cleanup of both identities. Cleanup is mandatory but cannot erase failure evidence; the report contains only synthetic identifiers, hashes, timings, stage/event states, and redacted error classes. A score above 98% means every hard check passes. The production gate is operator-run after WSL/unit/integration/migration gates and is never substituted by the hermetic CI corpus.

> **▶ Amendment #116 (2026-08-04 — operator-authorized production corpus).** For the production-only gate in #115, the operator explicitly designates `D:\tmp\aura-document-pipeline-references\document_ingestion\baseline-corpus` (WSL: `/mnt/d/tmp/aura-document-pipeline-references/document_ingestion/baseline-corpus`) as the sole authorized source corpus. This later instruction supersedes #115's synthetic-document restriction only for those seven reviewed files; disposable identities, conversations, tenant databases, buckets, prefixes, and sandbox state remain mandatory, and the runner may not enumerate or read any sibling directory. The corpus is copied into a mode-0700 ephemeral staging directory, never modified, and logs/reports may contain only basename, byte size, SHA-256, timings, generated identifiers, lifecycle states, and redacted error classes—not extracted rows or document text. `Clienti.xlsx` retains the repository-recorded deterministic acceptance fact of 699 rows whose locality is TORINO; the real agent must derive that result through Aura document tools and return active version, raw SHA-256, and canonical locator. Cleanup deletes only resources created for the run and never deletes or alters the authorized source corpus.
>
> **▶ Amendment #117 (2026-08-05 — passage erasure is physical, not a tombstone).** Amendment #114 §"Delete, privacy, and reconciliation" requires the delete worker to "atomically mark ledger, asset, versions, document, job, and event deleted", and §"Backfill and rollback" designates `document_chunks`/`document_embeddings` as "the active provenance/projection ledger". Read together those two lines put the passage tables inside the delete contract, but "mark deleted" left their treatment ambiguous, and the implementation resolved the ambiguity by omission: `FinalizeDocumentDelete` never referenced either table, so extracted document text and its embedding vectors survived a nominally successful durable delete. The operator resolves the ambiguity in favour of erasure. For these two tables specifically, "marked deleted" means **physically deleted rows**, not a `deleted_at` tombstone: the chunk `text` column is the document body itself, and a retained tombstone is retained PII, which contradicts §"Observability and SLOs" ("zero post-delete bytes/projections/search hits"). Finalization is additionally gated on **zero live passage rows** for the document, fail-closed in the same shape the query already applies to `storage_objects` — a delete that cannot prove erasure must not report success, and leaves the document `deleting` for retry, never `dead_letter`-as-success. Operator/provenance history is unaffected: it lives in `ingestion_events`, which §"Backfill and rollback" already designates as the preserved operator history. No migration is required — the tables and their FK cascade already exist — and no new env knob is introduced. Machine-checkable acceptance: a real PostgreSQL integration assertion that after finalize **zero** live `document_chunks` and **zero** live `document_embeddings` rows remain for the deleted document, and that finalize **refuses** while any live passage row remains.
>
> **▶ Amendment #118 (2026-08-06 — Aura orchestrates the ingestion, it does not implement it: CocoIndex reconciles, Tika extracts, ArcadeDB retrieves).** Amendment #114 built an industrial document plane by hand, and #115/#116 gated it in production. The contract it delivers — provenance-bearing passages, durable erasure, cross-tenant non-disclosure — is **kept in full and is not reopened by this amendment**. What is superseded is the *implementation*, on measured grounds: Aura reimplemented, in Go and SQL, machinery that three specialised engines already provide, and reimplemented it worse.
>
> **The measurement that forces this.** Migration `0093_document_pipeline_convergence` (2026-08-05) introduced `document_pipeline_stages` with `input_fingerprint`, `producer_version`, `attempt_count`, `lease_generation`, `next_attempt_at`. Those are, one for one, CocoIndex's memoization keys, hand-written in 610 lines of SQL the day before a spike proved the library does it natively. Around that ledger sit **9.023 lines** of stage machine, lease reclaim, retry backoff, orphan sweep, durable-delete workers and a version/tombstone scheme that no query ever reads back (`document_retrieval.go:186` filters `active = true` everywhere), plus **1.085** further lines of integration tests never counted. The spike replaces all of it with ~400 lines, and the replacement is not a rewrite of the same idea: reconciliation makes the declared state the current state, so "what is no longer declared is deleted" is a property rather than a worker.
>
> **Three engines, three boundaries, and what stays Aura's.** `iscc-tika` **0.6.0** extracts (Apache-2.0, maintained; `extractous` is the same engine but unpushed since 2024-12-21). CocoIndex reconciles. ArcadeDB retrieves. Aura keeps exactly what no engine can know: identity and tenancy, the agent loop and tool contracts, the security boundary, and how a file reaches the sandbox. The delegation is deliberately partial and the boundary is evidence-based in **both** directions — `coco.__all__` exposes no query/search/rank symbol, so retrieval is not CocoIndex's job; and ArcadeDB exposes no text-to-vector function, so embedding is not the store's job and remains ours.
>
> **Docling is withdrawn, and with it #114's pinning of `quay.io/docling-project/docling-serve-cpu:v1.29.0`.** Measured on a real corpus (an operator BIFF `.xls`, a 47-page justified Constitution PDF, ISTAT's 1,2 MB `.xlsx`, plus a LibreOffice fan-out across csv/doc/docx/html/odp/ods/odt/pdf/ppt/pptx/rtf/xls/xlsx): Tika-native handles **15 formats of 16 with zero failures** at 0,26 s against 6,63 s on the same PDF (18×) and 1,44 s against 14,70 s on the spreadsheet (10×). MarkItDown, the previously promised replacement, is withdrawn in the same breath and for a harder reason than speed: it fails outright on `.doc`/`.ppt`/`.odt`/`.ods`/`.odp`, returns raw RTF markup as if it were text, and on justified PDFs emits 49,8 double spaces per 1k characters — which silently breaks the lexical leg of hybrid retrieval while producing *more* characters than a clean extractor (96.063 against 92.891), and is not configurable on that code path. **Legacy formats enter through LibreOffice**, already shipped in `docker/aura/Dockerfile`, which closes a live gap: `filecard/build.go:105` routes only `.xlsx`/`.xlsm`, so an ordinary 2010 `.xls` has no door into Aura today.
>
> **The reranker sidecar is withdrawn.** This one required two measurements, and the first was deliberately refused as insufficient: on OTT-QA (8.891 tables, n=200) reranking added a single point over dense top-1 (0,84 → 0,85), but that benchmark's cards are clean English written by the benchmark itself. The decisive measurement is dense-only routing over the production-shaped Italian corpus with the same 13 labelled questions and the same cards: **8/10 documents and 9/10 mechanism, identical to the reranker**. Dense additionally separates answerable from unanswerable on cards (worst answerable 0,2446 against best unanswerable 0,2334) where the reranker returned noise (0,0003 against 0,0006) — recorded as an indication, not a threshold, because it rests on three negatives with a 0,011 margin. `AURA_RERANK_*` and the `aura-rerank` service are removed; the GPU is returned to the embedder.
>
> **Abstention is re-specified as two questions, because they have different answers.** "Is anything in the corpus about this?" is decidable from retrieval (**0,90** on SQuAD-it). "Is the answer inside this passage?" is **not** (**0,65** on SQuAD 2.0; medians 0,9993 against 0,9974 — no threshold exists, because a cross-encoder scores relevance and an impossible SQuAD 2.0 question is maximally relevant to its paragraph). The second question therefore belongs to the model that reads the passage, as a prompt contract, and #114's retrieval-side abstention is narrowed to the first. This is also why removing the reranker leaves no hole.
>
> **The chunker's ceiling is 2048 TOKENS, not a byte budget.** EmbeddingGemma-300M's GGUF declares `context_length = 2048` and Google documents the same; a longer input is refused with HTTP 500. `AURA_DOCUMENT_CHUNK_MAX_TOKENS` keeps its 4096 validation ceiling only for a future wider model and must not exceed the served model's declared context. Relatedly, `AURA_EMBED_POOLING` is **deleted rather than validated**: the model file declares its pooling and llama.cpp obeys it when the flag is absent (verified: bit-identical vectors, max abs diff 0,0), so the knob could only ever be right by agreeing with the file — and when it disagreed it cost recall@1 0,90 → 0,70 in silence.
>
> **Amendment #115's production gate is retained in full and re-pointed.** Its component list replaces Docling with the extractor sidecar and drops the reranker; every other hard check — canonical ingest through ready activation, exact ground-truth answer with citation locator/version/SHA through a natural agent prompt, cross-tenant non-disclosure, retry/restart recovery, delete plus Garage absence, post-delete non-recall, cleanup of both disposable identities — stands unchanged, still fail-closed on any mock, skip, fallback or degraded status. **A green unit suite is explicitly not a substitute**: this amendment closes only when that gate runs against the production surface with the real agent and scores above 98%.
>
> **Machine-checkable acceptance.** (1) `document_search` returns a passage identity that `document_open` resolves — the F0 blocker, today broken because `Passage.document` carries the ingest walker's path. (2) A `.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt`, `.odt`, `.ods`, `.odp`, `.rtf`, `.pdf`, `.docx`, `.xlsx` and `.pptx` each ingest, and a known phrase survives **verbatim** through exact-phrase search on the justified PDF. (3) A legacy `.xls` reaches `filecard` with its header row correctly detected below a banner and numeric cells still numeric. (4) Add, modify and delete against the live source reconcile without restarting the sidecar. (5) `grep -ri docling` and `grep -ri AURA_RERANK` return nothing outside historical PRD amendments and `docs/`. (6) The #115 production gate scores above 98%. (7) Coverage stays at or above the 85% floor across the tag matrix after ~10k lines are removed.

> **▶ Amendment #141 (2026-08-25 — #115 follows the reconciler; #116 is withdrawn).** This amendment records a live measurement made before changing the gate. The exact #116 path, `/mnt/d/tmp/aura-document-pipeline-references/document_ingestion/baseline-corpus`, no longer contains the seven reviewed documents: its immediate files are the Aura repository root, including `.env`, binaries and source. The gate refused to read or stage that material, so #116's authorization and its `Clienti.xlsx` fact are withdrawn. The checked-in, synthetic `scripts/fixtures/document_pipeline_e2e/` corpus authorized by #115 is again the sole input: it is non-secret, reproducible and contains its own ground truth. The current `scripts/ingest_reconcile_e2e.sh` then failed on its first live pass before extraction because it still minted a non-UUID identity and queried a configurable `ARCADE_DB`; production now rejects malformed identities and derives the only readable database as `mem_<identity_uuid>`. Its cleanup also removed the failing container log before printing it. This measurement proves the named gate is stale; it does **not** yet prove ingest, retrieval, agent answer, isolation, restart, delete or cleanup green.
>
> The replacement keeps CocoIndex's smaller production model instead of recreating #114's retired control plane. For each of two disposable UUID identities the gate provisions one scoped Garage bucket/key, one derived per-identity ArcadeDB database/user and one persistent CocoIndex state volume. Canonical ingest is `object PUT → CocoIndex reconciliation → one IndexedDocument plus its Passage rows`; there is no PostgreSQL document activation, document version row, stage DAG, lease, retry worker, projection generation or tombstone to simulate. A byte modification is the new current object and raw SHA-256; deletion is physical removal of the object, IndexedDocument and Passage rows by reconciliation. Restart recovery means stopping and restarting the real sidecar with the same bucket and state volume, then proving reconciliation resumes without duplicate or stale rows. The gate retains PostgreSQL only for the disposable real-agent conversation and identity records and still runs the shipped migration head/round-trip guard.
>
> The production assertions are fail-closed: every fixture is audited as indexed; `document_search` returns `status=complete`, the expected canary, full raw SHA-256 and a canonical citation token anchored by SHA plus the only locators the writer produces (`char_start`/`char_end`, with ordinal as the fallback); `document_open` returns the exact original bytes; the configured OpenRouter model answers a natural prompt with the exact canary and returned citation/SHA; identity B cannot retrieve, scope, open or read identity A's object; an unchanged pass performs zero extractions; add and modify reconcile; a sidecar restart resumes; delete removes the Garage object and both ArcadeDB record classes; a fresh real-agent turn after delete cannot recall the canary; and both identities, conversations, buckets, keys, databases, containers and volumes are removed. Any mock, skip, fallback, degraded retrieval, missing cleanup postcondition or surviving resource scores zero. Ten hard assertions pass = **10.0/10 (>9.8)**. `scripts/ingest_reconcile_e2e.sh` remains the single orchestrator and is rewritten around these current contracts; a tagged live test may reuse the existing real-Runner/OpenRouter and two-identity provisioning harnesses, but no `document_pipeline_e2e*` runner/probe or other retired implementation is restored.
>
> This amendment also removes the dark schema exposed by the measurement. The current writer always supplies only `heading_path`, `char_start` and `char_end`; `projection_key`, `version_id`, `version_number`, `self_ref`, `captions`, page/bounding-box, sheet/table/row/column/cell and `tombstoned_at` are always null and therefore leave the Python dataclass, Go candidate/wire structs, DDL/select/decode paths and tests together. `pipeline_generation` remains only if a current reader uses it; otherwise it is removed by the same caller inventory. Historical prose may describe the retired pipeline, but executable code, schemas, tests, env catalog entries and current operational documentation may not advertise or guard it as a live surface.

> **Machine-checkable acceptance.** Pure tests pin label compaction, the Studio diameter formula/cap, type-derived colours, centred/wrapped node text, outlined edge text, arrowheads, and projection of parallel relationships. Renderer tests prove fCoSE is the sole layout, every non-empty node/edge caption reaches Cytoscape's native label layer, dense overviews retain captions, and pinned paths dim rather than delete off-path content. The authenticated desktop and mobile Playwright run must be rebuilt from `master`, show distinct non-overlapping nodes with visible names and relationship captions in captured canvases, keep the canvas nonblank, and report no browser or serious/critical accessibility errors.

> **Pattern rubato** dai 4 sistemi memory production-grade 2026 (mix-and-match): **mem0** (48k stars, 91% latency / 90% token saving): 2-fase pipeline extract+conflict, hybrid retrieval. **Letta MemGPT**: 3-tier storage Core/Recall/Archival. **Microsoft GraphRAG**: entity+relationship extraction LLM + Leiden community clustering hierarchical. **Cognee**: Cognify pipeline 6-stage + Memify post-processing (prune/strengthen/derive). Sources: [mem0 state 2026](https://mem0.ai/blog/state-of-ai-agent-memory-2026), [Letta docs](https://docs.letta.com/concepts/letta/), [GraphRAG guide 2026](https://blog.premai.io/graphrag-implementation-guide-entity-extraction-query-routing-when-it-beats-vector-rag-2026/), [Cognee architecture](https://www.cognee.ai/blog/fundamentals/how-cognee-builds-ai-memory).

> **Atomicity: 4 sub-slice archival MVP (11a/11b/11d/11e) ~1850 LOC**, ognuno atomic + smoke green. **11c — Community detection è DEFERITA fuori dall'MVP Phase 15 (amendment #27)** — feature lazy/on-demand futura, non parte della sequenza atomica: GDS resta installato (Slice 0.7) per algoritmi ad-hoc (PageRank/WCC/Node-Similarity), ma il job schedulato Leiden + le community-summary LLM sono rimandati (vedi §11c sotto). **+ 11f Task Canvas (~400 LOC, amendment #25) è sequencing-indipendente** — non parte della sequenza atomica di Phase 15: può atterrare a ~Phase 9-10 (dipende solo da context management / Phase 6, non da ingestion/retrieval).

**Goal.** Aura **conosce** (ingest + index) e **ricorda** (retrieve) — sia il world dell'utente (documenti, entità, conversazioni passate) sia il proprio (agent journal, insight cross-conv). Pipeline MVP: file/URL/conversation → markitdown (Slice 9c) → chunker → embedder (Slice 0.7 sidecar) → Neo4j HNSW + entity LLM extraction → retrieval hybrid + LLM re-ranker. (Leiden community detection + summarization è la sub-slice 11c, DEFERITA fuori dall'MVP — amendment #27.)

### Pre-requisiti

- Slice 0.7 Neo4j infra + HNSW + `aura-llama-embed` sidecar
- Slice 0.9 Agent runtime abstraction (per background goroutine come `BackgroundAgent`)
- Slice 1.7 identity (scope, oggi single-user `local`)
- Slice 1.8 conversation persistence (rollup `:UserConversation`)
- Slice 5 web tools (per `ingest.url` riusa `web_fetch`)
- Slice 7e snippet (mirror in Neo4j `:UserSnippet` per semantic search)
- Slice 9c markitdown sidecar (document → markdown universal parser)
- Slice 10 Agent.md (Core tier già implementato)

### Decisioni cumulate (chiusura 2026-05-28)

| Aspetto | Decisione |
|---|---|
| Memory taxonomy cognitiva | **3 tipi**: Episodic (past events temporal) + Semantic (entities/relations) + Procedural (behaviors/scripts). Industry consensus 2026. |
| Storage tier (Letta-style) | **3 tier**: Core (in-context, Agent.md + top-K AgentInsight, ~2K token) + Recall (Postgres `conversation_turns` searchable) + Archival (Neo4j full graph, retrieved via tool). |
| Entity extraction | **Auto-extract sempre on** durante ingestion. LLM tier=reasoning batch ogni 10 chunk. Type taxonomy **POLE+O (amendment #29)**: `type` chiuso Person/Org/Location/Concept/Event/Topic/**Other** + proprietà `subtype` free-form. Cost ~$0.05/documento medio. |
| Retrieval | **Hybrid BM25 + HNSW + graph 1-hop expansion, fuse via Weighted-RRF Cypher-native (amendment #26, rank-based scale-free), poi LLM re-ranker tier=worker**. Re-rank top-20 → top-5. Max quality, +LLM cost ~$0.001/query. (Fusione lineare pesata = fallback deprecato.) |
| Privacy isolation | **No isolation single-user mode**: tutti node sotto identity `'local'` default. Future multi-user richiede refactor (accettato pre-merge). |
| Community detection | **DEFERITA fuori MVP (amendment #27, 11c)** — il job schedulato Leiden + community-summary LLM è over-engineering per il target single-user/self-hosted/cost-sensitive (le summary tematiche globali rispondono a una domanda di corpus-analytics che il single-user raramente pone; ogni community richiede una summary LLM rigenerata al drift del grafo; Microsoft stessa è passata a LazyGraphRAG). Diventa una feature lazy/on-demand futura. **GDS resta installato** (Slice 0.7) per PageRank/WCC/Node-Similarity ad-hoc; solo lo `gds.leiden.stream` schedulato + summary sono rimandati. Il valore cognitivo (local retrieval) è pienamente coperto da 11d (hybrid WRRF + graph 1-2 hop) senza community. |
| Memify post-processing | **Cognee pattern**: soft-archive stale entity (no mention 180gg → `archived_at`, NO hard delete — amendment #29) + strengthen RELATED_TO weight su co-occurrence + derive facts da multi-hop traversal. Background 24h. |
| Agent memory | **Episodic + Insight + cached injection (amendment #11)**: `:AgentEpisode` post-conv summary + `:AgentInsight` cross-conv pattern. Pre-conv inject top-K Insight relevant nel system prompt come `messages[2]`. **In-memory LRU cache TTL `AURA_AGENT_INSIGHT_CACHE_TTL_SEC=600` (10 min)** — preserva byte-identity di `messages[2]` turn-su-turn (Slice 4 invariant cross-slice). Senza cache: Slice 4 KV cache si rompe quando Slice 11e atterra (Pitfall #3, Risk #5). |

### Architettura (4 sub-slice archival MVP 11a/11b/11d/11e + 11c DEFERITA amendment #27 + 11f Task Canvas sequencing-indipendente)

> **[SUPERSEDED #61]** Il build bespoke 11a/11b/11d/11e qui sotto è rimpiazzato dal server MCP `agent-memory` (vedi Amendment #61 in testa a §Slice 11). Resta come storico di design / riferimento sui pattern (content-hash dedup, valid-time, POLE+O, NOOP) che hanno informato la scelta. Solo 11f Task Canvas resta target d'implementazione.

**11a — Schema Neo4j + taxonomy doc (~200 LOC, niente impl)**:
```cypher
// === USER MEMORY (single-user 'local' scope) ===
CREATE CONSTRAINT document_id FOR (d:Document) REQUIRE d.id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT chunk_id    FOR (c:Chunk)    REQUIRE c.id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT entity_id   FOR (e:Entity)   REQUIRE e.id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT community_id FOR (cm:Community) REQUIRE cm.id IS UNIQUE;

// amendment #24: vector.dimensions HARDCODED a 768 (NON `${AURA_EMBED_DIMENSIONS}`):
// il runner migrate.go calcola il checksum sui byte grezzi del file PRIMA di ogni
// sostituzione → templating per-env romperebbe l'invariante checksum (vedi nota #24
// + ritiro acceptance #18 sotto). Contratto dimensione garantito a runtime da pingEmbed.
CREATE VECTOR INDEX chunk_embedding FOR (c:Chunk) ON (c.embedding)
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 768, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine', `vector.hnsw.m`: 32, `vector.hnsw.ef_construction`: 200}}; -- amendment #20: HNSW M=32 (NOT default 16) per recall@5 ≥ 0.8 @ 100K corpus
CREATE VECTOR INDEX entity_embedding FOR (e:Entity) ON (e.embedding)
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 768, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine', `vector.hnsw.m`: 32, `vector.hnsw.ef_construction`: 200}}; -- amendment #20: HNSW M=32 (NOT default 16) per recall@5 ≥ 0.8 @ 100K corpus
CREATE VECTOR INDEX community_embedding FOR (cm:Community) ON (cm.embedding)
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 768, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine', `vector.hnsw.m`: 32, `vector.hnsw.ef_construction`: 200}}; -- amendment #20: HNSW M=32 (NOT default 16) per recall@5 ≥ 0.8 @ 100K corpus
CREATE VECTOR INDEX agent_insight_embedding FOR (i:AgentInsight) ON (i.embedding)
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 768, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine', `vector.hnsw.m`: 32, `vector.hnsw.ef_construction`: 200}}; -- amendment #20: HNSW M=32 (NOT default 16) per recall@5 ≥ 0.8 @ 100K corpus
CREATE VECTOR INDEX reasoning_trace_embedding FOR (rt:ReasoningTrace) ON (rt.embedding)
  OPTIONS {indexConfig: {`vector.dimensions`: 768, `vector.similarity_function`: 'cosine', `vector.hnsw.m`: 32, `vector.hnsw.ef_construction`: 200}}; -- amendment #24: 5° index (reasoning traces, gated AURA_MEMORY_REASONING_TRACE_ENABLED)

CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX chunk_text FOR (c:Chunk) ON EACH [c.text];
CREATE FULLTEXT INDEX entity_name FOR (e:Entity) ON EACH [e.name];

CREATE INDEX entity_type   FOR (e:Entity)        ON (e.type);
CREATE INDEX entity_mentions FOR (e:Entity)      ON (e.mention_count);
CREATE INDEX episode_agent FOR (ep:AgentEpisode) ON (ep.agent_kind);
CREATE INDEX insight_agent FOR (i:AgentInsight)  ON (i.agent_kind);
// amendment #29: `identity_id` (OQ6) e `archived_at` (OQ4) sono scritti su :Entity ma
// NON indicizzati in MVP — in single-user lo scope è costante e l'archived-filter è
// query-time. L'index su `identity_id` è lo step additivo che atterra col landing
// multi-user (vedi OQ6); l'index su `archived_at` solo se il filtro diventa hot.

// Labels + properties:
// NB (amendment #29, OQ6): ogni nodo porta anche `identity_id` (costante 'local' in MVP single-user)
//     e ogni Cypher di lettura è scopato `WHERE n.identity_id = $identity_id` (refactor multi-user additivo).
// :Document   {id, source_uri, title, ingested_at, chunk_count, status, content_hash, identity_id}
// :Chunk      {id, document_id, sequence, text, embedding[768], tokens_count, identity_id}
// :Entity     {id, name, type, subtype, embedding[768], mention_count, first_seen_at, last_mentioned_at, archived_at, identity_id}
//             type ∈ {Person, Organization, Location, Concept, Event, Topic, Other}  // amendment #29 POLE+O: +Other catch-all
//             subtype = string free-form LLM-extracted (es. "Author","Family"); archived_at = soft-archive Memify (amendment #29 OQ4)
// :Community  {id, level (0=leaf, N=root), summary, embedding[768], member_count}  // amendment #27: schema provisioned, popolato solo quando 11c atterra (DEFERITA fuori MVP)
// :UserConversation {id, started_at, topic_summary, embedding[768], turn_count}
// :AgentEpisode  {id, agent_kind, started_at, ended_at, goal, outcome, summary}
//                agent_kind ∈ {chat, reasoning, worker}
// :AgentInsight  {id, agent_kind, pattern, confidence, observation_count, embedding[768], created_at}
// :ReasoningTrace {id, episode_id, step, decision, rationale, embedding[768], created_at}  // amendment #24, gated AURA_MEMORY_REASONING_TRACE_ENABLED

// Relations:
// (:Document)-[:HAS_CHUNK {seq}]->(:Chunk)
// (:Chunk)-[:MENTIONS {confidence}]->(:Entity)
// (:Entity)-[:RELATED_TO {weight, type}]->(:Entity)
// (:Entity)-[:IN_COMMUNITY]->(:Community)        // amendment #27: schema provisioned, popolato solo quando 11c atterra (DEFERITA fuori MVP)
// (:Community)-[:CONTAINS]->(:Community)   // hierarchical — amendment #27: idem, popolato solo da 11c (DEFERITA)
// (:UserConversation)-[:DISCUSSED]->(:Entity)
// (:UserConversation)-[:CITES]->(:Chunk)
// (:UserConversation)-[:USED_SNIPPET]->(:UserSnippet)   // Slice 7e mirror
// (:AgentEpisode)-[:LEARNED {strength}]->(:AgentInsight)
// (:AgentEpisode)-[:HANDLED]->(:UserConversation)
// (:AgentEpisode)-[:REASONED {seq}]->(:ReasoningTrace)   // amendment #24, gated
```

> **11a amendment #24 (2026-05-31) — Temporal validity model + NOOP + reasoning traces.**
> Convergenza dello studio comparativo 2026 (mem0 `ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/`**`NOOP`** + Zep/Graphiti valid-time + neo4j-agent-memory POLE+O reasoning nodes). Tre delta di **solo schema** in 11a (nessuna impl in 11a; plasmano il comportamento di 11b/11d/11e). Tutto sotto identity `'local'` (single-user) come il resto di Slice 11.
>
> **(1) Valid-time sulle fact-edge (Zep/Graphiti, semplificato — mono-temporale).** `:RELATED_TO` porta `valid_from` (timestamp, default = ingest time), `valid_to` (timestamp, `null` = vero adesso) e `confidence` (float 0-1). La conflict resolution è *invalidazione, non cancellazione*: un fatto contraddittorio imposta `valid_to = datetime()` sull'edge precedente e CREATE quello nuovo (la storia resta interrogabile). **Chi decide il conflitto:** 11a è solo-schema (fornisce le colonne); la *detection* di contraddizione fattuale (chiave = stesso `(startNode, type)` con `endNode` incompatibile — es. `(User)-[:LIVES_IN]->(città)` che cambia città — `:RELATED_TO` non ha proprietà `predicate`, il predicato È il `type` della relazione; distinta dal dedup di entità per fuzzy name+type) è responsabilità del **reconciler LLM di 11b** che emette `ADD | UPDATE(+invalidazione) | DELETE | NOOP` — non un constraint a write-time del grafo. Il retrieval (11d) DEVE preferire le edge con `valid_to IS NULL` e PUÒ esporre quelle superate solo su query esplicitamente storica (**11d acceptance da aggiornare di conseguenza** — vedi sotto). Schema aggiornato:
>   `// (:Entity)-[:RELATED_TO {weight, type, valid_from, valid_to, confidence}]->(:Entity)`
>   Il bi-temporale pieno (secondo asse `t_created`/`t_expired` di ingestion) è **rimandato** (Open question 7): un solo asse valid-time copre il failure mode dominante "il fatto è cambiato nel tempo" alla scala single-user.
>
> **(2) NOOP come esito di estrazione di prim'ordine (mem0).** Il reconciler entity/fact di 11b emette per ogni candidato uno di `ADD | UPDATE | DELETE | NOOP`. `NOOP` ("già noto, nulla cambia") è il guard anti-bloat e il caso comune sul re-ingest: non scrive nulla ed è loggato in `ingest_audit.action`. Questo **supera** la formulazione nuda "MERGE existing OR CREATE new" di 11b §entity_extractor: MERGE-senza-cambi == `NOOP`, MERGE-con-valore-cambiato == `UPDATE` (+ invalidazione valid-time del punto (1)).
>
> **(3) Reasoning traces come nodi di prim'ordine (neo4j-agent-memory POLE+O).** Nuova label `:ReasoningTrace {id, episode_id, step, decision, rationale, embedding[768], created_at}` + relazione `(:AgentEpisode)-[:REASONED {seq}]->(:ReasoningTrace)`. Predispone il journal (11e) a imparare dalle *proprie* decisioni passate, non solo dagli outcome. Vector index `reasoning_trace_embedding` (768d cosine, HNSW M=32, ef_construction 200) accanto ai quattro index di 11a. **Schema provisioned, NESSUN consumer in MVP**: con `AURA_MEMORY_REASONING_TRACE_ENABLED=false` (default) nulla scrive `:ReasoningTrace`, e l'insight clustering di 11e legge `:AgentEpisode` (outcome), non `:ReasoningTrace`. Lo schema atterra ORA solo per evitare una seconda migration; il read-path concreto in 11e è un *enhancement futuro*, non wiring MVP.
>
> **Nota path migration (auto-riconciliazione PRD).** La convenzione *implementata* è `internal/knowledge/migrations/000N_*.cypher` (vedi `internal/knowledge/migrate.go`, audit in `aura.knowledge_migrations`), **non** il path obsoleto `internal/db/migrations/neo4j/0002_memory_schema.cql` citato nell'acceptance 11a sotto. Lo schema temporale/reasoning atterra come `internal/knowledge/migrations/0002_memory_schema.cypher`. **Le migration Cypher sono forward-only** (il runner non ha sezione down; il marker `// -- migrate:up` è solo un commento, e un checksum-drift su versione applicata è errore fatto-corruzione): la riga di acceptance 11a "Migration Cypher … reversibile" va letta come *teardown via* `aura memory wipe-vectors --confirm` + re-apply, non come down-migration. Correzione propagata nell'acceptance 11a sotto e nel commit template 11a.
>
> **Conflitto risolto — dimensioni hardcoded vs templating (#18).** Il runner `migrate.go:loadMigrations` calcola il checksum sui **byte grezzi del file** *prima* di qualunque sostituzione; una sostituzione `${AURA_EMBED_DIMENSIONS}` per-env renderebbe il checksum env-dipendente (falso "history corruption" su host diverso) o desincronizzerebbe body-auditato vs body-applicato. Quindi: **il DDL di `0002_memory_schema.cypher` hardcoda `768`** (come già fa `0001_init.cypher`), e la riga di acceptance #18 sul templating `${...}` è da **ritirare** per le migration Cypher (il guard di dimensione resta `pingEmbed` al boot, `internal/knowledge/ping.go`). Non si possono avere insieme templating + checksum-su-byte-grezzi.
>
> **Limite splitter (D-08).** `splitCypherStatements` splitta su `;` naïve: `0002_memory_schema.cypher` NON deve contenere `;` dentro literal stringa (le `OPTIONS {...}` con `'cosine'`/`'standard'` sono safe; un futuro `CALL apoc`/`SET` con `;` in una stringa richiederebbe prima l'upgrade dello splitter).
